keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Arranging Nodes Snapping
text:
Snapping aligns the position and size of nodes to the background grid.
This feature allows nodes to snap to a grid, ensuring that node layouts remain clean and visually aligned.
Snapping can be toggling the snap icon (:bl-icon:`snap_off`/:bl-icon:`snap_on`) in the editor's headers
or toggled temporarily while transforming nodes by holding Ctrl.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/arranging.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Arranging Nodes > Auto-Offset
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Arranging Nodes Auto-Offset
text:
When you drop a node with at least one input and one output socket onto an existing connection between two nodes,
*Auto-offset* will, depending on the direction setting, automatically move the left or right node away to make room
for the new node.
*Auto-offset* is a feature that helps organizing node layouts interactively without interrupting the user workflow.

Auto-offset is enabled by default,
but it can be disabled in the Preferences.

You can toggle the offset direction while you are moving the node by pressing T.

The offset margin can be changed using the *Auto-offset Margin*
setting in the Editing section of the Preferences.

Admonition: Example Video
   :class: seealso

   `Auto-Offset. A workflow enhancement for Blender's node editors <https://vimeo.com/135125839>`__.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/arranging.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Transform
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Transform
text:
Shortcut:  G, R, S

You can move the selected node(s) by clicking and dragging any empty part of them.
Alternatively, press G, move the mouse, and click LMB to confirm.

Dragging a node on top of an existing link will intelligently insert the selected node into the link path.
This generally uses the first socket that matches the link type.
The automatic node attachment feature can be toggled with Alt.
When a node is automatically attached, the surrounding nodes
will be offset to the right or left depending on the T toggle;
see editors-nodes-usage-auto-offset for more information.

While dragging nodes, you can press F to toggle their parent
Frame:

- If the nodes are inside a frame, they will be detached from it.
- If the nodes are not inside a frame and there is a frame under the cursor, they will be attached to that frame.

In general, it is recommended to arrange your nodes so that data flows from left to right, top to bottom.

The width of a node can be adjusted by dragging its left or right border.
When multiple nodes are selected, resizing one node affects all selected nodes.

Rotating (R) and scaling (S) only apply when multiple nodes are selected,
and only affect their positions.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Connecting Sockets
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Connecting Sockets
text:
LMB-click on a socket and drag. "Connect to Output" will see a line coming out of it; this is called a *link*.
Keep dragging and connect the link to an input socket of another node, then release the LMB.

While multiple links can route out of an output socket, typically a single link can be attached to an input socket,
that is unless the input is a multi-socket input with looks like a pill shaped socket.

To swap multiple links of a similar type, press and hold Alt while moving a link.
This feature also works when adding a new link into a pre-existing socket.

To reposition the outgoing links of a node, rather than adding a new one,
hold Ctrl while dragging from an output socket.
This works for single as well as for multiple outgoing links.

Nodes that have no connections can be inserted on a link
by just moving the node over the link and release when the link is highlighted.

Make Links J
   Select multiple nodes with open sockets, then use the Make Links to create links between them.
   Use Make Links again if there are other nodes which can be connected.

Make and Replace Links Shift-J
   *Make and Replace Links* works similarly to *Make Links*, but it will replace existing links if any exist.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Mute Links
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Mute Links
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-Alt-RMB

Activate the menu item or hold the key combination,
then draw a line across one or more links to mute/unmute them.
A muted link acts as though it's no longer there; this also means the input fields
for specifying fixed values become visible again.

When muting links on the input side of a reroute node,
the links on its output side will be muted too.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Cut Links
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Cut Links
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-RMB

Activate the menu item or hold the key combination,
then draw a line across one or more links to delete them.

Note:

   The key combination is normally reserved for Lasso Select.
   In node editors, lasso selection is instead performed with Ctrl-Alt-LMB.

Detach Links Alt-LMB drag
   Use Detach Links to cut all the links attached to the selected nodes
   and move the nodes to a new location.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Cut/Copy/Paste
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Cut/Copy/Paste
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-C, Ctrl-V

These operators allow transferring nodes within a node tree,
between different node trees, or even between Blender instances.

Cut Ctrl-X
   Removes the selected nodes and places them on the clipboard.
   When possible, links are automatically reconnected to preserve the node flow.

Copy Ctrl-C
   Copies the selected nodes to the clipboard, including the connections between them.

Paste Ctrl-V
   Inserts the nodes from the clipboard into the node tree.

Note:

   Pasted nodes are placed at the same coordinates as when they were copied.
   The same considerations as duplicating nodes apply.

Tip:

   Nodes can be copied and pasted between Blender instances.
   This also works across different node editors, provided the node
   types are supported by the destination editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Duplicate
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Duplicate
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-D

Select one or more nodes, activate the menu item or press the key combination,
then move the mouse to a new location and click LMB (or press Return)
to place the duplicated node(s).

Note:

   When you duplicate a node, the new node will be positioned *exactly* on top of the node that was duplicated.
   If you leave it there (and it is quite easy to do so),
   you can **not** easily tell that there are *two* nodes there!
   When in doubt, select a node and move it slightly to see if something is hidden underneath.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Duplicate Linked
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Duplicate Linked
text:
Shortcut:  Alt-D

Duplicate selected nodes, but not their node trees (in the case of group nodes), and move them.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Swap
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Swap
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-S

The *Swap* operator replaces the selected node with another node type chosen from the menu.

All existing links are automatically reconnected where possible,
matching input and output sockets by name and type.
If a connection cannot be matched, it is left unconnected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Mute
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Mute
text:
Shortcut:  M

Muting a node removes its contribution to the node tree,
and makes all links pass through it without change.
Links will appear red as an indicator of passing through the muted node.

Tip:

   Individual node links can be muted with bpy.ops.node.links_mute.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Node Preview
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Node Preview
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-H

Shows/Hides a preview region on the node that displays the frame
after that node's operation has been applied. This can also be toggled
by clicking the material ball icon in the node header.

Note: This operator are only available in the :doc:`Compositor </compositing/index>`.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Unconnected Sockets
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Unconnected Sockets
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-H

Collapses/Expands any input or output sockets that have no other nodes connected to them.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Collapse
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Collapse
text:
Shortcut:  H

Collapses the node so only the node header is visible.
This can also be toggled by clicking the triangle on the left of the node header.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Collapse and Hide Unused Sockets
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Collapse and Hide Unused Sockets
text:
Shortcut:  H

Applies both the bpy.ops.node.hide_socket_toggle and bpy.ops.node.hide_toggle operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Read View Layers
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Read View Layers
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-R

Reads all the current scene's render layers from cache, as needed.
This can be used to save RAM while rendering because the render layers do not have to be saved in RAM.
And also for recovering some information from a failed render.
For this to work, Cache Result must be enabled.

Note: This operator are only available in the :doc:`Compositor </compositing/index>`.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Delete with Reconnect
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Delete with Reconnect
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-X Ctrl-Delete

Deletes the selected node(s), then creates new links connecting their former input nodes
to their former output nodes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Nodes > Connect to Output
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Editing Nodes Connect to Output
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-Alt-LMB

Connect the output of the selected node to the final output of the node tree
(Material Output or World Output in Shader,
the final Group Output in Geometry Nodes and Compositor, Output in Texture Nodes),
or, if the node is inside a group, to the Group Output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/editing.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Node Groups
text:
Grouping nodes can simplify a node tree by hiding complexity and reusing common functionality.
A node group is visually identified by its green title bar.

Conceptually, node groups allow you to treat a *set* of nodes as a single unit.
They are similar to functions in programming: reusable, composable, and parametrizable.

For example, suppose you create a "Wood" material and want to use it in multiple colors.
You could duplicate the entire node setup for each color, but maintaining those duplicates
would be tedious if you later decide to change the wood grain detail.
Instead, you can move the nodes that generate the wood pattern into a node group.
Each material can then reuse this group and supply a custom color as input.
Any updates to the grain detail need to be made only once—inside the node group.

Node groups can be nested; that is, a group can contain other groups.

Note:

   Recursive node groups are prohibited to avoid infinite recursion.
   A group cannot contain itself, directly or indirectly.

Tip:

   Like other data-blocks, node groups with names that start with . are hidden
   from menus and lists and can only be accessed via search.
   This is useful for node asset authors who want to hide internal utility groups from end users.

*Group Input* and *Group Output* nodes are used to represent data flowing into and out of the group.

The *Group Input* node provides access to the group's input sockets from within the node group.
These sockets act as parameters that control the behavior of the group from the outside.
You can connect them to internal nodes to drive values such as factors, colors, or geometry inputs.

Note:

   Input values that do not affect the output will be grayed out.

The *Group Output* node defines the data that is passed out of the node
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Managing Inputs/Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Managing Inputs/Outputs
text:
You can add, remove, and reorder input and output sockets in the *Group* panel in the Sidebar.
New sockets can also be created directly by dragging a link to or from the hollow socket
on the *Group Input* or *Group Output* node to another socket in the node editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Reusing Node Groups
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Reusing Node Groups
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-A

Existing node groups can be placed again after they're initially defined, be it in the same
node tree or a different one. It's also possible to import node groups from a different blend-file
using File > Link/Append.

Tip:

   When appending node groups from another blend-file,
   Blender does not distinguish between types such as material or compositing groups.
   To avoid confusion, it is recommended to adopt a naming convention, like using prefixes
   (`Mat_`, `Comp_`, `Geo_`, etc.), to indicate the group's context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Group
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Group
text:
This panel contains properties that relate the group node such as its name and look.

Name
   The name of node as displayed in the interface-nodes-parts-title.

Description
   The message displayed when hovering over the interface-nodes-parts-title or in add menus.

Color Tag
   Color tag of the node group which influences the header color.

Node Width
   The width for newly created group nodes.

   :bl-icon:`node` (Set Default Node Width)
      Set the width based on the parent group node in the current context

Show Manage Panel Geometry Nodes
   Enables displaying the geometry_nodes-manage_panel panel in Geometry Nodes modifiers
   when creating a modifier from a node group asset.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Usage :guilabel:`Geometry Nodes`
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Usage :guilabel:`Geometry Nodes`
text:
This panel is only visible in the Geometry Node Editor.

Modifier
   The node group is intended for use with the geometry nodes.

Tool
   The node group is intended to be used as a tool.

The data-block menu in the header of the Geometry Node Editor
only lists the node groups whose Usage matches the current bpy.types.SpaceNodeEditor.node_tree_sub_type.

Tip:

   If you accidentally disable both Usages, the node group will not be accessible through the
   data-block menu anymore. To make it accessible again, you can add it as a node to a different node
   group (Add > Group), select that node, and press Tab to enter it.
   From there, you can enable one of the Usages again.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Group Sockets
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Group Sockets
text:
This panel is used to add, remove, reorder, and edit the user interface elements of a node group.
It defines how sockets appear on the group node and organizes them for clarity and usability.

Available item types include:

- **Inputs**: Define input sockets for the node group.
- **Outputs**: Define output sockets for the node group.
- **Panels**:
   Group and organize related sockets together. Useful for structuring complex node setups.
   Panels always appear at the bottom of the node interface. They can be nested by dragging one panel
   on top of another in the interface item list.
- **Panel Toggle**:
   Adds a boolean checkbox to a panel's header, allowing control over its contents.
   This option is only available when a panel is selected in the interface item list.

   Panel toggles have their own options under the *Panel Toggle* subpanel.
   Note that toggle sockets are **not** listed directly in the interface list—panels with toggles
   instead show a boolean socket icon next to their name. To make the toggle socket visible again,
   it must be unlinked from the panel.

Note:

      A panel toggle does not automatically disable or gray out its sockets.
      To visually and functionally disable sockets, use a
      Switch Node or similar logic and disconnect the socket
      manually.

Interface Item List
   A UI list view showing all input/output sockets and panels.
   Each item can be renamed and configured individually. The name appears in the node's user interface.

Tip:

      Selecting a socket label on the node itself will also select that socket in the *Interface Item List*.

   Duplicate Item
      Duplicates the selected socket or panel.

   Make Panel Toggle
      Converts the selected boolean input into a toggle for its parent panel.
      Only avai
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Animation
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Animation
text:
Controls animation data for node group properties, including active Actions
and their assigned Slot.

See animation-actions-slots-manual-assign for more information.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Make Group
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Make Group
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-G

Creates a new node group that contains all selected nodes.

*Group Input* and *Group Output* nodes will be created to represent connections to unselected nodes outside the group.
Inputs will be routed to the *Group Input* and outputs routed to the *Group Output*.

When grouping a **single node**, the resulting node group will:

- Preserve the interface of the original node, including panels and default values.
- Inherit the name of the original node

When grouping **multiple nodes**, the group is created with inputs and outputs sockets generated from the connections.
In this case, a generic name such as "NodeGroup", "NodeGroup.001", etc. is used.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Insert Into Group
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Insert Into Group
text:
Moves the selected nodes into the active group node.
To use, select a set of nodes, ending with the destination group node,
then, running the operation will move those nodes into that group.
The moved nodes are collected into a group of their own to preserve their connection context,
having their own group input and output nodes.
The group's existing input and output nodes are updated with new sockets, if any, from the new nodes.
The node group must be edited to contain a single *Group Input* and a single *Group Output* node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Edit Group
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Edit Group
text:
Shortcut:  Tab, Ctrl-Tab

With a node group selected, press Tab to move into it and see its content.
Press Tab again (or Ctrl-Tab) to leave the group and go back to
its parent, which could be the top-level node tree or another node group.
You can refer to the breadcrumbs in the top left corner of the node editor
to see where you are in the hierarchy.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Ungroup
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Ungroup
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-Alt-G

Removes the group and places the individual nodes into your editor workspace.
No internal connections are lost, and now you can link internal nodes to other nodes in your workspace.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Separate
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Separate
text:
Shortcut:  P

The *Separate* operator removes the selected nodes from a node group
and places them in the parent node tree.
This is useful when nodes need to be edited outside of a group for clarity or reuse.

Copy
   Duplicates the selected nodes into the parent node tree,
   while keeping the originals inside the group.
   This is useful when you want to reuse nodes outside of the group
   but still preserve the group definition.

Move
   Moves the selected nodes to the parent node tree,
   removing them from the original group.
   This is useful when simplifying a group or exposing its contents directly.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Groups > Join Group Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Groups Join Group Inputs
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-J

Merges multiple selected *Group Input* nodes into one consolidated *Group Input* node when possible.
Existing links are preserved, and duplicate inputs are unified to reduce clutter and simplify the node tree.

This operation is useful for cleaning up node groups that have become
disorganized or contain redundant input nodes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/groups.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Nodes
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Nodes Nodes
text:
Blender contains different node-based editors with different purposes,
so this section only explains how to work with nodes in general.
The list below shows the different types of nodes and where they're documented.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Header
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Header
text:
The *Header* contains various menus, buttons and options, partially based on the current node tree type.

View
   This menu changes your view of the editor.
Select
   This menu allows you to select a node or groups of nodes.
Add
   This menu allows you to add nodes.
Node
   This menu allows you to do things with selected nodes.

:bl-icon:`pinned` Pinned
   When enabled, the editor always displays the currently selected node tree,
   regardless of changes in the active object or scene.
   This allows you to edit a material, texture, or compositor node tree independently
   of what is selected in the 3D Viewport or which scene is active.
   Useful when working across multiple objects or scenes but wanting to keep the editor
   focused on one specific node tree.
Parent Node Tree
   Leaves the current node group and returns to the parent node group/tree.
Snapping
   Change options for snapping node positions to achieve a cleaner node tree layout.
   See arranging.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Overlays
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Overlays
text:
Overlays are information that is displayed on top of the nodes and node trees.
There is a toggle to show or hide all overlays for the node editor next to the overlay popover.

Wire Colors
   Color node links based on their connected sockets.

Reroute Auto Labels
   Label Reroute Nodes
   based on the label of connected reroute nodes.

Context Path
   Display breadcrumbs in the upper left corner indicating the hierarchy location
   of the node tree/group that's currently being displayed.

   Clicking an earlier breadcrumb returns to that level of the hierarchy. The arrow next to a breadcrumb opens a menu
   containing the node groups that can be entered from that level. The groups are sorted by name, and the group
   on the current path is highlighted. Selecting a group enters it directly.

Annotations
   Displays Annotations in the preview region.

Previews
   Display each node's interface-nodes-parts-preview if the node's preview is also toggled.

Timings
   Display each node's last execution time.
   This option is only available for compositing and geometry nodes.

   In the context of geometry nodes, see modeling-geometry_nodes-inspection-timings.

Text Info
   Displays information about the image in the upper-left corner of the
   Compositor editor, similar to the Image Editor.

   The overlay shows the render resolution (*Render Size*) and the
   dimensions of the displayed image (*Image Size*).

Render Region
   Displays a border showing the final render region defined in the scene.
   Space outside the render region appear shaded for reference.

Passepartout Alpha
   Controls the opacity of the shaded area outside the render region.
   Higher values darken the outside area more, making the render region stand out.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Toolbar
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Toolbar
text:
The *Toolbar* contains a set of tools that can be used in the node editor.

Select
   Select or move nodes and links.

   Select Box
      Select nodes or links by dragging a box around them.

   Select Circle
      Select nodes or links by clicking or dragging with a circular brush.

   Select Lasso
      Select nodes or links by drawing a free-form lasso.

Annotate
   Draw free-hand annotation.

   Annotate Line
      Draw straight line annotation.
   Annotate Polygon
      Draw a polygon annotation.
   Annotate Eraser
      Erase previous drawn annotations.

Link Cuts
   Delete connections between nodes by drawing a line across the links.
   See bpy.ops.node.links_cut for more information.

Mute Links
   Mute connections between nodes by drawing a line across the links.
   Muted links are kept in place but ignored in evaluation.
   See bpy.ops.node.links_mute for more information.

Add Reroute
   Insert a reroute
   point on links by drawing a line across them.
   Reroute nodes help organize complex node trees by redirecting connections.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Sidebar
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Sidebar
text:
The Sidebar region contains properties for
the currently selected node as well as node editor-specific settings.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Node
text:
The *Node* tab in the Sidebar contains properties that control the behavior
and appearance of the active node. Available options depend on the node
type and the editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Properties
text:
The properties that are shown depend on the type of node selected,
e.g. a Mix node has different properties than a Mask node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Custom Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Custom Properties
text:
Create and manage your own properties to store data in the active node.
See the Custom Properties page for more information.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Annotations
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Annotations
text:
You can select the Annotate tool in the Toolbar to make annotations in the node editor.
See Annotate Tool for more info.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Navigating
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Navigating
text:
Navigating the node editors is done with the use of both mouse movement and keyboard shortcuts.

Pan MMB
   Move the view up, down, left and right.
Zoom Ctrl-MMB, Wheel
   Move the camera forwards and backwards.
Frame Selected NumpadPeriod
   Adjusts the zooms to fit only the selected nodes in the view.
Frame All Home
   Adjusts the zoom to fit all nodes in the view.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Editors > Adding Nodes
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Editors Adding Nodes
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-A

Nodes are added via the *Add* menu in the editor's header or using a keyboard shortcut.

Nodes can also be added by dragging a connection from an existing node's input or output socket
and dropping the connection above an empty space instead of connecting to another socket.
This action will open a search menu with a list of compatible nodes
and their sockets that can be added and connected to the existing node.
Confirming the menu selection will add the node which can then be moved and placed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/node_editors.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Node Parts
text:
All nodes in Blender are based on a similar construction.
This applies to any type of node.
These parts include the title, sockets, properties and more.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Title
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Title
text:
The title shows the name/type of the node;
it can be overridden by changing the node's Label.
On the left side of the title is the *collapse* toggle
which can be used to collapse the node. This can also be done with H.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Preview
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Preview
text:
Previews are an overlay that shows a small image above the node displaying the node result.
Not all nodes support previews, but the ones that do can be toggled using
the :bl-icon:`hide_off`/:bl-icon:`hide_on` icons in the top right-hand corner of the node next to the title.

Previews can be disabled for the whole node tree by using
Previews overlay toggle.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Sockets
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Sockets
text:
Sockets are the inputs and outputs of a node, displayed as small colored shapes
along its left and right edges. Input sockets receive data from other nodes,
while output sockets provide data to connected nodes.

Each socket has a shape and color that indicate the type of data it handles.

Sockets can be connected by dragging from an output socket to a compatible input socket.

Some nodes allow sockets to be added dynamically.
These sockets can be renamed by double-clicking their names.

Unused sockets can be hidden using Ctrl-H, reducing visual clutter in complex node trees.

Shader (bright green)
   Used for shaders in Cycles and EEVEE.
Geometry (Sea Green)
   Used in Geometry Nodes.
Menu (Dark Gray)
   Used for enum style inputs that show a dropdown menu or radio button in the UI.
Bundle (dark turquoise)
   Represents a generic bundle of multiple data types.
   Bundles can contain several values (e.g., geometry, vectors, or colors) grouped together,
   allowing compact data transfer between nodes.
Closure (light brown)
   Used in Shader Nodes and Geometry Nodes
   for logical or procedural encapsulation.
   A closure can store and pass groups of node inputs and logic, enabling reusable "callable" node behaviors.

Boolean (light pink)
   Used to pass a true or false value.
Color (yellow)
   Indicates that the socket accepts/produces color information.
   The colors may or may not have an alpha component depending on the node tree type.
Float (light gray)
   Indicates that the socket accepts/produces floating-point numbers.
Integer (lime green)
   Used to pass an integer value (a number without a fractional component).
Integer Vector (slate blue)
   A vector made of integer values which can be either two or three-dimensional.
String (light blue)
   Used to pass a text v
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Socket Shape
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Socket Shape
text:
Data sockets can have different shapes, indicating the data structure use to transport data.
The data structure determines how values are passed and interpreted.
More complex structures allow passing multiple values through a single connection.

Auto
   Automatically detects a good structure type based on how the socket is used.
Dynamic (Circle)
   Socket can work with multiple types of structures.
Single (Rectangle)
   These sockets expects a single value, they are represented by a tall rectangular shape.
Fields (Diamond)
   Represents a value that can vary per element (e.g. per point, edge, or face).
   You can think of a field as a "value map", similar to how the brightness of pixels
   in a grayscale image represents varying values across space.

   If a single value is connected to a field socket,
   it is implicitly broadcast all elements receive the same value.
   It also means that socket-inspection will show the value instead of field input names.

Seealso:

      Geometry Nodes Fields Documentation
Grid (Four Squares)
   Represents a grid data structure, which stores values sampled across a **2D surface** or a **3D volume**.
   Grids can represent data such as image pixels, voxel densities, or other sampled values in space.
   They allow complex operations where values are distributed continuously across space,
   rather than being attached to individual geometry elements.
Lists (Three Lines)
   Represents an ordered collection of values.

   Lists can contain any number of items of the same data type and allow multiple values
   to be passed through a single socket. They are commonly used for operations that gather,
   filter, sort, or process collections of values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Inputs
text:
The inputs are located on the bottom left side of the node,
and provide the data the node needs to perform its function.
Each input socket, except for the green shader input, when disconnected,
has a default value which can be edited via a color, numeric, or vector interface input.
In the screenshot of the node above, the second color option is set by a color interface input.

Some nodes have special sockets that can accept multiple inputs.
These sockets will have an ellipsis shape rather than a circle to indicate their special behavior.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Outputs
text:
The outputs are located on the top right side of the node,
and can be connected to the input of nodes further down the node tree.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Conversion
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Conversion
text:
Some socket types can be converted to others either implicitly or explicitly.
Implicit conversion happens automatically without the need of a conversion node.
For example, Float sockets and Color sockets can be linked to each other.

Once a socket conversion is made, data may be lost and cannot be retrieved later down the node tree.
Implicit socket conversion can sometimes change the data units as well.
When plugging a *Value* input node into an angle socket, it'll default to use radians
regardless of the scene's bpy.types.UnitSettings.
This happens because the Value node has no unit while the angle input does.

Valid conversions:

- Between color and vector -- mapping between color channels and vector components.
- Between color and float -- the color data is converted to its grayscale equivalent.
- Color/float/vector to Shader -- implicitly converts to color and gives the result of using an Emission node.
- Between float and integer -- integers simply become floats, floats are truncated.
- Between float and vector --  when a float becomes a vector the value is used for each component.
  When a vector becomes a float the average of the components is taken.
- Between float and boolean -- values greater than 0 are true, true maps to 1, and false maps to 0.
- Between rotations and matrices.

Explicit conversion requires the use of dedicated conversion nodes.
Examples include:

- shader to rgb
- rgb to bw
- implicit conversion

Some nodes also provide conversion operations directly. For example,
the math node includes
functions to convert between degrees and radians.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Parts > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Node Parts Properties
text:
Many nodes have settings which can affect the way they interact with inputs and outputs.
Node settings are located below the outputs and above any inputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/parts.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Selecting Nodes
text:
Nodes in the editor can be selected and manipulated.
Selections determine which nodes can be moved, duplicated, or connected.
The active node (last selected) is highlighted with a lighter outline.
It serves as the reference for certain operations, such as grouping or linking,
and also determines which properties are displayed in the *Sidebar* and *Properties Editor*.

Nodes are selected with LMB.
Multiple nodes can be selected by holding Shift-LMB.

Blender also provides a variety of selection tools and shortcuts for quickly choosing nodes
based on their type, connections, or layout.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Invert
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Invert
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-I

Inverts the current selection, selecting all unselected nodes and deselecting the currently selected ones.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Box Select
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Box Select
text:
Shortcut:  B

Click and drag to select nodes within a rectangular region.
See Box Select for more details.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Circle Select
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Circle Select
text:
Shortcut:  C

Click and drag with a circular brush to select nodes.
See Circle Select.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Linked From
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Linked From
text:
Shortcut:  L

Expands the selection to all nodes connected to the inputs of the selected nodes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Linked To
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Linked To
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-L

Expands the selection to all nodes connected from the outputs of the selected nodes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Select Grouped
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Select Grouped
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-G

Selects nodes that share similar properties with the active node.

- **Type**: Select all nodes of the same type (e.g. all *Math* nodes).
- **Color**: Select nodes with the same custom color.
  (This refers to user-assigned editor colors, not the color data processed by nodes.)
- **Prefix/Suffix**: Select nodes whose names match the same starting or ending text.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Activate Same Type Previous/Next
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Activate Same Type Previous/Next
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-] / Shift-[

Cycles through nodes of the same type, activating the previous or next node in the node tree
and centering it in the view.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selecting Nodes > Find Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes Selecting Nodes Find Node
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-F

Opens a search pop-up to quickly locate and select a node within the current node tree.
Nodes can be searched by name, socket label, warning messages,
or certain socket values such as strings and data-block references.

Once a match is selected, the editor view automatically pans and centers on the found node,
highlighting it for easy access.

This operator is especially useful in large node trees for navigating complex networks efficiently.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/selecting.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Comment Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Comment Node Comment Node
text:
The *Comment* node adds text annotations to a node tree, making it easier to
document complex setups and explain how different parts of a node tree work.

Unlike Frame Nodes,
which are primarily used to organize nodes into groups,
Comment nodes are designed for longer descriptions and notes.
They support multiple lines of text and basic Markdown formatting, allowing
comments to include headings, emphasis, and links.

Comment nodes have no input or output sockets and do not affect the
evaluation of the node tree.

The background color matches that of Frame nodes, with alternating shades
when nested inside frames to help distinguish the comment from its surroundings.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/comment.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Comment Node > Editing Comments
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Comment Node Editing Comments
text:
The text of a Comment node can be edited in several ways:

- Double-click the node.
- Select the node and press F2.
- Hover over the node and press Return.
- Click the :bl-icon:`greasepencil` icon on the node.
- Edit the text in the Sidebar > Node > Properties panel.

When not being edited, the comment is displayed with its Markdown formatting applied.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/comment.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Comment Node > Text Formatting
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Comment Node Text Formatting
text:
Comment nodes support basic Markdown syntax for formatting text.
For example:

.. code-block:: markdown

   # Main Heading

   ## Subheading

   **Bold text** and *italic text*.

   [Link to documentation](https://docs.blender.org/)

Markdown formatting is rendered directly within the node,
making it possible to create readable documentation without additional nodes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/comment.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Frame Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Frame Node Frame Node
text:
The *Frame* node is used to organize and group other nodes within the editor.
It helps manage complex node trees by visually grouping related nodes together.

Frames are particularly useful when the setup is too large to view easily at once,
or when you want to separate logical sections of a node tree without creating a reusable Node Group.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/frame.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Frame Node > Usage
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Frame Node Usage
text:
- Nodes can be added to a frame by dragging them inside it.
- Moving the frame also moves all contained nodes.
- Frames can be resized by dragging the corners or edges.
- The frame can display a custom label, useful for naming sections of your node setup.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/frame.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Frame Node > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Frame Node Properties
text:
Label Size
   Font size of the label. For example, for subordinate frames to have smaller titles.
Shrink
   Once a node is placed in the Frame, the Frame shrinks around it so as to remove wasted space.
   At this point it is no longer possible to select the edge of the Frame to resize it, instead resizing occurs
   automatically when nodes within the Frame are rearranged.
   This behavior can be changed by disabling this option.
Text
   When you need to display more comprehensive text, frame nodes can display the contents of a text data-block.
   This is read-only, so you will need to use the *Text Editor* to modify the contents.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/frame.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Frame Node > Join in New Frame
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Frame Node Join in New Frame
text:
Shortcut:  F

Creates a new *Frame* node around the selected nodes.

When called using the shortcut F, a popup appears allowing you to assign a custom
Label to the new frame node.
This label is shown as the title of the frame and can be used to describe its contents.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/frame.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Frame Node > Add to Frame
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Frame Node Add to Frame
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-P

Once a frame node is placed, nodes can be added by dropping them onto the frame or
by selecting the node(s) then the frame and using Ctrl-P.
This can be thought of as Parenting the selection to the frame.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/frame.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Frame Node > Remove from Frame
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Frame Node Remove from Frame
text:
Shortcut:  Alt-P

To remove nodes from a frame, select and use Alt-P.
This can be thought of as unparenting the selection from the frame.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/frame.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Layout Nodes
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Layout Nodes Layout Nodes
text:
Layout nodes help organize and document node trees without affecting their evaluation.
They can be used to group related nodes, organize connections, and add explanatory text,
making complex node setups easier to understand and maintain.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Reroute Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Layout Reroute Node Reroute Node
text:
A node used primarily for organization.
Reroute looks and behaves much like a socket on other nodes in that it supports one input
connection while allowing multiple output connections.

To quickly add a Reroute node into an existing connection, hold Shift and RMB
while sweeping across the link to add a *Reroute node*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/layout/reroute.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Enable Output Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Output Enable Output Node Enable Output Node
text:
The *Enable Output* node toggles the visibility and value
of a socket for a Node Group outputs.
It can be used to conditionally show or hide outputs from a node group depending on an input value or condition.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/output/enable_output.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Enable Output Node > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Output Enable Output Node Inputs
text:
Enable
   A boolean field controlling whether the connected output socket is visible and active.
   When *False*, the corresponding output socket in the group is hidden.
Value
   The value to pass to the output when it is enabled.
   This input can be any supported data type depending on the node's *Data Type* property.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/output/enable_output.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Enable Output Node > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Output Enable Output Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The data type of the *Value* input and *Value* output.
   This determines what kind of data the node passes through (e.g. *Float*, *Vector*, *Color*, *Geometry*, etc.).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/output/enable_output.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Enable Output Node > Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Output Enable Output Node Outputs
text:
Value
   The same data as the *Value* input when *Enable* is *True*.
   When *Enable* is *False*, the output is disabled and not available to the group output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/output/enable_output.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Enable Output Node > Usage
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Output Enable Output Node Usage
text:
The *Value* output can be connected to a *Switch*, *Index Switch*, or *Menu
Switch* node. The switch output must ultimately be connected to a Group Output.
The output is enabled based on the selected switch input, allowing different
group outputs to be enabled by different branches.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/output/enable_output.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Bundle Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Combine Bundle Node Combine Bundle Node
text:
The *Combine Bundle* node creates a new Bundle
from multiple input values.
Each input becomes an element of the bundle, identified by its socket name.
Values can be accessed in other parts of the node tree using the
Separate Bundle
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/combine_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Bundle Node > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Combine Bundle Node Inputs
text:
The node can contain an arbitrary number of input sockets.
Each socket can be given a custom name and type. Supported types include (but not limited to):

- Geometry
- Objects
- Values (e.g. float, integer, boolean, vector, color)
- Fields
- Nested Bundles
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/combine_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Bundle Node > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Combine Bundle Node Properties
text:
Properties are available in the *Node* tab of the Sidebar.

Sync Sockets
   Updates the current node to match the socket signature of the connected nodes.
   Use this after renaming, adding, or removing sockets.

Define Signature
   Locks the current item list and types to stabilize interfaces when publishing node groups.
   When enabled, adding/removing items is disabled until the option is turned off.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/combine_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Bundle Node > Bundle Items
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Combine Bundle Node Bundle Items
text:
List of bundle items
   Displays one entry per element in the bundle.
   Double-click to rename.

   Add Item
      Add a new socket to the bundle.
   Remove Item
      Delete the selected socket.

Type
   The data type for the selected item (e.g. Float, Vector, Geometry, Object, Bundle).
   For value types, a default value control is shown and used when the socket is unlinked.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/combine_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Bundle Item Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Get Bundle Item Node Get Bundle Item Node
text:
The *Get Bundle Item* node retrieves a value stored inside a bundle using a string path.
Bundles are used to group heterogeneous data together, and this node allows accessing
individual items from such a structure.

If the requested path does not exist in the bundle, a default value is returned and the
*Exists* output is set to false.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/get_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Bundle Item Node > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Get Bundle Item Node Inputs
text:
Bundle
   The input bundle to retrieve data from.

Path
   The path identifying the item inside the bundle.
   Paths are written using slash-separated to represent bundles inside other bundles.
   (for example: settings/size or attributes/color).

Remove
   If enabled, the retrieved item is removed from the bundle before it is passed through
   to the *Bundle* output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/get_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Bundle Item Node > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Get Bundle Item Node Properties
text:
Socket Type
   The data type of the retrieved item.
   This determines the type of the *Item* output socket.

Shape
   Defines the data structure supported by the *Item* output, such as a *Single* value,
   *Field*, or *Grid*.
   The shape determines how the data is evaluated and passed through the node network.

   This option is available in the Sidebar.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/get_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Bundle Item Node > Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Get Bundle Item Node Outputs
text:
Bundle
   The resulting bundle after optionally removing the retrieved item.

Item
   The value retrieved from the bundle at the specified path.
   If the path does not exist, this outputs the default value for the selected socket type.

Exists
   Outputs *True* if an item was found at the given path, otherwise *False*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/get_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Nested Bundle Paths Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Get Nested Bundle Paths Node Get Nested Bundle Paths Node
text:
The *Get Nested Bundle Paths* node searches a bundle and any nested bundles,
returning the paths to items that match the specified filter.

This is useful for locating typed bundles or values without requiring them
to exist at a fixed location within the bundle hierarchy.

Tip:

   This node searches recursively through nested bundles, making it useful
   for locating typed bundles regardless of where they are stored in the
   bundle hierarchy.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/get_nested_bundle_paths.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Nested Bundle Paths Node > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Get Nested Bundle Paths Node Inputs
text:
Bundle
   Bundle to search.

Mode
   Determines which bundle items are matched.

   :All: Return the paths to all items.
   :Bundle Type: Return the paths to typed bundles matching the specified type.
   :Data Type: Return the paths to values with the specified data type.

Pattern Mode Bundle Type
   How bundle types are matched.

   :Exact:
      Match bundles whose type exactly matches the specified type.
   :Wildcard:
      Match bundles whose type matches the specified pattern.

      The pattern may contain a single wildcard character (*).

Bundle Type Bundle Type
   Bundle type or pattern to search for.

Data Type Data Type
   Data type of bundle values to search for.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/get_nested_bundle_paths.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Node Bundles
text:
A *bundle* is a container that groups multiple values into one socket.
This makes it possible to pass many values through
a single link, similar to a *struct* in programming.

Bundles reduce the number of exposed inputs and outputs in a node group,
and can contain mixed data types such as geometry, fields, values, objects,
or even nested bundles.

.. --- section-nodes ---
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles > Nodes
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Nodes
text:
The following nodes are provided for working with bundles:

Bundle nodes allow adding or removing an arbitrary number of sockets,
with flexible type support.

Bundles can be attached to geometry using the
get geometry bundle and
set geometry bundle.
These can be used to pass bundled data between modifiers and objects.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles > Typed Bundles
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Typed Bundles
text:
A typed bundle is a bundle that contains a special *Type* item identifying
its purpose. The type is stored as a string and allows node groups to
recognize bundles without relying on their internal structure.

Using types makes bundles easier to exchange between node groups and
different Geometry Nodes modifiers, since a node group can search for a
specific type rather than assuming a particular bundle layout.

Bundles can also contain other bundles, allowing complex data to be
organized hierarchically.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles > Creating Typed Bundles
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Creating Typed Bundles
text:
The Add Typed Bundle operator
creates a typed bundle by constructing a bundle containing the required *Type* item.

Important:

   The string item named Type is reserved for identifying typed bundles.
   It should not be used for any other purpose within a bundle.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles > Searching Typed Bundles
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Searching Typed Bundles
text:
The Get Nested Bundle Paths node searches a
bundle hierarchy for bundles with a matching type.

This allows node groups to locate typed bundles even when they are nested
inside other bundles.

For example, a geometry may contain multiple bundles describing different
components. A node group can search for all bundles of a particular type
without requiring them to exist at a fixed location.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles > Usage
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Usage
text:
Bundles are useful in many workflows:

- **Simplified interfaces** -- group inputs into a single socket for clarity.
- **Physics simulations** -- package all entities and constraints for a solver.
- **Declarative systems** -- store complex structured data for evaluation later.
- **Texture sets** -- combine PBR maps (Base Color, Roughness, Normal) into one socket.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Node Bundles > Socket Syncing
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Node Bundles Socket Syncing
text:
Bundles use socket names to match their inputs and outputs.
If two bundle nodes are connected but have mismatched signatures,
Blender can offer to sync them automatically.

- Sync happens automatically when a node is connected for the first time.
- Existing sockets are never updated automatically to avoid overwriting data.
- A :bl-icon:`file_refresh` button (*Sync Sockets*) button appears in the node header when a mismatch is detected,
  allowing manual synchronization.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Join Bundle Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Join Bundle Node Join Bundle Node
text:
The *Join Bundle* node combines multiple bundles into a single output bundle.
Each connected input bundle is merged together, producing one bundle
that contains all items from the inputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/join_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Join Bundle Node > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Join Bundle Node Inputs
text:
Bundle
   One or more input bundles to combine.
   Each bundle's contents are merged by name into the output bundle.

Note:

   If multiple bundles contain sockets with the same name (duplicate keys),
   the value from the first occurrence is used.
   An information icon in the node header will indicate if duplicate keys are detected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/join_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Join Bundle Node > Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Join Bundle Node Outputs
text:
Bundle
   The resulting bundle that contains all items from the input bundles.

   Use the separate bundle to access individual items from the combined bundle if needed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/join_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Bundle Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Separate Bundle Node Separate Bundle Node
text:
The *Separate Bundle* node extracts individual values from a
Bundle.
Each output corresponds to an element in the bundle, identified by its socket name.

This node is the counterpart of the
Combine Bundle
node and is typically used to retrieve structured data that was previously grouped together.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/separate_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Bundle Node > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Separate Bundle Node Properties
text:
Properties are available in the *Node* tab of the Sidebar.

Sync Sockets
   Updates the current node to match the socket signature of the connected nodes.
   Use this after renaming, adding, or removing sockets.

Define Signature
   Locks the current item list and types to stabilize interfaces when publishing node groups.
   When enabled, adding/removing items is disabled until the option is turned off.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/separate_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Bundle Node > Bundle Items
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Separate Bundle Node Bundle Items
text:
List of bundle items
   Displays one entry per element in the bundle.
   Double-click to rename.

   Add Item
      Add a new socket to the bundle.
   Remove Item
      Delete the selected socket.

Type
   The data type for the selected item (e.g. Float, Vector, Geometry, Object, Bundle).
   For value types, a default value control is shown and used when the socket is unlinked.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/separate_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Bundle Node > Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Separate Bundle Node Outputs
text:
This node has a dynamic set of output sockets. Each socket outputs the value of the corresponding
bundle item, using the item's name and type as defined in the bundle.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/separate_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Store Bundle Item Node
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Store Bundle Item Node Store Bundle Item Node
text:
The *Store Bundle Item* node writes a value into a bundle at a specified path.
If an item already exists at the given path, it is replaced.
If the path does not exist, it is created automatically.

This node is commonly used to build or modify bundles incrementally,
allowing heterogeneous data to be grouped and passed through node networks.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/store_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Store Bundle Item Node > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Store Bundle Item Node Inputs
text:
Bundle
   The input bundle to store data into.

Path
   The path identifying where the item will be stored inside the bundle.
   Paths are written using slash-separated to represent bundles inside other bundles.
   (for example: settings/size or attributes/color).

Item
   The value to store at the specified path.
   The data type and structure of this input are defined by the node properties.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/store_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Store Bundle Item Node > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Store Bundle Item Node Properties
text:
Socket Type
   The data type of the *Item* input.
   This determines the type of data that can be stored in the bundle.

Shape
   Defines the data structure supported by the *Item* input, such as a *Single* value,
   *Field*, or *Grid*.
   The shape determines how the data is evaluated and stored in the bundle.

   This option is available in the Sidebar.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/store_bundle_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Add Typed Bundle
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Add Typed Bundle Add Typed Bundle
text:
:Editor:    Geometry Node Editor

Adds a Combine Bundle node configured as a typed bundle.

The operator creates a *Combine Bundle* node containing the required
Type string item and initializes it with the chosen bundle type.
Additional bundle items can then be added as needed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/typed_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Add Typed Bundle > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Bundles Add Typed Bundle Inputs
text:
Type
   String identifying the type of the bundle.

Important:

   Typed bundles reserve the string item named Type to identify the
   bundle type.

   Renaming or removing this item, or using the name Type for another
   string item, will prevent the bundle from being recognized as a typed
   bundle.

Seealso:

   See Typed Bundles for more information about typed bundles.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/bundles/typed_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Closure Closure Closure
text:
The *Closure* node defines a zone that encapsulates a reusable section of nodes behaving like a function.
It specifies inputs, outputs, and internal logic that can be executed elsewhere in the node tree using an
Evaluate Closure node.

Closures allow users to pass custom procedural logic into node groups, making tools more modular and adaptable.
Instead of duplicating or editing an existing group, a closure can expose user-defined behavior while preserving
the structure of the main system.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/closure/closure.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure > Inputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Closure Closure Inputs
text:
Closures define their own inputs, which act as parameters for the internal node logic.
These inputs can be created by dragging the blank input socket into another socket or by adding sockets manually in
the node's properties. Each input defines a parameter that the closure can receive when it is evaluated elsewhere.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/closure/closure.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure > Properties
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Closure Closure Properties
text:
The *Closure* node does not have functional properties of its own, but its interface is configurable through the
*Node* tab in the Sidebar. Inputs and outputs can be added, removed, and renamed to define the closure's signature.

Sync Sockets
   Updates the current node to match the socket signature of the connected nodes.
   Use this after renaming, adding, or removing sockets.

Define Signature
   Marks the current zone as the source of a closure signature that other nodes can reference. This ensures consistent
   input and output definitions across multiple closure instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/closure/closure.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure > Input Items
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Closure Closure Input Items
text:
List of input sockets
   Displays one entry per socket defined in the closure. Double-click an entry to rename it.

Add Item
   Add a new input socket to the closure.

Remove Item
   Delete the selected input socket.

Type
   Defines the data type for the selected socket (e.g. Float, Vector, Geometry, Object, Bundle).
   For value types, a default value control appears and is used when the socket is unlinked.

Shape
   Defines the data structure supported by the input socket, such as a *Single* value, *Field*, or *Grid*.
   The shape determines how the data is evaluated and passed through the node network.
   See interface-controls-nodes-socket_shape for more information.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/closure/closure.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure > Output Items
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Closure Closure Output Items
text:
Available when the closure's output zone is selected.

List of output sockets
   Displays one entry per socket defined in the closure output. Double-click to rename.

Add Item
   Add a new output socket to the closure.

Remove Item
   Delete the selected output socket.

Type
   Defines the data type for the selected socket (e.g. Float, Vector, Geometry, Object, Bundle).
   For value types, a default value control appears and is used when the socket is unlinked.

Shape
   Defines the data structure supported by the input socket, such as a *Single* value, *Field*, or *Grid*.
   The shape determines how the data is evaluated and passed through the node network.
   See interface-controls-nodes-socket_shape for more information.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/interface/controls/nodes/types/utilities/closure/closure.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure > Outputs
keywords: Interface > Controls > Nodes > Types > Utilities > Closure Closure Outputs
text:
