source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/geometry_materials.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Material Index Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Material Index Node Material Index Node
text:
The *Material Index* node outputs which material in the list of materials of the geometry
each element corresponds to. Currently the node supports mesh data, where material_index
is a built-in attribute on faces.

The node to set this data is
the Set Material Index node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/material_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Material Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Material Selection Node Material Selection Node
text:
The *Material Selection* node provides a selection for meshes that use this material.
Since the material_index is stored on each face, the output will be implicitly interpolated to
a different domain when necessary. For example, every vertex connected to
a selected face will be selected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/material_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Replace Material Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Replace Material Node Replace Material Node
text:
The *Replace Material* node swaps one material with another.
Replacing a material with this node is more efficient than creating a selection of all faces
with the old material with the material selection
and then using the set material.

Note:

   Currently this node only adjusts mesh data.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/replace_material.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Replace Material Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Replace Material Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Old
   Material that is going to be replaced.

New
   Material that is replacing the old material.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/replace_material.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Material Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Set Material Node Set Material Node
text:
The *Set Material* changes the material assignment in the specified selection,
by adjusting the material_index attribute. If the material is already used
on the geometry, the existing material index will be reused.

Note:

   This node adjusts mesh, curves, point clouds, and volume data;
   other data types do not support materials.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/set_material.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Material Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Set Material Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input containing a mesh.

Material
   The material to apply to the geometry.

Selection
   Whether to change the material of each face.
   True values mean the material will be changed, false values mean it will remain the same.

   Note, volumes and point clouds only support a single material,
   in these cases a field input will be ignored.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/set_material.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Material Index Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Set Material Index Node Set Material Index Node
text:
The *Set Material Index* node sets the material index for a geometry.

The node to get this data is the Material Index
node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/set_material_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Material Index Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Material Set Material Index Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Whether to change the material index for each face.
   True values mean the material index will be changed, false values mean it will remain the same.

Material Index
   The new material index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/material/set_material_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bake Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bake Node Bake Node
text:
The *Bake* node allows saving and loading intermediate geometries.
This node bakes parts of the node tree for better performance.

The data format used to store geometry data is not considered to be an import/export format.
Volume objects, however, are saved using the OpenVDB file format which can be used interoperably.

Important:

   - It's not guaranteed that data written with one Blender version can be read by another Blender version.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bake.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bake Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bake Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input, which is used as the default bake item.
   More bake items can be added by dragging sockets into the blank socket or in the *Bake Items* panel.
   Items can be renamed by Ctrl-LMB on the socket name or in the nodes *Properties* panel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bake.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bake Node > Bake Items
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bake Node Bake Items
text:
:Editor:    Geometry Node Editor

The *Bake Items* panel is used to manage the input sockets
of the node thus also managing what data is baked.

Bake Items List
   Used to manage the inputs and outputs of the bake node.
   Items can be added, removed, renamed, and sorted.

Socket Type
   The data (bpy.types.NodeLink) of the input/output.

Attribute Domain
   The attribute domain used to evaluate the input field on.

Is Attribute
   Bake item is an attribute stored on a geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bake.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bake Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bake Node Properties
text:
Note:

   Some properties can only be edited in the Properties panel
   (Sidebar > Node > Properties).

Bake Mode
   The *Bake* node can calculate the geometry of a single frame or an animation.

   :Animation:
      Bakes the geometry data for multiple frames.
      By default the scene frame range is used, however, a *Custom Range* can also be defined.
   :Still: Bakes the geometry data of the current frame.

Bake
   Performs all necessary geometry calculations and saves the data on disk or packed into the .blend file.

   Pack/Unpack
      Packs or unpacks already baked data. When unpacking, there are different options to control where the data will
      be stored. The options are the same as for the Unpack Resources operator.

   :bl-icon:`trash` Delete Geometry Node Bake
      Deletes the bake data.

Bake Target
   Specifies where the baked data should be stored.

   :Inherit from Modifier:
      The setting is copied from the modifier that contains the bake node. This is the default.
   :Packed:
      The baked data is packed into the .blend file. So no separate file is necessary.
   :Disk:
      The baked data is stored in a separate directory on disk.

Custom Path
   Specify a path where the baked data should be stored manually.

   Bake Path
      Location on disk where the baked data is stored.
      Note, this path is also used for simulation zones.

Custom Range Animation
   Override the simulation frame range from the scene.

Start, End
   The start and end frame numbers for the custom range.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bake.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bake Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bake Node Outputs
text:
For each input, the same output is added to act as a pass through.

Geometry
   Standard geometry output, which is used as the default bake item.
   More bake items can be added by dragging sockets into the blank socket or in the *Bake Items* panel.
   Items can be renamed by Ctrl-LMB on the socket name or in the nodes *Properties* panel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bake.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bounding Box Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bounding Box Node Bounding Box Node
text:
The *Bounding Box* node creates a box mesh with the minimum volume that encapsulates
the geometry of the input. The node also can output the vector positions of the bounding dimensions.

The mesh output and the *Min* and *Max* outputs do not take instances into account. Instead,
for instanced geometry, a bounding box is computed for each instance rather than the whole geometry.
To compute the bounding box including the instances,
a realize instances can be used.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bounding_box.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bounding Box Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bounding Box Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Use Radius
   For curves, point clouds, and Grease Pencil objects,
   include the radius attribute when calculating the bounds.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bounding_box.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bounding Box Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Bounding Box Node Outputs
text:
Bounding Box
   The resulting box that encapsulate the input geometry.

Min
   The coordinates corresponding to the box's -X, -Y, -Z position values,
   i.e. how far the box extends in each of the negative axes directions.

Max
   The coordinates corresponding to the box's +X, +Y, +Z position values,
   i.e. how far the box extends in each of the positive axes directions.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/bounding_box.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Convex Hull Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Convex Hull Node Convex Hull Node
text:
The *Convex Hull* node outputs a convex mesh that is enclosing all points in the input geometry.

Note:

   When the node is used on a geometry with instances, the algorithm will run once per instance,
   resulting in many convex hull meshes in the instance geometries. The *Realize Instances* node can
   be used to get a convex hull of an entire geometry.

Important:

   Volumes are not supported by this node, and attributes are not automatically transferred to the result.

Note:

   This node is affected by the limitations of floating point precision. If points are too close together,
   they may be merged in the result mesh.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/convex_hull.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Delete Geometry Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Delete Geometry Node Delete Geometry Node
text:
The *Delete Geometry* node removes the selected part of a geometry.
It behaves similarly to the Delete tool in Edit Mode.
The type of elements to be deleted can be specified with the domain and mode properties.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/delete_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Delete Geometry Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Delete Geometry Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field that is true for parts of the geometry to be deleted.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/delete_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Delete Geometry Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Delete Geometry Node Properties
text:
Domain
   The domain on which the selection field is evaluated.

   :Point:
      The selection is on the points, control points, and vertices of the geometry.
   :Edge:
      The selection is on the edges of the mesh component. The other components
      are not modified.
   :Face:
      The selection is on the faces of the mesh component. The other components
      are not modified.
   :Spline:
      The selection is on the splines in the curve component. For each spline, it
      will either be deleted entirely or not at all. The other components are not
      modified.
   :Instance:
      The selection is on the top-level instances, and the entire instance is
      removed if it is selected. If the input also contains realized geometry,
      that will be unaffected.

Mode
   The type of elements to be affected.
   This only applies to the mesh component.

   :All:
      Vertices, edges, and faces in the selection will be deleted.
   :Only Edges & Faces:
      Vertices won't be deleted, even if they are in the selection.
   :Only Faces:
      Only faces in the selection will be deleted.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/delete_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Displace Geometry Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Displace Geometry Node Displace Geometry Node
text:
The *Displace Geometry* node moves geometry elements along a specified direction or vector,
offsetting their positions to create deformations or surface displacements.
It can be used to apply procedural surface detail, simulate wave-like motion, or modify
shapes based on fields such as textures or vertex attributes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/displace_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Displace Geometry Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Displace Geometry Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   The input geometry to displace.

Selection
   Determines which elements of the geometry are affected by the displacement.
   Unselected elements remain unchanged.

Strength
   The distance to move each element along the chosen offset direction or vector.

Offset Method
   Determines how the displacement direction is defined.

   :Normal: Offsets elements along their surface normal direction.
   :Vector: Offsets elements according to a custom input vector.

Offset Distance Normal
   The displacement distance when using *Normal* mode.

Offset Vector Vector
   The displacement vector when using *Vector* mode.
   The vector is normalized internally unless otherwise specified.

Substeps
   The number of intermediate steps to divide the displacement into.
   Fields, including normal and position, are re-evaluated at each substep for more stable
   or accurate iterative results.

Post Substep Process
   A index
   that defines a geometry operation to apply after each substep of the displacement.
   This allows additional geometry processing to be performed during the iterative displacement.

   The closure has the following parameters:

   - **Geometry** -- The geometry at the current substep.
   - **Selection** -- The selected elements at that stage.
   - **Strength** -- The displacement strength for the substep.
   - **Substep Index** -- The current substep iteration number.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/displace_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Displace Geometry Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Displace Geometry Node Outputs
text:
Geometry
   The displaced geometry after applying the offset according to the specified method and parameters.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/displace_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Duplicate Elements Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Duplicate Elements Node Duplicate Elements Node
text:
The *Duplicate Elements* node creates a new geometry with the specified elements
from the input duplicated an arbitrary number of times. The positions of elements
are not changed, so all of the duplicates will be at the exact same location.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/duplicate_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Duplicate Elements Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Duplicate Elements Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field that is true for parts of the geometry to be deleted.

Amount
   Field indicating how many times each input element should be duplicated.
   If the value is zero for an element, it will not be included in the output at all.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/duplicate_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Duplicate Elements Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Duplicate Elements Node Properties
text:
Domain
   The type of geometry element to duplicate

   :Point:
      Duplicate the points of meshes, curves, or point clouds.
      Any other elements will not be included in the output.
   :Edge:
      Duplicate mesh edges. Faces will not be included in the output.
   :Faces:
      Duplicate mesh faces. Each duplicated face will be separate,
      in other words they will not share edges with other faces.
   :Spline:
      Individual curves from the input curves component will be duplicated.
   :Instances:
      Input top-level instances will be duplicated.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/duplicate_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Duplicate Elements Node > Output
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Duplicate Elements Node Output
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry output.

Duplicate Index
   An attribute field with a value for every output element describing which
   duplicate of the corresponding input. The value for every input element will
   start at 0 and increase to Amount - 1.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/duplicate_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Duplicate Elements Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Duplicate Elements Node Examples
text:
Combined with the geometry to instance,
this can be used to create a basic efficient "Array" operation. This should be more efficient
because the duplicates are instances.

The "Duplicate Index" is used to move each instance in the result a different amount.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/duplicate_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Geometry Components Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Get Geometry Components Node Get Geometry Components Node
text:
The *Get Geometry Components* node extracts a single component from the input geometry.

It can be used to isolate one geometry type, modify it, and merge it back without
splitting and handling all other component types.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/get_geometry_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Geometry Components Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Get Geometry Components Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   The input geometry.

Type
   The type of geometry component to extract.

Remove
   Remove the extracted component from the geometry output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/get_geometry_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Geometry Components Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Get Geometry Components Node Outputs
text:
Geometry
   The extracted geometry component.
   If the selected component does not exist, an empty geometry is output.

Components
   The input geometry with the extracted component removed when *Remove* is enabled.
   Otherwise, this is the unchanged input geometry.

Exists
   Whether the input geometry contains the selected component.
   This only checks whether the component exists, not whether it contains any elements.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/get_geometry_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge by Distance Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Merge by Distance Node Merge by Distance Node
text:
The *Merge by Distance* node merges selected mesh vertices or point cloud points within a given distance,
merging surrounding geometry where necessary. This operation is similar to the bpy.ops.mesh.remove_doubles
operator or the weld.

Tip:

   For more control over which elements are merged, the
   Cluster by Distance,
   Cluster by Connected,
   and Merge Points
   nodes can be combined to build custom merge workflows.

   This makes it possible to merge elements based on arbitrary selections,
   groups, or connectivity without relying solely on distance-based merging.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/merge_by_distance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge by Distance Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Merge by Distance Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field that is true for parts of the geometry to be deleted.
   Unselected points will be completely unused for the operation--
   they will not be merged into other points, and no points will merge into them either.

Tip:

      When possible, using the selection input can be a simple way to speed up the node,
      since searching for nearby points is a relatively expensive operation that gets even
      more expensive when more points are involved.

Mode
   Method for choosing which vertices are merged.

   :All: Merge includes all geometry including loose parts.
   :Connected: Merge only includes attached geometry i.e. the modifier will not merge loose parts together.

Distance
   The distance to use for searching for nearby points.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/merge_by_distance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge Points Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Merge Points Node Merge Points Node
text:
The *Merge Points* node merges selected points in a point cloud or mesh.

Points are merged independently for each unique *Merge ID*, allowing
multiple groups of points to be merged in a single operation.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/merge_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge Points Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Merge Points Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field indicating which points participate in the merge.

   Unselected points are unaffected. They are neither merged into other
   points nor can selected points merge into them.

Merge ID
   Integer field defining independent merge groups.

   Points with the same merge ID are merged together. Points with
   different merge IDs are merged separately.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/merge_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Components Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Separate Components Node Separate Components Node
text:
The *Separate Components* node splits a geometry into a separate output
for each type of data in the geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/separate_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Components Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Separate Components Node Outputs
text:
Mesh
   Mesh component of the input geometry.

Curve
   Curve component of the input geometry.

Point Cloud
   Point cloud component of the input geometry.

Volume
   Volume component of the input geometry.

Instances
   Instances component of the input geometry. Even if the instances contain geometry data with
   one of the other types, all instances will be added to this output.
   A realize instances can be added to move the data from
   geometry instances to their corresponding outputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/separate_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Geometry Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Separate Geometry Node Separate Geometry Node
text:
The *Separate Geometry* node produces two geometry outputs. Based on the *Selection* input,
the input geometry is split between the two outputs.

Tip:

   This node can be combined with the compare
   for a more precise control of which parts are separated to a given output geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/separate_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Geometry Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Separate Geometry Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard Geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field used to calculate which output each part of the geometry will go to.
   Parts in the selection will move to the *Selection* output.
   Parts not in the selection will move to the *Inverted* output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/separate_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Geometry Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Separate Geometry Node Properties
text:
Domain
   The domain on which the selection field is evaluated.

   :Point:
      The selection is on the points, control points, and vertices of the geometry.
   :Edge:
      The selection is on the edges of the mesh component. The other components
      are not modified.
   :Faces:
      The selection is on the faces of the mesh component. The other components
      are not modified.
   :Spline:
      The selection is on the splines in the curve component. For each spline, it
      is either entirely in the selection or not at all. The other components are not
      modified.

Note:

      When selecting a domain that doesn't modify all components, the unmodified
      components will appear in both outputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/separate_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Geometry Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Separate Geometry Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   The parts of the geometry in the selection.

Inverted
   The parts of the geometry not in the selection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/separate_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Smooth Geometry Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Smooth Geometry Node Smooth Geometry Node
text:
The *Smooth Geometry* node smooths connected parts of a geometry by averaging the positions
of neighboring elements. It can be used to reduce surface irregularities or create a
softened, more organic appearance without significantly altering the overall shape.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/smooth_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Smooth Geometry Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Smooth Geometry Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   The input geometry to be smoothed.

Selection
   Controls which elements are affected by the smoothing operation.
   Unselected elements remain unchanged.

Iterations
   The number of smoothing steps to perform.
   Higher values result in a stronger smoothing effect.

Weight
   Relative mix weight of neighboring elements.
   Determines how strongly each element is influenced by the positions of its neighbors.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/smooth_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sort Elements Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Sort Elements Node Sort Elements Node
text: The *Sort Elements* node rearranges geometry elements by changing their indices.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/sort_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sort Elements Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Sort Elements Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   The selection of elements to sort, if left blank, all elements are sorted.
   Non-selected elements will keep their current indices.

Group ID
   Elements with the same group ID are sorted together.
   If the connected socket is not a field, this socket has no effect.

Sort Weight
   The sorted values used to do the reordering.
   If the connected socket is not a field, this socket has no effect.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/sort_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sort Elements Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Sort Elements Node Properties
text:
Domain
   The domain on which the selection and group ID fields are evaluated.

   :Point:
      The fields are evaluated on points, control points, and vertices.
   :Edge:
      The fields are evaluated on the edges of the mesh component.
   :Faces:
      The fields are evaluated on the faces of the mesh component.
   :Spline:
      The fields are evaluated on the splines in the curve component.
   :Instance:
      The fields are evaluated on the top-level instances. Realized instances are ignored.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/sort_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split To Instances Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Split To Instances Node Split To Instances Node
text:
Splits a selection of geometry elements (such as faces) into groups,
then turns each group into an instance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/split_to_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split To Instances Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Split To Instances Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field indicating which geometry elements to include.

Group ID
   Integer field indicating which group each element belongs to. Elements with the
   same ID will be moved into the same output instance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/split_to_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split To Instances Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Split To Instances Node Properties
text:
Domain
   The type of geometry to extract and split.
   This is also the domain on which the *Selection* and *Group ID* fields are evaluated.

   :Point:
      Points, spline control points, and vertices.
   :Edge:
      Mesh edges.
   :Face:
      Mesh faces.
   :Spline:
      Curve splines.
   :Instance:
      Top-level instances. Realized instances are ignored.
   :Layer:
      Grease Pencil layers.

Note:

      Geometry that doesn't match the selected domain will be removed.
      For example, if you choose *Edge*, any faces, splines, and instances in the input
      geometry will be lost.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/split_to_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split To Instances Node > Output
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Split To Instances Node Output
text:
Instances
   The instances containing the grouped geometry elements.

Group ID
   Group ID of each instance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/split_to_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split To Instances Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Split To Instances Node Examples
text:
In the example above, we start with a grid of 1000x1000 square faces serving as "pixels."
Then, we group these faces into patches by assigning them a group ID sampled from a Voronoi texture,
and move each resulting instance by a random amount along the Z axis.

Note that, because the texture outputs floating point values between 0 and 1 while the group ID
is an integer, all the values would be rounded to 0 or 1 and we would only get two groups.
To get more variation, we multiply the texture value by 1000.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/split_to_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform Geometry Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Transform Geometry Node Transform Geometry Node
text:
The *Transform Geometry Node* allows you to move, rotate or scale the geometry.
The transformation is applied to the entire geometry, and not per element.
The set position is used for moving
individual points of a geometry. For transforming instances individually, the instance
translate,
rotate, or
scale nodes can be used.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/transform_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform Geometry Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Operations Transform Geometry Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Mode
   How the transformation is specified.

   :Components: Provide separate inputs for location, rotation and scale.
   :Matrix: Use a transformation matrix.

Translation
   Translation of the entire geometry in the local space of the modified object.

Rotation
   Euler rotation in the local space of the modified object.

Scale
   Scale for the geometry in the local space of the modified object.

Transform
   A Transformation Matrix, available when using *Matrix* mode.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/operations/transform_geometry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Active Element Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Active Element Node Active Element Node
text:
The *Active Element* node outputs the index of the Active point, edge, face, or layer.

Note:

   This node can only be used in the Tool context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/active_element.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Active Element Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Active Element Node Outputs
text:
Index
   Index of the active element in the specified domain.

Exists
   True if an active element exists in the mesh, false otherwise
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/active_element.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Geometry Bundle Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Get Geometry Bundle Node Get Geometry Bundle Node
text:
The *Get Geometry Bundle* node extracts the bundle stored on a geometry.

Bundles can store arbitrary data alongside geometry, allowing information to
be passed between node groups, modifiers, and objects without modifying the geometry itself.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/get_geometry_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Geometry Bundle Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Get Geometry Bundle Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Geometry from which to retrieve the bundle.

Remove
   Removes the bundle from the geometry after extracting it.

   This can improve performance by avoiding unnecessary copies when the
   bundle is no longer needed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/get_geometry_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Geometry Bundle Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Get Geometry Bundle Node Outputs
text:
Geometry
   The input geometry.

   If *Remove* is enabled, the output geometry no longer contains the
   extracted bundle.

Bundle
   The bundle stored on the input geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/get_geometry_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: ID Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read ID Node ID Node
text:
The *ID* node gives an integer value indicating the stable random identifier of each element on the point domain,
which is stored in the id attribute.

The node to set this data is the set id node.

Note:

   Unlike other built-in attributes, the id attribute does not always exist.
   In that case, this node will output the index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/id.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Index Node Index Node
text:
The *Index* node gives an integer value indicating the position of each element in the list,
starting at zero. This depends on the internal order of the data in the geometry, which is not
necessarily visible in the 3D Viewport. However, the index value is visible in the left-most column
in the Spreadsheet Editor.

Note:

   Indices in geometry data are often defined by the internals of complex algorithms that create it.
   If no inputs change, indices will be the same when the same node tree is executed multiple times.
   However, they may not be predictable when inputs to nodes that generate geometry or change its
   topology are adjusted. Additionally, updates to algorithms in newer versions of Blender may
   change the order of generated elements.

   To avoid relying on consistent indices, it is recommended to calculate them locally,
   or to avoid operations that change topology when they must be consistent over time.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/input_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Named Attribute Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Named Attribute Node Named Attribute Node
text:
The *Named Attribute* node outputs the data of an attribute based on the
context of where it is connected (the field-context).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/named_attribute.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Named Attribute Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Named Attribute Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The data type used for the retrieved data.
   geometry-nodes-attribute-search can be used to give a basic list of possible
   attribute names and data types. When a value is chosen from the search menu, the data
   type is set to automatically choose the data type from the geometry nodes result.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/named_attribute.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Named Attribute Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Named Attribute Node Outputs
text:
Attribute
   The attribute data stored on the geometry.

Exists
   True if the attribute accessed by the node is present in the connected context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/named_attribute.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Normal Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Normal Node Normal Node
text:
The *Normal* node returns a vector for each evaluated point indicating the
normal direction. The output can depend
on the attribute domain used in the node evaluating the field, but the output
is always a normalized `unit vector <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_vector>`__.

:Face:
   On the face domain, the normal is the "up" direction of the face.

:Mesh Vertices:
   For mesh vertices, the normal is an average of the surrounding face normals.
   If the vertex does not have any connected faces, the output is simply the normalized position
   of that vertex.

:Edge:
   The normal output for each edge is the average of the edge's two vertex normals.

:Face Corner:
   The output for each face corner is the same as the face normal of the corresponding face.

:Curve Control Points:
   The output of this node when used for curve geometry is the evaluated normal of the curve,
   which depends on the twist method. The normal vector is always perpendicular to the direction
   of the curve's path at every point.

Warning:

   For NURBS and Bézier spline curves, keep in mind that the value retrieved from this node is
   the value at every control point, which may not correspond to the visible *evaluated* points.
   For NURBS splines the difference may be even more pronounced and the result may not be as expected.
   A resample curve can be used to create a poly spline,
   where there is a control point for every evaluated point.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/normal.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Normal Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Normal Node Outputs
text:
Normal
   Vector indicating the normal of each geometry element.

True Normal
   For meshes, outputs normals without custom normals attributes taken into
   account.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/normal.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Position Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Position Node Position Node
text:
The *Position* node outputs a vector of each point of the geometry the node is connected to.

The node can work on geometry domains besides points. In that case, the position data will be
automatically interpolated to the new domain. For example, when used as part of the input to
the split edges, the position for each edge
will be the average position of the edge's two vertices.

For instances themselves, the output is the origin of each instance. However, if the node is for
a geometry node that adjusts data inside instances, the position output of this node will be
in the local space of each instance. See the geometry-nodes_instance-processing page
for more details.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/position.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Radius Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Radius Node Radius Node
text:
The *Radius* node outputs the radius value at each point on the evaluated geometry.
For curves, this value is used for things like determining the size of the mesh created in
the Curve to Mesh node.
For point clouds, the value is used for the display size of the point in the viewport.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/radius.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Selection Node Selection Node
text:
The *Selection* node outputs true for geometry that is selected, and false elsewhere.

The corresponding data flow node is the set selection.

Note:

   This node can only be used in the Tool context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Selection Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Read Selection Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   Boolean field set to true for geometry that is selected in edit mode.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/read/selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Principal Components Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Principal Components Node Geometry Principal Components Node
text:
The *Geometry Principal Components* node performs a Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
on a field of positions.

PCA analyzes how the positions are distributed, finding the center of the
data along with the orthogonal axes that best describe its orientation and
shape. The resulting axes are ordered by how much the data varies along each
direction, from greatest to least.

This is useful for determining the dominant orientation of geometry,
aligning objects to point clouds, generating local coordinate systems,
or measuring the extent of a distribution.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Principal Components Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Principal Components Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Geometry containing the points to analyze.

   All geometry component types except volumes are supported.

Position
   Position values used in the analysis.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Principal Components Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Principal Components Node Outputs
text:
Group Center
   Center of the analyzed group.

Rotation
   Rotation whose local axes correspond to the principal axes of the data.

Principal Components
   Variance of the data along each principal axis.

   Larger values indicate greater spread along the corresponding axis.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Principal Components Node > Principal Axes
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Principal Components Node Principal Axes
text:
Longest Axis
   Unit vector corresponding to the direction of greatest variance.

Intermediate Axis
   Unit vector corresponding to the direction of intermediate variance.

   Together with the other axes, it forms a right-handed orthogonal basis.

Shortest Axis
   Unit vector corresponding to the direction of least variance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Proximity Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Proximity Node Geometry Proximity Node
text:
The *Geometry Proximity* node computes the closest location on the target geometry.

Tip:

   The map range is often helpful to use with the distance
   output of this node to create a falloff with a maximum distance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_proximity.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Proximity Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Proximity Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Group ID
   Splits the elements of the input geometry into groups which can be sampled individually.

Sample Position
   The given position to calculate the closest location on the target.

Sample Group ID
   Determines in which group the closest nearest element is detected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_proximity.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Proximity Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Proximity Node Properties
text:
Target Element
   :Faces:
      Calculate the closest point anywhere on the faces of the target's mesh geometry.
   :Edges:
      Calculate the closest point anywhere on the edges of the target's mesh geometry.
   :Points:
      Calculate the closest point or vertex on the target geometry. This mode is usually the fastest.
      This mode works for both point cloud and mesh geometry, the other modes only work for meshes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_proximity.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Proximity Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Proximity Node Outputs
text:
Position
   Closest location on the surface of the target mesh, or the closest point in the target point cloud
   in *Points* mode.

Distance
   Distance (as floating-point value) from the source position to the closest location in the target.

Is Valid
   Whether the sampling was successful. It can fail when the sampled group is empty.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_proximity.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Geometry Proximity Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Geometry Proximity Node Examples
text:
The different modes of the node: faces, edges and points.
In this example the Geometry Nodes modifier is added on the target plane.
Note that the larger plane is subdivided and the smaller plane is not.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/geometry_proximity.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index of Nearest
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Index of Nearest Index of Nearest
text:
The **Index of Nearest** node is a way to find other close elements in the same geometry.
If needed you can use Group ID to determine the group of neighbors to be analyzed together.

This is an alternative to the sample nearest node.
The main difference is that this node does not require a geometry input, because the geometry
from the field context is used.

Tip:

   This is often combined with the evaluate at index or
   the sample index node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/index_of_nearest.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index of Nearest > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Index of Nearest Inputs
text:
Position
   The position for each element to search.
   By default, this is the same as if the position was connected.

Group ID
   ID to group elements together.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/index_of_nearest.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index of Nearest > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Index of Nearest Outputs
text:
Index
   The index
   of the closest element in the same geometry component.

Has Neighbor
   This is true when the group of the element has at least two elements.
   This is only relevant when using *Group ID*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/index_of_nearest.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Raycast Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Raycast Node Raycast Node
text:
The *Raycast* node intersects rays from one geometry onto another. The source geometry is defined by
the context of the node that the *Raycast* node is connected to.
Each ray computes hit points on the target mesh and outputs normals, distances
and any surface attribute specified.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/raycast.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Raycast Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Raycast Node Inputs
text:
Target Geometry
   Geometry that rays are tested against.

Attribute
   An optional field input evaluated on the *Target Geometry* that will be interpolated at the hit points.
   The resulting values are outputted with the *Attribute* output.

Interpolation
   How attributes of the target mesh are mapped to the attribute values on the result geometry.

   :Interpolated:
      Vertex and corner attributes are interpolated smoothly, with a barycentric function.
   :Nearest:
      Choose the value of the closest vertex without interpolating.

Source Position
   The position from where to start each ray. By default, this is the same as
   if the position was connected.

Ray Direction
   Direction of each ray from the starting position.
   The field is evaluated on the geometry from the context of the field evaluation, not the *Target Geometry*.

Ray Length
   Maximum distance a ray can travel before being considered "no hit".
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/raycast.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Raycast Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Raycast Node Outputs
text:
Is Hit
   Boolean output that is true for each ray which has hit the *Target Geometry*.

Hit Position
   The location of the intersection point with the target mesh.

Hit Normal
   The surface Normal vector at the hit location.

Hit Distance
   The distance from the *Source Position* to the *Hit Position*.
   If the ray does not hit, the *Ray Length* is returned.

Attribute
   Interpolated values of the *Attribute* input sampled at the *Hit Position*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/raycast.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Index Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Sample Index Node Sample Index Node
text:
The *Sample Index* node retrieves values from a source geometry at a specific index.

Tip:

   If the *Geometry* used for the input is the same as the geometry from the field context,
   this node is equivalent to the evaluate at index. Using that node
   is usually preferable since avoiding the geometry socket makes the whole setup easier to use in other situations
   and share.

Tip:

   The Point domain is shared by different components (Mesh, Point Cloud, Curve).
   This node simply samples the *Value* from the first non-empty component,
   checked in the order: Mesh, Point Cloud, Curve.
   The separate components can be used to sample directly from a
   specific component.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/sample_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Index Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Sample Index Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   The geometry to retrieve the attribute from.

Value
   A field to evaluate on the source *Geometry*. The values are then retrieved from specific
   indices for the output.

Index
   Which index to use when retrieving the data from the input *Value* field. Any index can be
   connected, resulting in a "shuffling" of the values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/sample_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Index Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Sample Index Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The data type to use for the retrieved values.

Domain
   The attribute domain that the attribute is transferred from, or in other words,
   the domain used to evaluate the *Attribute* input. For example, it is possible to transfer data from the
   faces of one geometry to the points of another.

Clamp
   Clamp the indices to the size of the attribute domain instead of outputting a default value for invalid indices.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/sample_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Nearest Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Sample Nearest Node Sample Nearest Node
text:
The *Sample Nearest* node retrieves the index
of the geometry element in its input geometry that is closest to the input position.

This node is similar to the geometry proximity,
but it outputs the index of the closest element instead of its distance from the current location.

Tip:

  If you want to find nearest to each point in same geometry, its better to use
  the index of nearest node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/sample_nearest.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Nearest Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Sample Nearest Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   The geometry to sample.

Note:

      This node only supports point cloud and mesh inputs.

Sample Position
   The position to start from when finding the closest location on the target geometry.
   By default, this is the same as if the position was connected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/sample_nearest.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Nearest Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Sample Sample Nearest Node Outputs
text:
Index
   The index of the closest geometry element of the
   chosen domain. For the *Face Corner* domain this is defined to be the closest corner on the closest face.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/sample/sample_nearest.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Box Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Box Selection Node Box Selection Node
text:
The *Box Selection* node creates a selection of elements located within a defined 3D box.
It can be used to isolate geometry inside a specific region of space, such as selecting
points, faces, or instances within a bounded area.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/box_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Box Selection Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Box Selection Node Inputs
text:
Center
   The center position of the selection box in 3D space.

Size
   The size of the box in each axis (X, Y, Z).
   Defines the width, height, and depth of the selection region.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/box_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Box Selection Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Box Selection Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   A boolean field indicating which elements fall inside the box volume.
   True for elements inside or intersecting the box; false otherwise.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/box_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Normal Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Normal Selection Node Normal Selection Node
text:
The *Normal Selection* node creates a selection of elements whose normals point
in a specified direction within a given angular threshold.
It is useful for selecting geometry that faces a certain way, such as upward-facing
surfaces, walls, or elements oriented toward a light or camera.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/normal_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Normal Selection Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Normal Selection Node Inputs
text:
Direction
   A vector that defines the reference direction to compare against the element normals.
   The direction should typically be normalized.

Threshold
   The maximum angular difference between the element normal and the given direction
   for the element to be included in the selection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/normal_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Normal Selection Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Normal Selection Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   A boolean field indicating which elements have normals pointing
   within the given angular threshold of the specified direction.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/normal_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sphere Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Sphere Selection Node Sphere Selection Node
text:
The *Sphere Selection* node creates a selection of elements that lie within a defined spherical region.
It can be used to isolate points, faces, or instances inside or near a sphere, making it useful for
localized effects, falloffs, or region-based operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/sphere_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sphere Selection Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Sphere Selection Node Inputs
text:
Center
   The center position of the sphere in 3D space.

Radius
   The radius of the sphere, defining the distance from the center within which elements are selected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/sphere_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sphere Selection Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Selection Sphere Selection Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   A boolean field indicating which elements fall inside or on the surface of the sphere.
   True for elements within the radius; false for those outside.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/selection/sphere_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Geometry Bundle Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Geometry Bundle Node Set Geometry Bundle Node
text:
The *Set Geometry Bundle* node stores a bundle on a geometry.

Bundles can store arbitrary data alongside geometry, allowing information to
be passed between node groups, modifiers, and objects without modifying the geometry itself.

The bundle stored on a geometry can later be retrieved with the
Get Geometry Bundle node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_geometry_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Geometry Bundle Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Geometry Bundle Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Geometry on which to store the bundle.

Bundle
   Bundle to store on the geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_geometry_bundle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Geometry Name Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Geometry Name Node Set Geometry Name Node
text:
The *Set Geometry Name* node stores a custom name on the geometry, overriding the name which
might come from the object info or a
grease pencil to curves.
The name is displayed in the spreadsheet and can helpful for debugging purposes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_geometry_name.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set ID Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set ID Node Set ID Node
text:
The *Set ID* node fills the id attribute on the input geometry. If the attribute does not
exist yet, it will be created with a default value of zero. The ID is also created by
the distribute points on faces, and it is used in
the random value and other nodes if it exists.

The input node for this data is the id.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_id.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set ID Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set ID Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Whether or not to change the value on each point or instance.
   True values mean the value will be changed, false values mean the value will remain the same.

ID
   The value for each element. By default, this input uses
   the index, which is useful
   when stable IDs are desired when deleting a dynamic number of instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_id.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Position Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Position Node Set Position Node
text:
The *Set Position* node controls the location of each point, the same way as controlling
the position attribute.
If the input geometry contains instances, this node will affect the location of the origin of each instance.

The input node for this data is the position.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_position.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Position Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Position Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Whether or not to change the position of each point or instance.
   True values mean the position will be changed, false values mean it will remain the same.

Position
   The new position for selected elements. By default, this is the same as
   if the position was connected,
   meaning the node will do nothing.

Offset
   An optional translation for each point. This is evaluated at the same time as the *Position* input,
   meaning that fields evaluated for it will not reflect the changed position.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_position.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Selection Node Set Selection Node
text:
The *Set Selection* node controls which geometry is selected.

The input node for this data is the selection.

Note:

   This node can only be used in the Tool context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Selection Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Geometry > Write Set Selection Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field for specifying which elements should be selected in the output geometry.
   Elements for which this field evaluates to false are implicitly de-selected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/geometry/write/set_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Gizmos
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Gizmos Gizmos
text:
Gizmos allow changing inputs of Geometry Nodes directly in the 3D viewport.
This is often more intuitive than controlling the inputs in the modifier or node editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/gizmos.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Gizmos > Using Gizmos
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Gizmos Using Gizmos
text:
Node inputs that can be controlled with a gizmo have an additional icon.
The gizmos of that node are shown if it is selected.
Clicking on the icon pins the gizmo, so that it is shown even if the node is not selected.
Modifying the gizmo in the 3D viewport, modifies the value in the socket.

Note:

   Built-in nodes do not have their own gizmos yet.
   It's possible to create node groups that have gizmos though.

Gizmos are often automatically propagated when an input socket with a gizmo is linked.
The gizmo then controls the value that it is propagated to, instead of the input of the node group directly.
Not all nodes support propagating gizmos, but many math operations do.
A double link indicates that the propagation was successful.

Gizmos can also be propagated to Group Inputs, in which case they are also available on the parent group node.
If the current group is used by a modifier directly, the gizmo will also be available on the modifier.
Gizmos that are propagated to the modifier always show when the modifier is active, independent of whether any node
is visible or selected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/gizmos.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Gizmos > Creating Custom Gizmos
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Gizmos Creating Custom Gizmos
text:
Adding custom gizmos to a node group that generates or modifies geometry can make it more convenient to use.

To add a gizmo to a node group, one has to use one of the gizmo nodes.
The main aspect that makes gizmos unintuitive at first is that there is a **bidirectional dependency**:
changing the gizmo position changes the controlled value and vice versa.

The most simple custom gizmo setup is shown below.
The Linear Gizmo node adds a gizmo that is drawn in the 3D viewport.
The gizmo controls the value that is plugged into it.
When trying this, you will notice that the gizmo always jumps back to the origin while the value is still changed.
That is because the Position of the gizmo node does not depend on the value yet.

When the gizmo position is made dependent on the value, the gizmo works more than one would expect.
It now also works in both directions: changing the value moves the gizmo and moving the gizmo changes the value.

Multiple values can be plugged into the Value input of gizmo nodes at once.
In that case, all these values are modified at the same time when moving the gizmo.
Multiply or divide nodes can be used if the values should change at different rates.

The Transform output of gizmo nodes should be joined into the geometry that the gizmo controls.
This helps Blender to understand that the gizmos should be transformed together with the geometry later on.

Note:

   Generally, it is possible to build the entire node group functionality first and to add gizmos afterwards.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/gizmos.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil to Curves Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Operations Grease Pencil to Curves Node Grease Pencil to Curves Node
text:
The *Grease Pencil to Curves* node converts each Grease Pencil layer into an instance
that contains curves.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/operations/grease_pencil_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil to Curves Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Operations Grease Pencil to Curves Node Inputs
text:
Grease Pencil
   Standard Grease Pencil geometry.

Selection
   Selects the layers to convert.

Instances as Layers
   Create a separate curve instance for every layer.

Tip:
      This is equivalent to a Realize Instances
      operation after creating the curve geometry instances. This can simplify some logic later on, but
      typically keeping this operation off will be much better for performance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/operations/grease_pencil_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge Layers Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Operations Merge Layers Node Merge Layers Node
text:
Combines multiple Grease Pencil Layers into a single layer.

Seealso:

   Merge Layers Operator
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/operations/merge_layers.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge Layers Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Operations Merge Layers Node Inputs
text:
Grease Pencil
   The Grease Pencil object with multiple layers to combine.
Selection
   Operate of a subset of layers by setting the field layer index value to *true*.
   By default, all layers are selected.
Mode
   Determines how to choose which layers are merged.

   :By Name: Combine all layers which have the same name.
   :By Group ID: Provide a custom group ID for each layer and all layers with the same ID will be merged into one.
Group ID
   The index numbers of the layer to be merged.
   This input is only visible when using *By Group ID* Mode.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/operations/merge_layers.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil Color Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Read Grease Pencil Color Node Grease Pencil Color Node
text:
The *Grease Pencil Color* node outputs the color attributes of Grease Pencil strokes.
Separate outputs are provided for the stroke points and the stroke fill.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/read/grease_pencil_color.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil Color Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Read Grease Pencil Color Node Outputs
text:
Point
   The color of each point in the stroke.

Fill
   The fill color of the stroke.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/read/grease_pencil_color.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil Draw Time Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Read Grease Pencil Draw Time Node Grease Pencil Draw Time Node
text:
The *Grease Pencil Draw Time* node outputs timing information stored for each point
of a Grease Pencil stroke.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/read/grease_pencil_draw_time.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil Draw Time Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Read Grease Pencil Draw Time Node Outputs
text:
Creation Time
   The time at which the point was created relative to the start of the stroke.

Delta Time
   The time elapsed between the creation of the point and the previous point in the stroke.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/grease_pencil/read/grease_pencil_draw_time.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grease Pencil Fill ID Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Grease Pencil > Read Grease Pencil Fill ID Node Grease Pencil Fill ID Node
text:
The *Grease Pencil Fill ID* node outputs the fill ID of each Grease Pencil stroke.
The fill ID can be used to identify and group strokes based on their fill.
