   The available options are defined by the connected menu socket.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/constant/menu.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Object Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Constant Object Node Object Node
text:
The *Object* input node outputs a single object. It can be connected to other object sockets
to make using the same object in multiple places more convenient.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/constant/object.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Constant String Node String Node
text:
The *String* input node creates a single string. It can be connected to attribute name sockets
to make using the same attribute name in multiple places more convenient.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/constant/string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Vector Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Constant Vector Node Vector Node
text:
The *Vector* node outputs a constant vector value with 2, 3, or 4 components.
This node is commonly used to provide fixed directions, coordinates, or offsets to other nodes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/constant/vector.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Vector Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Constant Vector Node Properties
text:
Dimensions
   The number of components in the vector. Valid values range from 2 to 4.
   Increasing the dimension adds additional components to the vector.

   *This option can only be found in the Sidebar.*

X, Y, Z, W
   The value of each vector component.

   Only the components corresponding to the selected *Dimensions* are shown.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/constant/vector.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Dial Gizmo > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Dial Gizmo Inputs
text:
Value
   Special gizmo value socket.
   Everything that linked into this socket will be modified when the gizmo is rotated.
Position
   Position of the gizmo in the local space of the object.
Up
   Up or normal direction of the gizmo in the viewport.
Screen Space
   If enabled, the gizmo will always have the same size in the viewport independent of the zoom level.
   This affects the meaning of the radius input.
Radius
   In screen space mode, this is a factor on top of the default radius.
   Otherwise, this is the radius of the gizmo in Blender units.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/dial_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Dial Gizmo > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Dial Gizmo Outputs
text:
Transform
   Should be joined into the geometry that is controlled by this gizmo.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/dial_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Linear Gizmo
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Linear Gizmo Linear Gizmo
text:
The *Linear Gizmo* node provides the most widely applicable gizmo. It can e.g. be used to control the height of
something.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/linear_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Linear Gizmo > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Linear Gizmo Inputs
text:
Value
   Special gizmo value socket.
   Everything that linked into this socket will be modified when the gizmo is moved.
Position
   Position of the gizmo in the local space of the object.
Direction
   Specifies the direction in with the gizmo points or is moved.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/linear_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Linear Gizmo > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Linear Gizmo Properties
text:
Color
   Controls which theme color is used for this gizmo.
Draw Style
   Allows choosing between different styles of the gizmo.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/linear_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Linear Gizmo > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Linear Gizmo Outputs
text:
Transform
   Should be joined into the geometry that is controlled by this gizmo.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/linear_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform Gizmo
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Transform Gizmo Transform Gizmo
text: The *Transform Gizmo* node provides a compound gizmo that can control a position, rotation and scale.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/transform_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform Gizmo > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Transform Gizmo Inputs
text:
Value
   Special gizmo value socket.
   Everything that linked into this socket will be modified when the gizmo is modified.
Position
   Position of the gizmo in the local space of the object.
Rotation
   Local orientation of the gizmo.

Note:

   The rotation input is ignored by the 3D viewport if the transform orientation is set to global.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/transform_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform Gizmo > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Transform Gizmo Properties
text:
The node has properties in the sidebar which allow disabling parts of the gizmo.
This can be useful when e.g. controlling only a translation or only a rotation.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/transform_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform Gizmo > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Gizmo Transform Gizmo Outputs
text:
Transform
   Should be joined into the geometry that is controlled by this gizmo.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/gizmo/transform_gizmo.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import CSV Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import CSV Node Import CSV Node
text:
The *Import CSV* node reads data from a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file and generates a point cloud.
The first row (header) must contain unique names for each column. After the first line each row in the
file becomes a point, with numeric columns imported as attributes.

Attribute names are taken from the header row, and types are inferred from the first value in each
column:

- Integer values create integer attributes.
- Float values create float attributes.

Note:

   Only integer and float columns are supported. Other types, such as strings, are ignored.

This node is useful for visualizing external datasets in Geometry Nodes,
such as for scientific visualization or procedural generation based on tabular data.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/csv.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import CSV Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import CSV Node Inputs
text:
Path
   The path to the CSV file. The file must be structured with one row per point and values separated by a delimiter.

Delimiter
   The character used to separate values within each row of the CSV file,
   such as a comma (`,`), semicolon (`;`), or tab character.

Tip:

      Tab characters can be inserted using the special characters.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/csv.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import CSV Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import CSV Node Outputs
text:
Point Cloud
   A point cloud geometry where each row of the CSV file corresponds to a point.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/csv.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import Nodes
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import Nodes Import Nodes
text:
Nodes used to import data from external file formats.

Geometry Nodes supports automatically creating import nodes by dragging supported file types into the node editor.

When dropping a supported file into a Geometry Node tree,
the corresponding import node is added automatically and configured with the file path.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import OBJ Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import OBJ Node Import OBJ Node
text:
The *Import OBJ* node loads geometry data from a `.obj` file and outputs it as instances.

Each object defined in the OBJ file is imported as a separate instance,
which helps to preserve scene structure and optimize performance.
This approach allows for efficient manipulation and reuse of the geometry within Geometry Nodes workflows.

This node is useful for importing static 3D assets created in other modeling software.

Note:

   The node imports only mesh geometry; materials and textures are not imported.

Seealso:

   OBJ Import Operator
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/obj.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import OBJ Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import OBJ Node Outputs
text:
Instances
   A collection of instances representing the objects in the imported file.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/obj.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import PLY Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import PLY Node Import PLY Node
text:
The *Import PLY* node imports geometry from a .ply (Polygon File Format or Stanford Triangle Format) file.

PLY files are commonly used to store geometry from 3D scanning and modeling software.
They can contain mesh data with attributes such as vertex colors and normals,
as well as Gaussian splats used for rendering captured scenes.

The node automatically detects the type of geometry stored in the file,
importing it as either a mesh or a point cloud
containing Gaussian splats.
This allows both types of PLY files to be used in Geometry Nodes without additional setup.

Seealso:

   PLY Import Operator
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/ply.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import PLY Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import PLY Node Outputs
text:
Geometry
   The geometry imported from the PLY file.
   The resulting geometry type depends on the file contents.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/ply.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import SPZ Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import SPZ Node Import SPZ Node
text:
The *Import SPZ* node imports 3D Gaussian Splat data from an SPZ file
and outputs it as point cloud geometry.

SPZ is a compressed file format for storing 3D Gaussian Splats, which represent
a scene using collections of three-dimensional Gaussian distributions.
Each splat contains properties such as position, rotation, scale, opacity, and color.

The imported point cloud can be processed using Geometry Nodes
and rendered using Gaussian Splat rendering.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/spz.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import STL Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import STL Node Import STL Node
text:
The *Import STL* node imports mesh geometry from a `.stl` (Stereolithography) file.

STL files are commonly used for 3D printing and CAD applications and contain only surface geometry,
typically as a collection of triangles with no color, texture, or other attributes.

This node enables incorporating external STL assets into Geometry Nodes for procedural processing or visualization.

Seealso:

   STL Import Operator
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/stl.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import Text Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import Text Node Import Text Node
text:
The *Import Text* node reads the contents of a plain text file and outputs it as a single string.
This can be useful in motion graphics or data-driven workflows where external text needs to be
processed or displayed.

Note:

   Currently, only files with the `.txt` extension are supported.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/txt.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import VDB Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import VDB Node Import VDB Node
text:
The *Import VDB* node loads volumetric data from a `.vdb` file
and outputs it as a Volume geometry.
All grids present in the file are loaded and included in the resulting volume.

This node is useful for importing simulation data or procedural volumes created in external software.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/vdb.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Import VDB Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Import Import VDB Node Outputs
text:
Volume
   A Volume geometry containing all the grids from the specified VDB file.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/import/vdb.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: 3D Cursor Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene 3D Cursor Node 3D Cursor Node
text:
The *3D Cursor* node outputs the position and orientation of the 3D cursor in the scene.

Note:

   This node can only be used in the Tool context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/3d_cursor.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: 3D Cursor Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene 3D Cursor Node Outputs
text:
Location
   The position of the 3D cursor.

Rotation
   The orientation of the 3D cursor as a standard rotation value.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/3d_cursor.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bone Info Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Bone Info Node Bone Info Node
text:
The *Bone Info* node retrieves transform information for a bone from an armature object.

This can be used to drive Geometry Nodes with an armature, create
procedural rigging effects, or implement custom armature deformation using
vertex group attributes.

Note:

   A dependency cycle can occur if the *Bone Info* node uses one bone and another bone in the same armature in turn
   depends on the modified object, for example using a geometry attribute.
   Inside an armature each bone can be referenced individually, but the geometry modifier node can only add a
   dependency on the entire armature. This is because the bone name is a generic string that does not generally point
   to a single bone.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/bone_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bone Info Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Bone Info Node Inputs
text:
Armature
   Armature object to get bone poses from.

Bone Name
   Name of the bone to evaluate.

   If the specified bone does not exist, a warning is displayed unless the
   *Exists* output is used.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/bone_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bone Info Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Bone Info Node Properties
text:
Transform Space
   The space in which pose transforms are defined.

   :Original:
      Output the pose and rest pose relative to the armature object origin.
   :Relative:
      Bring the pose and rest pose into the modified object's space.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/bone_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bone Info Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Bone Info Node Outputs
text:
Pose
   Evaluated final transform of the bone.
Local Pose
   Difference between the pose and rest pose, relative to the parent bone. Not affected by the transform space.
Transform Pose
   Matrix representing the bone's location, rotation, and scale properties. Not affected by the transform space.
Rest Pose
   Original transform of the bone as defined in edit mode.
Rest Length
   Original length of the bone.
Exists
   Whether the specified bone exists in the armature.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/bone_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bone Info Node > Envelope
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Bone Info Node Envelope
text:
The following outputs provide the bone's envelope properties as defined in Edit Mode.
These values can be used to calculate procedural deformation weights or reproduce
envelope-based deformation in Geometry Nodes.

Envelope Distance
   Distance beyond the bone's head and tail radii over which its envelope influence extends.

Radius Head
   Radius of the bone's envelope at its head.

Radius Tail
   Radius of the bone's envelope at its tail.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/bone_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Camera Info Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Camera Info Node Camera Info Node
text:
The *Camera Info* node outputs the information about the selected camera object.

It can be used to customize geometry based on the camera's parameters,
for example when building camera-based visual effects or aligning geometry with the camera view.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/camera_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Camera Info Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Camera Info Node Inputs
text:
Camera
   The camera object to retrieve information from.

   To get the active camera, use the active camera.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/camera_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Camera Info Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Camera Info Node Outputs
text:
Projection Matrix
   A 4x4 matrix that represents the camera's projection transform, combining focal length,
   sensor size, shift, and clipping range. Can be used to project 3D coordinates into screen space.

Focal Length
   The focal length of the camera in millimeters. Affects field of view in perspective cameras.

Sensor
   The physical size of the camera sensor in millimeters, as a 2D vector (X and Y dimensions).
   This value is influenced by the sensor fit properties.

Shift
   Horizontal and vertical shift of the camera view, expressed as a 2D vector.

Clip Start
   The near clipping distance of the camera.

Clip End
   The far clipping distance of the camera.

Focus Distance
   The distance from the camera to the focus point, in Blender units.
   Typically used for depth of field calculations.

Is Orthographic
   A boolean output that is *true* when the camera is in orthographic mode, and *false* when in perspective mode.

Orthographic Scale
   The orthographic scale used when the camera is set to orthographic mode.
   Controls the size of the view area instead of using focal length.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/camera_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Children Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Children Node Collection Children Node
text:
The *Collection Children* node returns the child collections and objects
contained within a collection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_children.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Children Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Children Node Inputs
text:
Collection
   The collection to query.

Recursive
   Include collections and objects contained in nested child collections.

   When disabled, only the direct children of the input collection are returned.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_children.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Children Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Children Node Outputs
text:
Collections
   A list of child collections contained in the input collection.

   When *Recursive* is enabled, all descendant collections are included.

Objects
   A list of objects contained in the input collection.

   When *Recursive* is enabled, objects from all descendant collections are
   included.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_children.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Info Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Info Node Collection Info Node
text:
The *Collection Info* node gets information from collections.
This can be useful to control parameters in the geometry node tree with an external collection.

Tip:

   A *Collection Info* node can be added quickly by dragging a collection into the node editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Info Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Info Node Inputs
text:
Collection
   Collection to get the properties from.

Separate Children
   Output each child of the collection as a separate instance. The list of instances will be sorted
   alphabetically with the objects and child collections sorted together. This can be used with
   the *Pick Instance* option in the instance on points to
   choose between collection children at each point.

Note:

      Because renaming objects and collections does not cause a modifier re-evaluation, an update will
      need to be triggered manually for the node's output to reflect a changed name.

Reset Children
   Remove the transform of each of the collection's children when converting them to instances.
   This is useful in order to keep child objects visually separate in the viewport,
   while keeping every instance located directly at the location of the point it was added for.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Info Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Info Node Properties
text:
Transform Space
   The transformation of the output instances. The instances are transformed, but not the geometry of the
   collection in them.

   :Original:
      Output the instances relative to the collection offset.
   :Relative:
      Join the input collection instances with the modified object as geometry,
      maintaining the relative position between the objects in the scene.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Collection Info Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Collection Info Node Outputs
text:
Instances
   Instances of the collection in world space with all modifiers applied and represented as geometry in instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/collection_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Image Info Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Image Info Node Image Info Node
text:
The *Image Info* node gets information from image and animation.
This can be useful to generate parameters in the geometry node for arbitrary images. Image information can be either
general or frame-specific.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/image_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Image Info Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Image Info Node Inputs
text:
Image
   Source image to get parameters from.

Frame
   Frame index for frame-specific outputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/image_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Image Info Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Image Info Node Outputs
text:
Width
   The number of pixels along the X axis. Specific to each frame.

Height
   The number of pixels along the Y axis. Specific to each frame.

Has Alpha
   Whether the transparency channel be different from 1 for the pixels of this image frame. Specific to each frame.

Frame Count
   The number of frames in an image or video frame sequence. For a static image, always 1.

FPS
   The number of frames per second. For static image is always 0.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/image_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Is Viewport Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Is Viewport Node Is Viewport Node
text:
The *Is Viewport* node outputs whether the node tree is being evaluated for an
interactive viewport rather than for a final render.

This can be used to switch between different parts of a node tree depending on
the evaluation context. For example, computationally expensive operations can
be replaced with simpler alternatives while working interactively, while the
full-quality result is used for the final render.

In Geometry Nodes, the output is true when the node tree is evaluated for the
3D Viewport. In the Compositor, it is true when evaluated by the
Viewport Compositor.
For a final render, the output is false.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/is_viewport.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Is Viewport Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Is Viewport Node Outputs
text:
Is Viewport
   Boolean value indicating whether the node tree is being evaluated for an
   interactive viewport.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/is_viewport.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mouse Position Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Mouse Position Node Mouse Position Node
text:
The *Mouse Position* node returns information about the mouse cursor
such as its position and the region's dimensions.

Tip:

   When using this node, enable Wait for Click.
   to wait for a mouse click input (LMB) before running the operator from a menu.

Note:

   This node can only be used in the Tool context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/mouse_position.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mouse Position Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Mouse Position Node Outputs
text:
Mouse X
   The region-space mouse X location, in pixels, increasing from 0 at the left.
Mouse Y
   The region-space mouse Y location, in pixels, increasing from 0 at the bottom.
Region Width
   The total X size of the region in pixels.
Region Height
   The total Y size of the region in pixels.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/mouse_position.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Object Info Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Object Info Node Object Info Node
text:
The *Object Info* node gets information from objects.
This can be useful to control parameters in the geometry node tree with an external object,
either directly by using its geometry, or via its transformation properties.

An *Object Info* node can be added quickly by dragging an object into the node editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/object_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Object Info Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Object Info Node Inputs
text:
Object
   Object to get the properties from.

As Instance
   Output the entire object as single instance instead of realized geometry.
   This allows instancing non-geometry object types, because the output will contain an instance of the object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/object_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Object Info Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Object Info Node Properties
text:
Transform Space
   The transformation of the vector and geometry outputs.

   :Original:
      Output the geometry relative to the input object transform, and the location,
      rotation and scale relative to the world origin.
   :Relative:
      Bring the input object geometry, location, rotation and scale into the modified object,
      maintaining the relative position between the two objects in the scene.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/object_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Object Info Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Object Info Node Outputs
text:
Transform
   Transformation Matrix containing the location, rotation and scale of the object.
Location
   Location of the object in world space.
Rotation
   Rotation of the object in world space.
Scale
   Scale of the object in world space.
Geometry
   Geometry of the object in world space with all its modifiers applied.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/object_info.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Scene Time Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Scene Time Node Scene Time Node
text: The *Scene Time* node outputs the current time in the scene's animation in units of seconds or frames.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/scene_time.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Scene Time Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Scene Time Node Outputs
text:
Seconds
   Current scene time in seconds.

Frames
   Current scene frame.
   As an input in geometry nodes, this output may also output non-round numbers,
   in order to support higher quality motion blur.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/scene_time.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Self Object Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Self Object Node Self Object Node
text:
The *Self Object* node outputs the object that contains the geometry nodes modifier
currently being executed. This can be used to retrieve the original transforms.

When evaluated in the Tool context, this node returns the Active object.

Note:

   The geometry cannot be retrieved from this object with the
   object info, since its final geometry is still
   being evaluated.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/self_object.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Viewport Transform Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Viewport Transform Node Viewport Transform Node
text:
The *Viewport Transform* node retrieves the view direction and location of the index.

Note:

   This node can only be used in the Tool context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/viewport_transform.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Viewport Transform Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Input > Scene Viewport Transform Node Outputs
text:
Projection
   The 3D Viewport's perspective or orthographic projection matrix.
View
   The view direction and location of the 3D viewport.
Is Orthographic
   Whether the viewport is using orthographic projection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/input/scene/viewport_transform.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Inspection
text:
Inspecting intermediate values in a geometry node tree is useful while
building/understanding one or when trying to figure out why something is not working.
Blender provides multiple tools to understand how a node tree is working
or why it is not working.

Note:

   Generally, the inspection tools display data from the last time the node tree has been evaluated.
   If it has not been evaluated, no information is available.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Socket Inspection
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Socket Inspection
text:
Socket inspection shows information about the value in a socket during the last evaluation.
For primitive data types such as integers, vectors, and strings the actual value is shown.
For geometry sockets only some data about the geometry is stored, including the set of
data types the geometry contains, and a count of their elements.

Socket values are only logged from when the node tree was executed, so a node must be
connected to the *Group Output* to have a value for inspection. Values are not logged during
rendering, to improve performance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Attribute Search
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Attribute Search
text:
The attribute search is shown when clicking on an attribute input in the modifier.
It contains a list of all the attributes that were available at that point in
the modifier or node execution.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Viewer Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Viewer Node
text:
The Viewer node is used to display intermediate geometry in the Spreadsheet Editor
and the Viewport. For more information see viewer.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Node Warnings
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Node Warnings
text:
When the inputs to a node are invalid, it displays a warning in the title.
Hovering over the warning icon shows the error message. These warnings are only
generated when the node is executed, so a node must be connected to the *Group Output*
to have a warning.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Node Timings Overlay
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Node Timings Overlay
text:
Node timings show how long a node took to execute the last time the node group was evaluated.
They can be turned on in the overlays popover on the top right of the node editor.
When a node group is used in multiple places, the timings depend on the context of
the node editor, which is displayed in the path on the top left.

Frame nodes display the total time from all of the contained nodes
and the *Group Output* node displays the total time for the entire node group.

The displayed timings should only be considered an approximation, since they can
also take into account actions like copying or deleting a geometry input that aren't
part of the node's operation. Also, when a node uses multiple CPU cores, the evaluation
system might work on other nodes at the same time. It's also important to remember
that field nodes generally don't do work by themselves,
so their execution time is only added to the data-flow nodes they are connected to.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Named Attributes Overlay
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Named Attributes Overlay
text:
The "Named Attributes" overlay allows displaying when a custom named attribute is used
by a node or a node group. Named attributes can be used by the
capture attribute, the
named attribute, and the
remove named attribute,
and can be written to, read, or removed.

Using named attributes (as opposed to anonymous-attributes) can be problematic
when the original geometry already has attributes with the specified names. In that case
a geometry node group might mistakenly overwrite some essential data. The overlay helps
to make detecting that situation easy.

The same data is also available in the modifiers-geometry-nodes-named-attributes panel
in the modifier's UI.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Inspection > Geometry Randomization
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Inspection Geometry Randomization
text:
Many nodes don't guarantee the order of elements in which they output things. For example, the order of edges coming
out of the **Triangulate** node is deterministic but not well defined. The order may change between Blender versions.
Therefore, if node setups depend on a specific order, they may break when the Blender implementation changes. Changing
the order can often be necessary in order to fix bugs or improve performance.

"Geometry randomization" can be temporarily enabled to see if a blend-file depends on the indices in unstable ways.
When enabled, various internal algorithms shuffle the result geometry elements so that any dependence on it would not
work anymore. When building setups that are supposed to last a long time, it is recommended to check if they still
work with randomization enabled.

To enable it, first enable **Developer Extras** in the preferences.
Then search for **Set Geometry Randomization**.
The popup allows enabling and disabling the randomization.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/inspection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Bounds Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Bounds Node Instance Bounds Node
text:
The *Instance Bounds* node outputs the axis-aligned bounding box of each instance in the input geometry.
This can be used to determine the spatial extent of instances,
for example, to position or scale objects based on their size.

Note:

   Only top-level instances are considered; the bounds do not include nested instances inside the instance geometry.
   This avoids the performance cost of realizing nested instances for accurate bounds.

   See geometry-nodes_nested-instancing for more information.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_bounds.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Bounds Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Bounds Node Inputs
text:
Use Radius
   For curves, point clouds, and Grease Pencil geometries,
   take the radius attribute into account when computing the bounds.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_bounds.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Bounds Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Bounds Node Outputs
text:
Min
   The minimum corner of the bounding box for each instance, in local space.

Max
   The maximum corner of the bounding box for each instance, in local space.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_bounds.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Elements Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Elements Node Instance on Elements Node
text:
The *Instance on Elements* node creates instances of an object, collection, or geometry
on selected elements of an input geometry.
It can be used to distribute instances on points, edges, faces, or face corners,
providing flexibility for procedural instancing workflows.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Elements Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Elements Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   The geometry on which to create instances.

Instance On
   The geometry element type to instance on.

   :Points: Instances are created at the location of each point.
   :Edges: Instances are placed along edges.
   :Faces: Instances are placed on the surface of each face.
   :Corners: Instances are created at each face corner (vertex per face).

Mask
   A selection controlling which elements are used for instancing.
   Floating-point values between 0 and 1 are treated as probabilistic selections,
   resulting in a random subset of elements being used.

Input Type
   Defines how the instance geometry input is provided.

   :Data-Block: Instances are created from an object or collection data-block.
   :Geometry: Instances are created from input geometry provided to the node.

Instance Type Data-Block
   When using *Data-Block* input, determines whether to instance an *Object* or a *Collection*.

Object / Collection Data-Block
   The specific object or collection to instance when using *Data-Block* input mode.

Instance Geometry
   The geometry to instance when using *Geometry* input mode.

Realize Instances
   Converts all instances into real geometry, producing a single combined geometry output.
   This can be required for some subsequent geometry operations or modifiers.

Keep Surface
   Keeps the underlying surface used for instancing, rather than outputting only the instances.

Seed
   Random seed value used to vary random selections or random instance indexing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Elements Node > Pick Instance :guilabel:`Data-Block` :guilabel:`Collection`
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Elements Node Pick Instance :guilabel:`Data-Block` :guilabel:`Collection`
text:
When instancing from a collection, this option enables random or controlled selection
of which child object to instance per element.

Instance Index
   Determines how a child instance is chosen from the collection.

   :Random:
      Picks a random object from the collection for each element.
   :Sequence:
      Cycles through objects in collection order.
   :Input:
      Uses the value from the *Instance Index* input socket.

Instance Index Input
   Specifies the index of the object in the collection to be instanced,
   used when the *Instance Index* method is set to *Input*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Elements Node > Transform
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Elements Node Transform
text:
Surface Offset
   Moves instances along the element normal, offsetting them from the surface.

Align Rotation
   Aligns instance rotation to the orientation of the geometry element (e.g., normal direction).

Scale
   Controls the uniform or per-axis scaling of instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Elements Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Elements Node Outputs
text:
Geometry
   The resulting geometry containing all instances created on the selected elements.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Points Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Points Node Instance on Points Node
text:
The *Instance on Points* node adds a reference to a geometry to each of the points present
in the input geometry. Instances are a fast way to add the same geometry to a scene many times
without duplicating the underlying data. The node works on any geometry type
with a *Point* domain, including meshes, point clouds, and curve control points.

Any attributes on the points from the *Geometry* input will be available on the instance
domain of the generated instances.

Tip:

   The bpy.ops.object.duplicates_make_real operator can be used to create objects
   from instances generated with this node.

Note:

   To instance object types that do not contain geometry, like a light object, the
   object info can be used. Other objects like
   Metaball objects are not supported for instancing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Points Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Points Node Inputs
text:
Points
   Standard geometry input. The position of the points of this geometry affect the transforms of
   each instance output.

Note:

      If the input geometry contains instances, the node will create more instances on
      the points inside the instances, creating nested instancing.
      In this case, each new instance will have the transform created by the node from the *Rotation*
      and *Scale* inputs, but it will *also* be transformed based on the parent instances.

Selection
   Whether to instance on each point. True values mean an instance will be generated on the point,
   false values mean the point will be skipped.

Instance
   The geometry to instance on each selected point. This can contain real geometry, or multiple instances,
   which can be useful when combined with the *Pick Instance* option.

Pick Instances
   If enabled, instead of adding the entire geometry from the *Instance* input on every point,
   choose an instance from the instance list of the geometry based on the *Instance Index* input.
   This option is intended to be used with the collection info.

Instance Index
   The selection of index for every selected point, only used when *Pick Instances* is true.
   By default the point ID is used,
   or the index if that doesn't exist.
   Negative values or values that are too large are wrapped around to the other end of
   the instance list.

Rotation
   The Euler rotation for every instance. This can use the rotation output of nodes like
   Distribute Points on Faces
   and Curve to Points. An Euler rotation
   can also be created from a direction vector like the normal
   with the align rotation to vector.

Scale
   The size of each generated instance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance on Points Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance on Points Node Outputs
text:
Instances
   Standard geometry output. If the id attribute exists on the input geometry,
   it will be copied to the result instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_on_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Reference Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Reference Node Instance Reference Node
text:
The *Instance Reference* node outputs the reference_index attribute as an integer field.

Each unique instanced geometry source is assigned a reference index.
Instances that originate from the same geometry or object share the same value,
allowing them to be grouped, compared, or processed together.

This is useful for identifying instances with shared geometry sets,
creating variation per referenced asset, or selecting instances based on
their original source geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_reference.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Reference Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Reference Node Outputs
text:
Reference Index
   Integer field representing the reference index of each instance source.

   Instances sharing the same referenced geometry output the same value.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_reference.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Rotation Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Rotation Node Instance Rotation Node
text:
The *Instance Rotation* outputs the XYZ Euler rotation of each top-level instance in the
local space of the modifier object.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.

Note:

   Though rotations are often displayed in units of degrees in the spreadsheet or node editor,
   they are stored internally in radians, so this node outputs radians.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_rotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Rotation Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Rotation Node Outputs
text:
Rotation
   Vector that indicates the rotation of each top-level instance in radians.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_rotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Scale Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Scale Node Instance Scale Node
text:
The *Instance Scale* outputs the size of top-level instances on each axis in the
local space of the modifier object.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_scale.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Transform Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Transform Node Instance Transform Node
text:
The *Instance Transform* outputs the Transformation Matrix of each top-level instance in the
local space of the modifier object.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_transform.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instance Transform Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instance Transform Node Outputs
text:
Transformation
   Matrix that indicates the Transformation of each top-level instance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instance_transform.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instances to Points Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instances to Points Node Instances to Points Node
text:
The *Instances to Points* node generates points at the origins of top-level instances.
Attributes on the instance domain are moved to the point cloud points.

Note:

   Top-level instances are those that are owned by the node's input geometry.
   Instances owned by other instances, i.e. nested instances, are not considered
   by this node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instances_to_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instances to Points Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Instances to Points Node Inputs
text:
Instances
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   The instances used to generate points. True values mean a point is created for the instance,
   false values mean the instance is skipped.

Position
   Overrides the default position of generated point.

Radius
   Controls the radius of the result points.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/instances_to_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Randomize Transforms Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Randomize Transforms Node Randomize Transforms Node
text:
The *Randomize Transforms* node applies random translation, rotation, and scale to instances.
It is commonly used to create natural variation among duplicated objects, such as scattered
rocks, trees, or other elements in a scene.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/randomize_transforms.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Randomize Transforms Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Randomize Transforms Node Inputs
text:
Instances
   The input geometry containing the instances to be randomized.

Selection
   Controls which instances are affected by the randomization.
   Only selected instances will receive random transformations.

Local Space
   - When enabled, transformations are applied in each instance's local coordinate space.
   - When disabled, randomization is performed in the global coordinate space.

Offset
   The maximum translation offset for each axis. Defines the random range for instance movement.

Rotation
   The maximum rotation for each axis. Defines how much each instance can be rotated.

Scale Axes
   Determines how scaling is applied.

   :Uniform:
      Applies a single random scale factor uniformly to all axes.
   :Axes:
      Applies an independent random scale factor to each axis.

Scale
   The maximum scaling factor applied to each instance.

Flipping
   Randomly flips instances along one or more axes, effectively mirroring them.

Seed
   An integer value that initializes the random number generator.
   Changing the seed produces a different random arrangement while keeping the same parameters.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/randomize_transforms.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Randomize Transforms Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Randomize Transforms Node Outputs
text:
Instances
   The resulting geometry with randomized instance transforms applied.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/randomize_transforms.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Realize Instances Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Realize Instances Node Realize Instances Node
text:
The *Realize Instances* node makes any instances (efficient duplicates of the same geometry)
into real geometry data. This makes it possible to affect each instance individually,
whereas without this node, the exact same changes are applied to every instance of
the same geometry. However, performance can become much worse when the input
contains many instances of complex geometry, which is a fundamental limitation
when procedurally processing geometry.

Note:

   If the input contains multiple volume instances, only the first volume component is moved to the output.

.. editors note: keep up to date with join geometry
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/realize_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Realize Instances Node > Attributes
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Realize Instances Node Attributes
text:
When merging attributes from multiple geometry inputs, the highest complexity data type is chosen
for the output attribute. For example, if a weight attribute is a Boolean on one geometry input
and a vector on another, the weight attribute on the output geometry will use the vector data type.

Named and anonymous attributes are propagated from the instance domain
to the realized geometry. If an attribute exists both on the base geometry and on an instance,
the attribute values from the base geometry take precedence.

Note:

   - The id attribute receives special handling to prevent duplicate values. id values or indices
     of each instance are combined with id values from the geometry data points.
   - Vertex groups are preserved when realizing instances or joining geometries.
     If the domain and type propagation rules above result with the vertex domain and float type,
     then an attribute will be a vertex group on the output mesh.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/realize_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Realize Instances Node > Indices of Instanced Geometries
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Realize Instances Node Indices of Instanced Geometries
text:
When merging multiple geometry inputs that contain instances of geometries, The indices of the instanced
geometries may be reordered when merging. This means that while the order of the indices of the instances
are guaranteed to be the same as before merging, the order of the indices of the geometries that are
being instanced may be different than before merging.

The same behavior applies to material indices.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/realize_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Realize Instances Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Realize Instances Node Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Standard geometry input.
Selection
   Which top-level instances to realize.
Realize All
   Realize all levels of nested instances for each top-level instances
   (overrides the value of the *Depth* input).
Depth
   Number of levels of nested instances to realize for each top-level instance.
Preserve Normals
   Preserve the apparent face orientation of mirrored mesh instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/realize_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Rotate Instances Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Rotate Instances Node Rotate Instances Node
text:
The *Rotate Instances* node rotates geometry instances in local or global space.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/rotate_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Rotate Instances Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Rotate Instances Node Inputs
text:
Instances
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field used to determine if an instance will be rotated.

Rotation
   The Euler rotation to rotate the instances by.

Pivot Point
   The position around which each instance is rotated. If the *Local Space* input is true,
   the location is relative to the initial transform of the instance.

Local Space
   If enabled, the instances are rotated in local space. In other words,
   they are rotated around the axes described by the initial transform of each instance.
   When the input is disabled, the pivot point and rotation are specified in
   the local space of the modifier object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/rotate_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Scale Instances Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Scale Instances Node Scale Instances Node
text:
The *Scale Instances* node scales geometry instances in local or global space.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/scale_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Scale Instances Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Scale Instances Node Inputs
text:
Instances
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field used to determine if an instance will be scaled.

Scale
   The scale factor to apply to the instance's transform on each axis.

Center
   The position from which the instance origins are scaled. Each instance will move away from this location.
   When the *Local Space* input is enabled, this location is relative to the initial transform
   of each instance.

Local Space
   If enabled, the instances are scaled in local space. In other words,
   they are scaled in the directions the described by the initial transform of each instance.
   When the input is disabled, the *Center* and *Scale* inputs are specified in
   the local space of the modifier object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/scale_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Instance Transform Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Set Instance Transform Node Set Instance Transform Node
text:
The *Set Instance Transform* node Transforms geometry instances
using a Transformation Matrix.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/set_instance_transform.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Instance Transform Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Set Instance Transform Node Inputs
text:
Instances
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field used to determine if an instance will be rotated.

Transform
   The transformation matrix to translate, rotate, and scale individual instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/set_instance_transform.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Translate Instances Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Translate Instances Node Translate Instances Node
text:
The *Translate Instances* node moves top-level geometry instances in local or global space.

The instances page contains more information about geometry instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/translate_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Translate Instances Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Instances Translate Instances Node Inputs
text:
Instances
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   Boolean field used to determine if an instance will be translated.

Translation
   The vector to translate the instances by.

Local Space
   If enabled, the instances are translated relative to their initial rotation.
   Otherwise they are translated in the local space of the modifier object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances/translate_instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instances
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Instances Instances
text:
In addition to storing real data like a mesh or a curve, objects can store instances,
which themselves can reference more geometry, an object, or a collection. The purpose
of instancing is to allow duplicating geometry and storing it in an object, without duplicating
the actual data. This optimization allows render engines like Cycles
to handle the same geometry data in many different locations better than when the data is duplicated.

Each instance keeps track of which geometry it corresponds to
and how the instance is transformed compared to it's source geometry.
Instances can also store the id attribute,
which is used to correct motion blur when instances move in an animation.

Instances can be created with geometry nodes using the instance on points.

Warning:

   Currently instancing from geometry nodes cannot be mixed with instancing from the
   index panel in the property editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instances > Nested Instancing
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Instances Nested Instancing
text:
Since instances can store a geometry, and a geometry can contain instances, nested instancing is possible.
In other words, it is possible to instance an instance, or even a collection of instances.
For example, by default, the instance on points will create
nested instances by instancing instances on the points of real geometry.

Here, nested instancing is used to distribute geometry that contains both a mesh
and instances. The output geometry contains a "real" mesh and a group of instances.
Each instance contains a sphere mesh and many instances of a cone geometry.

What makes this method helpful is the output geometry only contains three unique meshes:
the plane, the sphere, and the cone. This would make the performance much better if the meshes
were more complicated.

Warning:

   Only eight levels of nested instancing are supported for rendering and viewing in the viewport.
   Though deeper trees of instances can be made inside geometry nodes, they must be realized at the
   end of the node tree.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instances > Realizing Instances
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Instances Realizing Instances
text:
The term "realizing" instances refers to converting the instances into unique geometry.
When instances are realized they will take up more memory and manipulation to geometry
will have to be processed individually rather than once per instancing geometry.

To realize instance use the realize instances.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Instances > Instance Processing
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes Instances Instance Processing
text:
Almost all nodes that process geometry do so by processing each unique
geometry separately rather than realized geometry. For example,
if a subdivision surface was placed at
the end of the example above, it would only have to subdivide three meshes,
rather than each instance of a mesh. Another important example is processing with
the output of the string to curves,
where each unique character only has to be processed once.

This method can improve performance a lot, but it means that the result of an operation
will be the same for every instance of a certain geometry. In order to have unique results
for every instance, the realize instances
node can be used.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/instances.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Dual Mesh Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Dual Mesh Node Dual Mesh Node
text:
The *Dual Mesh Node* converts a mesh into its dual, i.e. faces are turned into
vertices and vertices are turned into faces. This also means that attributes
which were on the face domain are transferred to the point domain in the dual mesh.

Warning:

   The Dual Mesh node only works on manifold geometry. To work with non-manifold geometry
   it's best to remesh the geometry first.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/dual_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Dual Mesh Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Dual Mesh Node Inputs
text:
Mesh
   Standard geometry input.

Keep Boundaries
   Keeps the non-manifold boundaries of the input mesh in place, by creating
   extra geometry, and avoiding the dual mesh transformation there.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/dual_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Dual Mesh Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Dual Mesh Node Examples
text:
The *Dual Mesh Node* combines nicely with triangulated meshes. In this case
an Ico Sphere is used, which is made up of nice and evenly spaced triangles.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/dual_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Edge Paths to Curves Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Edge Paths to Curves Node Edge Paths to Curves Node
text:
The *Edge Paths to Curves* node output curves that follow paths across mesh edges.

Seealso:

   This node is meant to use the output of the shortest edge paths.
   It is similar to the edge paths to selection, but it creates
   a curve that follow each path, rather than a selection of every visited edge.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/edge_paths_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Edge Paths to Curves Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Edge Paths to Curves Node Inputs
text:
Mesh
   Standard mesh input.

Start Vertices
   A selection of the vertices to start at when traveling along the next vertex indices.

Next Vertex Index
   Describes the path to follow at every vertex.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/edge_paths_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Edge Paths to Selection Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Edge Paths to Selection Node Edge Paths to Selection Node
text:
The *Edge Paths to Selection* node follows paths across mesh edges and outputs a selection
of every visited edge.

Seealso:

   This node is meant to use the output of the shortest edge paths.
   It can be combined with the separate geometry to remove
   any unused edges.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/edge_paths_to_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Edge Paths to Selection Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Edge Paths to Selection Node Inputs
text:
Start Vertices
   A selection of the vertices to start at when traveling along the next vertex indices.

Next Vertex Index
   Describes the path to follow at every vertex.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/edge_paths_to_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Edge Paths to Selection Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Edge Paths to Selection Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   A boolean field indicating all edges visited when traversing the mesh.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/edge_paths_to_selection.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Extrude Mesh Node
text:
The *Extrude Mesh Node* generates new edges or faces on the selected geometry elements
and moves them by a certain offset.

The operations are similar to the extrude tools
in mesh edit mode, though there are some differences. Most importantly, the node never keeps the back-faces
of the extrusion in place, they are always removed. Attribute propagation rules may also be different.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/extrude_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Inputs
text:
Mesh
   Standard geometry input.

Selection
   A boolean field indicating which elements should be extruded.

Offset
   The translation vector for each extruded element. By default, this is the element's
   normal.

Tip:

      If all the elements are extruded in the same direction, you may be able to improve performance
      by connecting a vector to this input,
      thereby skipping the normal calculation.

Offset Scale
   Scaling factor for the above translation vector.

Individual Face Mode Only
   Whether to extrude each face individually rather than extruding connected groups of faces together.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/extrude_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Properties
text:
Mode
   :Vertices:
      Attaches a new freestanding edge to each selected vertex.

   :Edges:
      Attaches a new quad face to each selected edges. Vertices shared by the
      original selected edges are also shared in the duplicated edges.

Note:

         Depending on the situation, the normals of the new faces may be arbitrary. If the selected
         edges each have only one connected face, then the node can pick a consistent orientation for the
         new faces, but if there is more than one connected face, or no connected faces, the normals
         may have to be adjusted afterwards.

   :Faces:
      Extrudes contiguous regions of selected faces, or each selected face individually,
      depending on the *Individual* boolean input.

      When the *Individual* input is false, the node will find regions of connected faces and generate
      new "side" faces on the boundaries of those regions. Any vertices, edges or faces on the *inside*
      of the regions simply are moved, not duplicated. If the whole mesh is selected and it is already
      a Manifold shape, then the result will just be that the whole mesh gets resized.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/extrude_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node > Output
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Output
text:
Mesh
   Standard geometry output.

Top
   A boolean field indicating the "top" elements in the extrusion. In *Vertex* mode, these are the new vertices;
   in *Edge* mode, the new edges; and in *Face* mode, the moved faces.

Side
   A boolean field indicating the "side" elements in the extrusion. In *Vertex* mode, these are the new edges;
   in *Edge* mode, the new faces; and in *Face* mode, too, the newly generated faces (as opposed to the moved ones).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/extrude_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Examples
text:
Here, the selection outputs are used to set materials on certain faces of the mesh.
A random value is used to limit the
extrusion to a random set of faces.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/extrude_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node > Attribute Propagation
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Attribute Propagation
text:
Attributes are transferred to the new elements with specific rules.
An attribute will never change domains on the resulting mesh.
The id attribute does not have any special handling.

Generally boolean attributes are propagated with "or", meaning any connected
"true" value that is mixed in for other types will cause the new value
to be "true" as well.

The following sections describe:
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/mesh/operations/extrude_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude Mesh Node > Vertex Mode
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Mesh > Operations Extrude Mesh Node Vertex Mode
text:
- New **vertices** have copied values from their original vertices.
