source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/accumulate_field.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Accumulate Field Node > Stacking Boxes
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Accumulate Field Node Stacking Boxes
text:
Here, the node is used in combination with the random value
to create a stack of randomly scaled boxes. The *Group Index* input is not used, because all boxes
are meant to be in the same stack.

A slightly more complicated version of the previous example,
using the *Group Index* input to create three separate stacks.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/accumulate_field.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cluster by Distance Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Cluster by Distance Node Cluster by Distance Node
text:
The *Cluster by Distance* node assigns cluster IDs to elements based on the
proximity of their positions.

Elements within the specified distance of one another are assigned the same
cluster ID. Separate *Group ID* values define independent sets of clusters.

For clustering based on mesh connectivity instead of spatial proximity, see
the Cluster by Connected node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/cluster_by_distance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cluster by Distance Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Cluster by Distance Node Inputs
text:
Selection
   Boolean field indicating which elements participate in the clustering.

   Unselected elements are ignored and do not contribute to any cluster.

Group ID
   Integer field defining independent clustering groups.

   Elements with different group IDs are clustered separately, even if they
   are within the specified distance.

Position
   Position of each element used to measure distances.

Distance
   Maximum distance between elements for them to belong to the same cluster.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/cluster_by_distance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cluster by Distance Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Cluster by Distance Node Outputs
text:
Cluster ID
   Integer field identifying the cluster assigned to each selected element.

   Elements with the same cluster ID belong to the same proximity-based cluster.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/cluster_by_distance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Evaluate at Index Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Evaluate at Index Node Evaluate at Index Node
text:
The *Evaluate at Index* node allows accessing data of other elements in the context geometry.
It is similar to the sample index.
The main difference is that this node does not require a geometry input, because the geometry
from the field context is used.

This node is also similar to the evaluate on domain node,
except that the value to retrieve from the specified domain is specified by an index rather than
an automatic domain interpolation.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/evaluate_at_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Evaluate at Index Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Evaluate at Index Node Inputs
text:
Index
   The index of the element in the selected domain
   to retrieve data from, i.e. "the fourth face", or "the first control point".

Value
   The field to retrieve data from.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/evaluate_at_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Evaluate at Index Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Evaluate at Index Node Properties
text:
Domain
   The attribute domain used for evaluation of the *Value* input.
   This is useful because it can be a different domain than the domain from the
   field context, i.e. to choose a vertex for each face.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/evaluate_at_index.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Evaluate on Domain Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Evaluate on Domain Node Evaluate on Domain Node
text:
The *Evaluate on Domain* allows evaluating a field for a different attribute domain
than the domain from the field context. For example, the face index could be used instead
of the face corner index, when setting the values of a UV Map

Note:

   This node is not necessary to retrieve data from other attribute domains; that is done automatically.
   Its utility comes from the fact that it's possible to control *when* the domain interpolation happens.
   Normally, input nodes interpolate their data to the current context's domain as soon as they create
   their output.

Tip:

   It may be preferable to use this node over the capture attribute,
   since it allows using a specific attribute domain without requiring a geometry socket input,
   which allows creating more reusable node groups.

Seealso:

   The method of retrieving data from another domain is somewhat similar to the
   evaluate at index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/evaluate_on_domain.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Evaluate on Domain Node > Output
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Evaluate on Domain Node Output
text:
Value
   The values from the input, evaluated on the chosen domain, then interpolated to the domain from
   the field context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/evaluate_on_domain.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Average Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Average Node Inputs
text:
Value
   The values the mean and median will be calculated from.

Group ID
   An index used to group values together for multiple separate averages.
   This can be thought of as a choice of the "bin" in which to place each value.
   This input has no effect when it is only a single value.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_average.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Average Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Average Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   :Float: The node will average a *Float* field.
   :Vector: The node will average a *Vector* field.

Domain
   The attribute domain used for evaluate the *Value* input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_average.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Average Node > Output
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Average Node Output
text:
Mean
   The sum of all values in each group divided by the size of said group.

Median
   The middle value in each group when all values are sorted from lowest to highest.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_average.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Min & Max Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Min & Max Node Inputs
text:
Value
   The values the minimum and maximum will be calculated from

Group ID
   An index used to group values together for multiple separate averages.
   This can be thought of as a choice of the "bin" in which to place each value.
   This input has no effect when it is only a single value.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_min_max.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Min & Max Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Min & Max Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   :Float: The node will average a *Float* field.
   :Integer: The node will accumulate an *Integer* field.
   :Vector: The node will average a *Vector* field.

Domain
   The attribute domain used for evaluate the *Value* input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_min_max.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Variance Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Variance Node Field Variance Node
text:
The *Field Variance* node computes the variance and standard deviation of a field over a given domain.
This is useful for measuring how much a value varies across geometry or within specific groups.

For example, it can be used to analyze the spread of values like weights, positions, or custom attributes
within each group defined by the *Group ID*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_variance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Variance Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Variance Node Inputs
text:
Value
   The field to evaluate. Can be a float or a vector depending on the *Data Type*.
   For vector values, variance is computed separately per component (X, Y, Z).

Group ID
   An index used to group values together for multiple separate variances.
   This can be thought of as a choice of the "bin" in which to place each value.
   This input has no effect when it is only a single value.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_variance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Variance Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Variance Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   :Float: The node will average a *Float* field.
   :Vector: The node will average a *Vector* field.

Domain
   The attribute domain used for evaluate the *Value* input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_variance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field Variance Node > Output
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Field Variance Node Output
text:
Standard Deviation
   The square root of the variance, describing the spread of values.

Variance
   A measure of the average squared deviation from the mean.
   Higher values indicate more variation in the input field.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/field_variance.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Principal Components Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Principal Components Node Principal Components Node
text:
The *Principal Components* node performs a Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
on a field of positions.

PCA analyzes how the positions are distributed, finding the center of the
data along with the orthogonal axes that best describe its orientation and
shape. The resulting axes are ordered by how much the data varies along each
direction, from greatest to least.

This is useful for determining the dominant orientation of geometry,
aligning objects to point clouds, generating local coordinate systems,
or measuring the extent of a distribution.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Principal Components Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Principal Components Node Inputs
text:
Position
   Position values to analyze.

Group ID
   Integer field defining independent analysis groups.

   Elements with the same group ID are analyzed together, while elements
   with different group IDs are processed independently.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Principal Components Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Principal Components Node Outputs
text:
Group Center
   Center of the analyzed group.

Rotation
   Rotation whose local axes correspond to the principal axes of the data.

Principal Components
   Variance of the data along each principal axis.

   Larger values indicate greater spread along the corresponding axis.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Principal Components Node > Principal Axes
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Field Principal Components Node Principal Axes
text:
Longest Axis
   Unit vector corresponding to the direction of greatest variance.

Intermediate Axis
   Unit vector corresponding to the direction of intermediate variance.

   Together with the other axes, it forms a right-handed orthogonal basis.

Shortest Axis
   Unit vector corresponding to the direction of least variance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/field/principal_components.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: For Each Geometry Element Zone
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities For Each Geometry Element Zone For Each Geometry Element Zone
text:
This zone type allows executing nodes for each element of a geometry. For example, the nodes can process
every face of a mesh, or every instance.

The zone is ideal for tasks that generate large or complex geometry for every element of an input geometry.
For example, generating a unique tree for every input curve, or a unique building on every input face.

The zone makes less sense for processing small amounts of geometry. In that case (for example each of a character's
hairs separately) it will likely **always be slower** than working on fewer larger geometries. The additional
flexibility from processing each element separately comes at the cost that Blender can't optimize the operation
as well. For node groups that need to handle lots of geometry elements, it's recommended to design the node setup
so that iteration over tiny sub-geometries is not required.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/for_each_geometry_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: For Each Geometry Element Zone > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities For Each Geometry Element Zone Inputs
text:
Geometry
   Geometry whose elements are iterated over.

Selection
   Which subset of the chosen *Domain* to process.

Index
   Index of the element in the source geometry. Note that the same index can occur more than
   once when iterating over multiple geometry component types at once.

Element
   The input geometry is split up into a separate geometry for each element.
   This is the single element geometry for the current iteration. This is not available
   for the *Face Corner* domain, since face corners cannot exist without their face.

Note:
      It can be quite inefficient to split up large geometries into many small elements.
      Because this output isn't computed if it's not used in the node graph, not using it
      will typically improve performance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/for_each_geometry_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: For Each Geometry Element Zone > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities For Each Geometry Element Zone Properties
text:
Domain
   Which attribute domain to process.

Inspection Index
   Geometry element index that is used by inspection features like the viewer
   or socket inspection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/for_each_geometry_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: For Each Geometry Element Zone > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities For Each Geometry Element Zone Outputs
text:
The *Main Geometry* outputs create attributes on the "main" output geometry (the first output).
Every single value on the inside of the zone becomes a value of the attribute at the current index.

The outputs in the *Generated* panel, including the default *Geometry* output are joined together from the
geometry generated from each element. Any non-geometry type below a specific geometry in this list will output
as an anonymous attribute on that joined geometry (and not the others).
Attributes from the zone's input geometry are also propagated to these geometry outputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/for_each_geometry_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index Switch Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Index Switch Node Index Switch Node
text:
The *Index Switch* node outputs one of its inputs based on an integer *Index* value.
Only the selected input is evaluated, making this node useful for switching between
multiple data inputs efficiently.

Seealso:

   The Menu Switch node provides similar functionality,
   but exposes the selection as a user-friendly menu rather than an index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/index_switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index Switch Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Index Switch Node Inputs
text:
Index
   Determines which of the following input sockets is passed through to the output.
   The index is zero-based (i.e., the first input corresponds to index 0).

Each socket represents a possible input to select from.
The active input is determined by the *Index* value.

Additional input sockets can be added by either:
- Dragging a connection onto the empty socket at the bottom of the list.
- Clicking the :bl-icon:`add` icon in the node header.

Tip:

   When the *Index* input is connected to a Menu Switch node
   set to *Integer* *Type*, the corresponding menu labels will automatically be shown next to the index value.
   This provides a clearer context for what each numeric index represents, making node networks more readable.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/index_switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Index Switch Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Index Switch Node Outputs
text:
Output
   Outputs the value from the input corresponding to the current *Index* value,
   without any modification.
   If the *Index* value is outside the range of available inputs, the output defaults
   to the first input or a zero-equivalent value, depending on the data type.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/index_switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure to List Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Closure to List Node Closure to List Node
text:
The *Closure to List* node evaluates a closure multiple times and stores the
resulting values in a list.

This is useful for generating lists procedurally, where each iteration can
produce a different value based on the current index or other inputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/closure_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure to List Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Closure to List Node Inputs
text:
Count
   The number of elements to generate in the output list.

Closure
   The closure that is evaluated once for each list element.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/closure_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Closure to List Node > Items
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Closure to List Node Items
text:
A list of all items evaluated from the input closure.

Each item definition creates a corresponding list output.

Socket Type
   The data type of the values stored in the generated list.

Shape
   The data structure used for the list items. This can be any supported
   socket shape, such as single values, fields or grids.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/closure_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine List Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Combine List Node Combine List Node
text:
The *Combine List* node creates a list by combining individual values into an ordered sequence.

Each input corresponds to an item in the resulting list, with the order of the inputs
determining the order of the items. Additional items can be added or removed to control
the size of the list.

This node is useful for constructing lists from individual values, which can then be
passed to other nodes that operate on lists.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/combine_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine List Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Combine List Node Inputs
text:
The node provides a separate input socket for each item defined in the *Items* list.

Each input specifies the value of the corresponding item in the resulting list.
The inputs are evaluated in the same order as they appear on the node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/combine_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine List Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Combine List Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the list. All items in the list use the same data type.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/combine_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine List Node > Items
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Combine List Node Items
text:
A list of items that defines the number and order of the node's input sockets.

Each item creates a corresponding input socket on the node.
Items can be reordered to change their position in the resulting list.

The :bl-icon:`add` button adds a new item, while the :bl-icon:`remove` buttons
removes the selected item.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/combine_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine List Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Combine List Node Outputs
text:
List
   A list containing the values of all input items, in the order defined by the *Items* list.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/combine_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to List Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Field to List Node Field to List Node
text:
The *Field to List* node evaluates one or more fields and converts their values into lists.

Each field is evaluated for every element in the current context, and the
resulting values are collected into a list. This is useful when working with
nodes that operate on lists rather than fields.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/field_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to List Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Field to List Node Inputs
text:
Field Inputs
   One or more field inputs to evaluate.
   Additional fields can be added in the node properties.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/field_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to List Node > Items
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Field to List Node Items
text:
A list of all input fields to be evaluated.

Each item definition creates a corresponding list output.

Socket Type
   The data type of the field to evaluate and the generated list values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/field_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to List Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Field to List Node Outputs
text:
Each field defined in the node properties creates a corresponding list output.

The output list contains the evaluated value of the field for every element in
the current context.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/field_to_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Filter List Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Filter List Node Filter List Node
text:
The *Filter List* node splits a list into two lists based on a boolean selection.

Items with a corresponding selection value of true are placed in the
*Selection* output, while items with a selection value of false are placed
in the *Inverted* output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/filter_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Filter List Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Filter List Node Inputs
text:
List
   The input list to filter.

Selection
   A boolean list used to determine which items are included in each output.

   The selection list is matched to the input list by index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/filter_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Filter List Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Filter List Node Outputs
text:
Selection
   A list containing all items whose corresponding selection value is true.

Inverted
   A list containing all items whose corresponding selection value is false.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/filter_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get List Item Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Get List Item Node Get List Item Node
text: The *Get List Item* node returns the value stored at a specific index in a list.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/get_list_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get List Item Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Get List Item Node Inputs
text:
List
   The input list.

Index
   The index of the item to retrieve.

   Indices are zero-based, meaning the first item in the list has an index of 0.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/get_list_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get List Item Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Get List Item Node Outputs
text:
Value
   The value stored at the specified index in the input list.

   If the index is outside the bounds of the list,
   the default value for the selected data type is returned.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/get_list_item.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sort List Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Sort List Node Sort List Node
text:
The *Sort List* node sorts the elements of a list according to a weight value.

The sort order is ascending, with elements having lower weights placed
before elements with higher weights.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/sort_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sort List Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > List Sort List Node Inputs
text:
List
   The input list to sort.

Selection
   Controls which list elements are sorted.

   Deselected elements remain in their original positions.

Group ID
   Separates the list into independent groups.

   Elements with the same group ID are sorted together, while elements in
   different groups are sorted independently.

Sort Weight
   Value used to determine the order of the list elements.

   Lower values are placed before higher values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/list/sort_list.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bit Math Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Bit Math Node Bit Math Node
text:
The *Bit Math* node performs bitwise operations on 32-bit integer values.
It is useful for low-level data manipulation and logic operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/bit_math.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bit Math Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Bit Math Node Inputs
text:
A
   The first integer input. Used by all operations.
B
   The second integer input. Only used by operations that require two inputs (*And*, *Or*, *Exclusive Or*).
Shift
   The number of bits to shift or rotate. Used only for *Shift* and *Rotate* operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/bit_math.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bit Math Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Bit Math Node Properties
text:
Operation
   The bitwise operation to apply:

   :And: Returns a value where the bits of A and B are both set.
   :Or: Returns a value where the bits of either A or B are set.
   :Exclusive Or: Returns a value where only one of A or B has the bit set (XOR).
   :Not: Inverts the bits of A. Equivalent to `-A - 1` in decimal.
   :Shift: Shifts the bits of A by the amount specified in *Shift*. Positive shifts are to the left; negative to the
    right.
   :Rotate: Rotates the bits of A by the amount specified in *Shift*. Positive rotates left; negative rotates right.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/bit_math.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Boolean Math Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Boolean Math Node Properties
text:
Mode
   :And:
      True when both inputs are true.
      (`AND <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND_gate>`__)
   :Or:
      True when at least one input is true.
      (`OR <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OR_gate>`__)
   :Not:
      Opposite of the input.
      (`NOT <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOT_gate>`__)
   :Not And:
      (True when at least one input is false.
      `NAND <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAND_gate>`__)
   :Nor:
      True when both inputs are false.
      (`NOR <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOR_gate>`__)
   :Equal:
      True when both inputs are equal. Also known as "exclusive nor".
      (`XNOR <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XNOR_gate>`__)
   :Not Equal:
      (`XOR <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XOR_gate>`__)
      True when both inputs are different. Also known as "exclusive or".
   :Imply:
      True unless the first input is true and the second is false.
      (`IMPLY <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMPLY_gate>`__)
   :Subtract:
      True when the first input is true and the second is false. Also known as ""not imply".
      (`NIMPLY <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NIMPLY_gate>`__)
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/boolean_math.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Compare Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Compare Node Compare Node
text:
The *Compare* node compares two values and outputs whether they satisfy a selected comparison operation.

The node supports all generic data types, including data-blocks. For vector inputs, additional comparison
modes are available that can perform more complex comparisons while reducing the number of required nodes
and improving node tree readability.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/compare.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Compare Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Compare Node Inputs
text:
A, B
   Standard value inputs of the selected type.
C
   Compared against the dot product of two input vectors in when the *Mode* property is set to *Dot Product*.
Epsilon
   This value is used as a threshold for still considering the two inputs as equal
   for the Equal and Not Equal operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/compare.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Compare Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Compare Node Properties
text:
Type
   The data type to compare.

Mode
   Method used to compare vector inputs.

   :Element-Wise:
      Compare each axis of the input vectors separately, and output true only when the result is true
      for each axis.
   :Length:
      Compare the length of the two input vectors.
   :Average:
      Compare the average of the elements of the input vectors. This is the same as the implicit
      conversion used when setting the node's data type to *Float*.
   :Dot Product:
      Compare the dot product of the two vectors with the separate *C* input, using the selected operation.
      The dot product outputs a single value that says how much the two vectors "agree".
   :Direction:
      Compare the angle between the two vectors with the separate *Angle* input, using the selected operation.
      The vectors are normalized, so their length does not matter.

Operation
   The comparison operation to perform.
   Available operations depend on the selected data type.

   :Less Than:
      True when the first input is smaller than second input.
   :Less Than or Equal:
      True when the first input is smaller than the second input or equal.
   :Greater Than:
      True when the first input is greater than the second input.
   :Greater Than or Equal:
      True when the first input is greater than the second input or equal.
   :Equal:
      True when both the difference between the two inputs is smaller than the *Epsilon* input.
   :Not Equal:
      True when both the difference between the two inputs is larger than the *Epsilon* input.
   :Brighter:
      True when the first color input is brighter than the second.
   :Darker:
      True when the first color input is darker than the second.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/compare.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Compare Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Compare Node Examples
text:
Here, the compare node is used with the *Direction* mode to compare the direction of the
sphere's face normals to the "direction"
of the cube object's location. Anywhere that the directions are less than 32.9 degrees apart,
the faces will be selected, and deleted.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/compare.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Float To Integer Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Float To Integer Node Float To Integer Node
text:
The *Float To Integer* node takes a single floating point number input and converts it to
an integer with a choice of methods.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/float_to_integer.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Float To Integer Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Float To Integer Node Properties
text:
Rounding Mode
   :Round: Outputs the closest integer to Float, rounding either up or down based on the value.
   :Floor: Outputs the closest integer less than Float, always rounding down.
   :Ceiling: Outputs the closest integer greater than Float, always rounding up.
   :Truncate: Outputs the closest integer between Float and zero. For positive numbers, acts like Floor.
              For negative numbers, acts as Ceiling.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/float_to_integer.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Hash Value Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Hash Value Node Hash Value Node
text:
The *Hash Value* node takes a value input and hashes this to
an integer.

Important:

   Hashes cannot be relied upon to be used as unique
   identifiers because they are not guaranteed to be unique.
   It can be used to generate somewhat stable randomness
   especially in cases where *White Noise* does not offer
   enough flexibility.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/hash_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Hash Value Node Inputs

Seed

name: Hash Value Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Hash Value Node Properties
text:
Data Type

   The node supports float, integer, vector, color,

source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/hash_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Integer Math Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Integer Math Node Inputs
text:
Value
   Standard integer value input. Depending on the operation
   there will be more than one input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/integer_math.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Integer Math Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Math Integer Math Node Properties
text:
Operation
   The mathematical operator to be applied to the input values:

   Functions
      :Add: The sum of the two values.
      :Subtract: The difference between the two values.
      :Multiply: The product of the two values.
      :Divide: The division of the first value by the second value.
      :Multiply Add: The sum of the product of the two values with *Addend*.
      :Absolute:
         The input value is read without regard to its sign.
         This turns negative values into positive values.
      :Negate: Changes the sign of the input value.
      :Power: The *Base* raised to the power of *Exponent*.

   Comparison
      :Minimum: Outputs the smallest of the input values.
      :Maximum: Outputs the largest of two input values.
      :Sign:
         Extracts the sign of the input value. All positive numbers
         will output 1. All negative numbers will output -1. And 0 will output 0.

   Rounding
      :Divide Round: Divide the values and round the result toward zero.
      :Divide Floor: Divide the values and floor the result down to the nearest integer.
      :Divide Ceiling: Divide the values and ceil the result up to the nearest integer.
      :Floored Modulo: Returns the positive remainder of a division operation.
      :Modulo: Outputs the remainder once the first value is divided by the second value.
      :Greatest Common Divisor: The largest positive integer that divides into each of the values.
      :Least Common Multiple: The smallest positive integer that is divisible by both values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/math/integer_math.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Invert Matrix Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Matrix Invert Matrix Node Invert Matrix Node
text: Returns the `inverse <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/MatrixInverse.html>`__ of the given matrix.

name: Matrix Determinant Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Matrix Matrix Determinant Node Matrix Determinant Node
text:
The *Matrix Determinant* node computes the `determinant <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant>`__ of the passed
in matrix.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/matrix/matrix_determinant.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Matrix SVD Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Matrix Matrix SVD Node Matrix SVD Node
text:
The *Matrix SVD* node computes the 3D `singular value decomposition
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singular_value_decomposition>`__ of the input matrix. The SVD describes the matrix in
terms of a left and a right transformation U and V with a diagonal scaling matrix `S inbetween.

M = U * S * transpose(V)

Only the 3x3 part of the input matrix M is used, the translation part (4th column vector) is not used. The matrix
does not have to be a pure (affine) transformation, any input matrix can be decomposed.

The output matrices U and V consist only of rotations and reflections (+1 or -1 scaling). If the input matrix
M has a positive determinant then U and V are pure rotations. The scaling matrix S is described only
by the diagonal vector.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/matrix/matrix_svd.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Multiply Matrices Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Matrix Multiply Matrices Node Multiply Matrices Node
text:
The *Multiply Matrices* node performs a
`matrix multiplication <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_multiplication>`__
on two input matrices.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/matrix/multiply_matrices.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Project Point Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Matrix Project Point Node Project Point Node
text:
Applies a projection matrix to a point. Specifically, this node turns the given
Euclidean vector (X, Y, Z) into the homogeneous vector (X, Y, Z, 1),
multiplies the given projection matrix by it,
and turns the resulting homogeneous vector back into a Euclidean one by dividing
it by the absolute value of its W component. This last step is also known as
perspective division.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/matrix/project_point.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Project Point Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Matrix Project Point Node Inputs

Vector

Transformation
   The projection matrix.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/matrix/project_point.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Menu Switch Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Menu Switch Node Menu Switch Node
text:
The *Menu Switch* node outputs one of its inputs based on a selected menu item.
Only the active input is evaluated, allowing efficient switching between multiple options.

On top of not evaluating any inactive inputs, which is something all switch nodes do, the
*Menu Switch* has the extra functionality that it hides any socket that is connected
to an inactive input, even if they are indirectly coupled through an *Index Switch* or
*Switch* node. This can be used to hide irrelevant settings from the node interface or
modifier panel.

The available menu entries are defined by the user. Menu items can be
added and removed, as well as renamed and reordered in the editor side
bar. Renaming a menu entry keeps existing links of the matching input
socket.

The menu can be used in node groups and the nodes modifier UI.
Connecting the menu input with a *Group Input* node will expose the menu
as a group input. A menu socket in a node group, reroute node, or other
pass-through nodes needs to be connected to a *Menu Switch* node in
order to work. An unconnected menu socket will show an empty menu by
default.

Connecting multiple *Menu Switch* nodes to the same output
socket creates a conflict (even when the menu entries are the same).
To avoid this a menu switch can be wrapped in a node group. Multiple
node groups of the same type can be connected to the same menu, since
they contain the same menu switch node.

Seealso:

   The index switch
   is similar but it exposes the choices as an integer index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/menu_switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Menu Switch Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Menu Switch Node Inputs
text:
Menu
   Determines which input socket is passed through to the output.

One input is created for each menu entry. The input corresponding to the selected menu item
is evaluated and passed through.

Menu item labels can be renamed using Ctrl-LMB on the socket name or in the node's *Properties* panel.

Additional input sockets can be added by:
- Dragging a connection onto the empty socket at the bottom of the list.
- Clicking the :bl-icon:`add` icon in the node header.

Unused inputs are not computed, improving performance in complex node networks.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/menu_switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Menu Switch Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Menu Switch Node Outputs
text:
Output
   Outputs the value from the input corresponding to the selected menu item, unchanged.

For each menu entry, an additional Boolean output is created.
The output corresponding to the selected item is *true*, and all others are *false*.
These Boolean outputs can be used to trigger different node branches, control visibility,
or drive conditional operations elsewhere in the node tree.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/menu_switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Rotation Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Rotation Node Random Rotation Node
text:
The *Random Rotation* node generates random rotation values within a specified angular range.
It can be used to randomize the orientation of instances, particles, or elements of a geometry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_rotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Rotation Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Rotation Node Inputs
text:
Min Zenith
   The minimum zenith (vertical) rotation angle.
   Defines the lower limit of the random rotation.

Max Zenith
   The maximum zenith (vertical) rotation angle.
   Defines the upper limit of the random rotation.

ID
   An ID to drive the random number generator seed. By default, this input uses the same value
   as the id, which is the id attribute of the context
   geometry if it exists, and otherwise the index.

Tip: Single Random Value

      By default, the node generates a unique random rotation for each element (based on its ID).
      To generate a single random rotation for the entire geometry, connect a constant value
      (such as an integer) to the *ID* input.

Seed
   A field to seed the random number generator. This can be used to produce
   a different set of random rotations even when using the same *ID* input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_rotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Rotation Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Rotation Node Outputs
text:
Rotation
   The output rotation as a rotation socket. This can be used directly
   to orient instances or to drive other transformations in the node tree.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_rotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Value Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Value Node Random Value Node
text: The *Random Value* node outputs a white noise like value as a *Float*, *Integer*, *Vector*, or *Boolean* field.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Value Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Value Node Inputs
text:
Min
   The minimum value of the range where random values are sampled from.
   This input is only available for *Float*, *Integer*, and *Vector* types.

Max
   The maximum value of the range where random values are sampled from.
   This input is only available for *Float*, *Integer*, and *Vector* types.

Probability
   The probability ratio for the random *Boolean* output to be *True*.
   This input is only available for *Boolean* types.

ID
   An ID to drive the random number generator seed.

Note:

      For geometry nodes, by default, this input uses the same value
      as of the id, which is the id attribute of the context
      geometry if it exists, and otherwise the index.

Tip: Single Random Value

      By default, the random value node generates a value for each unique index.
      If a single random value is desired, connect a single value
      (such as an integer ) to the ID input.

Seed
   A field to Seed the random number generator. This can be used to generate
   a different set of random values, even for two nodes with the same *ID* input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Value Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Value Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   :Float: The output will be a *Float* field.
   :Integer: The output will be an *Integer* field.
   :Vector: The output will be a *Vector* field.
   :Boolean: The output will be a *Boolean* field.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Random Value Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Random Value Node Outputs
text:
Value
   Random values as a field.

Note:

   The random values of the Value output are not guaranteed to be unique. This means that two different
   ID and/or Seed input values may result in the same random value being generated.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/random_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Repeat Zone
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Repeat Zone Repeat Zone
text:
A *Repeat Zone* executes a set of nodes multiple times.

The zone consists of an input node on the left, an output node on the right,
and an orange area in the middle for placing the nodes to repeat. When the zone executes
for the first time, it evaluates its inputs and forwards them to its inner nodes.
These inner nodes can then write to the output node for providing inputs to the next
iteration, and for providing the result of the zone after the last iteration.

The nodes inside the zone can also take inputs from nodes outside the zone -- these
inputs are then the same in every iteration. However, nodes inside the zone can't
send their outputs to nodes outside the zone.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/repeat_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Repeat Zone > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Repeat Zone Inputs
text:
Iterations
   Number of times to execute the zone. The *Iteration* socket gives the index of
   the current iteration, starting from 0.

Geometry
   Default geometry input. Further inputs can be added by connecting a node's output
   to the zone's blank input, or by using the *Repeat Items* list in the node's
   *Properties* panel.

   The inputs can be renamed by clicking them with Ctrl-LMB in the zone
   itself or in the *Repeat Items* list. The latter also accepts double clicking.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/repeat_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Repeat Zone > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Repeat Zone Properties
text:
Repeat Items
   ui-list-view for adding, removing, reordering, and renaming the inputs of the zone.

   Socket Type
      The data type of the selected input.

Inspection Index
   The number of the iteration to show in socket inspection
   and in the viewer.

.. --- copy until this line ---
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/repeat_zone.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

Each iteration creates a cube, brings it into position, and

name: Align Rotation to Vector Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Rotation Align Rotation to Vector Node Align Rotation to Vector Node
text: The *Align Rotation to Vector* node rotates an Euler rotation into the given direction.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/rotation/align_rotation_to_vector.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Align Rotation to Vector Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Rotation Align Rotation to Vector Node Inputs
text:
Rotation
   The Euler rotation to align.

Important:

      This input has to be a rotation input. Be careful not to connect a direction vector
      like the normal.

Factor
   Determines how much the points are rotated towards the vector.
   Zero effectively disables the node and one means that the points are aligned with the vector perfectly.

name: Sample Sound Frequencies Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Sound Sample Sound Frequencies Node Sample Sound Frequencies Node
text:
The *Sample Sound Frequencies* node retrieves the amplitude of a frequency range
from a sound data-block at a given point in time.

This can be used to drive animations, procedural effects, or geometry based on
the intensity of specific frequency bands in an audio file.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/sound/sample_sound_frequencies.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Sound Frequencies Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Sound Sample Sound Frequencies Node Inputs
text:
Sound
   The sound data-block to sample.

Time
   The time, in seconds, at which to sample the sound.

All Channels
   Mix all audio channels together before sampling.

   For example, a stereo sound is converted to a single mono signal.

Channel
   The audio channel to sample when *All Channels* is disabled.

Low
   The lower bound of the sampled frequency range, in Hertz.

High
   The upper bound of the sampled frequency range, in Hertz.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/sound/sample_sound_frequencies.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sample Sound Frequencies Node > FFT
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Sound Sample Sound Frequencies Node FFT
text:
Settings that control the Fourier transform used for frequency analysis.

FFT Size
   The number of audio samples processed in each discrete Fourier transform.

   Higher values provide better frequency resolution but lower time resolution.
   Lower values provide better time resolution but lower frequency resolution.

   :128: Very high time resolution with coarse frequency resolution.
   :256: High time resolution with coarse frequency resolution.
   :512: Balanced toward time resolution.
   :1024: Moderate frequency and time resolution.
   :2048: Good balance between frequency and time resolution.
   :4096: Increased frequency resolution with reduced time resolution.
   :8192: High frequency resolution for detailed spectral analysis.
   :16384: Very high frequency resolution with low time resolution.
   :32768: Maximum frequency resolution with the lowest time resolution.

Window Function
   Applies a weighting function to the analyzed samples before performing the
   Fourier transform. This reduces discontinuities at the edges of the sample
   window, helping to reduce spectral artifacts.

   :Hann: General-purpose window with good frequency analysis characteristics.
   :Hamming: Similar to Hann with slightly different side-lobe behavior.
   :Blackman:
      Provides stronger suppression of spectral leakage at the cost of wider frequency peaks.
   :Rectangular: No windowing is applied.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/sound/sample_sound_frequencies.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

text:

source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/sound/sample_sound_frequencies.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Switch Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities Switch Node Switch Node
text:
The *Switch* node outputs one of two inputs depending on a condition.

When the inputs are regular values, only the input that is passed through
the node is evaluated. This means the unused input is not computed.

Note:

   For Geometry Nodes:

   When the inputs are fields, both inputs may be evaluated
   before the switch is applied. The switch then selects which result is used
   for each element. Because of this, the node should not be relied on to avoid
   evaluating expensive field inputs.

Seealso:

   The menu switch and index switch
   can be used to switch between an arbitrary amount of inputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/switch.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Format String Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Format String Node Format String Node
text:
The *Format String* node inserts values into a string using either a Python compatible
string format syntax or Blender's format specifier syntax.

This node simplifies string construction, allowing values to be combined
and formatted without converting numbers to strings or using multiple concatenate nodes.

Seealso:

   Python Syntax references:
   - `Python Format String Syntax <https://docs.python.org/3/library/string.html#format-string-syntax>`__
   - `{fmt} Format String Syntax <https://fmt.dev/latest/syntax/>`__
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/format_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Format String Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Format String Node Inputs
text:
Format
   A string using either python format style or Blender's format specifier.
   For example, Count: {} inserts the first input value in place of the `{}`.

Additional input values (Float, Integer, or String) can be managed in the Format Items list in the sidebar.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/format_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Format String Node > Format Items
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Format String Node Format Items
text:
A list view. to manage the dynamic list of inputs used in the format string.
Each entry corresponds to a value that can be inserted into the format using a placeholder.
See `Input Naming Behavior`_ to understand how inputs must be named.

Socket Type
   The type of value for this input:

   :Float: A floating-point number (e.g. 3.14).
   :Integer: An integer number (e.g. 42).
   :String: A text string.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/format_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Format String Node > Notes
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Format String Node Notes
text:
- Supports both unnamed ({}) and named ({name}) placeholders.
  However, all unnamed placeholders must appear before any named ones.
- Only float, integer, and string inputs are supported.
- Python-style conversions such as !r are not supported.
- Sub-attribute access (e.g. {vector.x}) is not supported.
- Percent-based formatting (e.g. %d, %s) is not supported.
- Alternate form specifiers using # (e.g. {:#x}) are not supported.
- Locale-based formatting using L (as in the `fmt` library) is not supported.
- Grouping options like thousands separators (e.g. {:,} or {:_}) are not supported.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/format_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Format String Node > Input Naming Behavior
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Format String Node Input Naming Behavior
text:
Each input must have a unique, valid identifier name used in placeholders (e.g. {value}).
This node uses special logic to automatically assign names to new inputs:

- If connected, the first character of the linked socket's name is used.
- Otherwise, names default to letters a through z.
- If needed, the original socket name is converted to a valid identifier.
- If all else fails, a unique suffix is appended (e.g. _001, _002).

Important:

   Input names must be valid identifiers and must be unique.
   If a name is invalid, the format operation may fail or produce incorrect output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/format_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Curves Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node String to Curves Node
text:
The *String to Curves* node converts a string to curve instances. Each unique character used in the string
is converted to a curve once, and further uses of that character are instances of the same geometry.
The name of each instance geometry is the character it represents.

This makes processing the output geometry very efficient, because each unique character
only has to be processed once. However, it means that the result will be the same
for every instance of the same character. To process each character individually,
the realize instances can be used.

Tip:

   Socket inspection can be used to see the value
   of the string input used when the node was evaluated, by holding the mouse over the socket.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node Inputs

String

Size
