Font
   Font glyph used to generate the curve.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Curves Node > Alignment
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node Alignment
text:
Align X
   Controls horizontal alignment of text on each line.

   :Left: Aligns the text to the left.
   :Center: Aligns the text to the center.
   :Right: Aligns the text to the right.
   :Justify: Aligns the text to the left and right.
   :Flush: Aligns the text to the left and right with equal character spacing.

Align Y
   Controls vertical alignment of the block of text.

   :Top: Aligns the text to the top.
   :Top Baseline: Aligns the text to the top baseline.
   :Middle: Aligns the text to the middle.
   :Bottom Baseline: Aligns the text to the bottom baseline.
   :Bottom: Aligns the text to the bottom.

Pivot Point
   Controls where on each character the output *Pivot Point* is placed.

   :Midpoint: Place the pivot points at the center of each character's bounds.
   :Top Left: Place the pivot points at the top left of each character's bounds.
   :Top Center: Place the pivot points at the middle of the top of each character's bounds.
   :Top Right: Place the pivot points at the top right of each character's bounds.
   :Bottom Left: Place the pivot points at the bottom left of each character's bounds.
   :Bottom Center: Place the pivot points at the middle of bottom of each character's bounds.
   :Bottom Right: Place the pivot points at the bottom right of each character's bounds.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Curves Node > Spacing
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node Spacing
text:
Character Spacing
   A factor by which the space between each character (kerning) is scaled on the X axis.

Word Spacing
   A factor by which whitespace between words is scaled on the X axis.

Line Spacing
   The distance between separate lines in the output. Scaled by the *Size* input.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Curves Node > Text Box
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node Text Box
text:
Overflow
   Controls how the text fits inside the text box.

   :Overflow:
      Wraps the text at the *Text Box Width*.
   :Scale To Fit:
      Scales the text size to fit the *Text Box Width* and *Text Box Height*.
   :Truncate:
      Only outputs text characters that fit within the width and height, based on the *Size* input.
      Any part of the string that did not fit is moved to the *Remainder* output.

Text Box Width
   The maximum width of each line, though individual words will not be wrapped.

Text Box Height
   The maximum height for all the lines of the text.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Curves Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node Outputs
text:
Curve Instances
   Geometry output containing one instance per character.

Remainder
   The part of the text that did not fit in the box described by the *Text Box Height* and
   *Text Box Width* inputs. Only used in the *Truncate* overflow mode.

Line
   An attribute field containing the line index of each character
   (on the instance domain).

Word
   An attribute field containing the word index of each character
   (on the instance domain).

Pivot Point
   Outputs the position described by the *Pivot Point* drop-down in the local space of each instance.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Curves Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Curves Node Examples
text:
The node can be used to make overflowing text boxes. Here, the text that does not fit into
the first node's fixed-size text box is passed to a separate *String to Curves* node,
then scaled with a *Scale to Fit* node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_curves.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Value Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Value Node String to Value Node
text:
The *String to Value* node converts a text string into a numerical value.
This is useful for parsing numbers from text input, file data, or dynamically generated strings.

The node reads characters from the beginning of the string until a valid number is parsed.
If parsing is unsuccessful, the node outputs a floating-point value of 0.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Value Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Value Node Inputs
text:
String
   The input text string to be converted into a numerical value.

Base Integer Data Type
   Numeric base used when parsing integers.

   For example, use 2 for binary, 8 for octal, 10 for decimal,
   or 16 for hexadecimal.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Value Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Value Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of numerical value to convert to:

   :Float: Converts the text to a floating-point number.
   :Integer: Converts the text to a 32-bit integer.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Value Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Value Node Outputs
text:
Value
   The resulting numerical value after conversion.

Length
   The number of characters successfully parsed as part of the number.
   This indicates where the numeric portion of the string ends, allowing further substring operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: String to Value Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text String to Value Node Examples
text:
- Converting the string "3.1415" with *Float* selected outputs a value of 3.1415 and a length of 6.
- Converting "42abc" with *Integer* selected outputs 42 and a length of 2.
- Converting an invalid string such as "hello" outputs 0 and a length of 0.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/string_to_value.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Tag Filter Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Tag Filter Node Tag Filter Node
text:
The *Tag Filter* node checks whether a list of tags matches a tag filter.

A tag filter consists of one or more tag names separated by commas. The node
returns true when any tag in the filter exists in the input tag list.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/tag_filter.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Tag Filter Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Tag Filter Node Inputs
text:
Tag Filter
   Comma-separated list of tag names to match.

   Whitespace around tag names is ignored. An empty filter matches all tag lists.

Tags
   List of tags to evaluate.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/tag_filter.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Tag Filter Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Tag Filter Node Outputs
text:
Match
   True when any tag in the *Tag Filter* exists in the input *Tags* list, otherwise false.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/tag_filter.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Tag Filter Node > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Tag Filter Node Examples
text:
- "metal" matches tag lists containing metal.
- "metal, painted" matches tag lists containing either metal or painted.
- "" (an empty filter) always matches.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/tag_filter.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Trim String Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Trim String Node Trim String Node
text:
The *Trim String* node removes specified characters from the beginning and/or end
of a string. It does not affect characters in the middle of the string.

This node is useful for cleaning up input data, such as removing unwanted prefixes,
suffixes, or extra whitespace.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/trim_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Trim String Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Trim String Node Inputs
text:
String
   The input string to trim.

Characters
   A set of characters to remove from the start and/or end of the string.

   Each character is treated individually, and the order does not matter.
   Any matching characters found at the boundaries of the string are removed
   repeatedly until a non-matching character is encountered.

Whitespace
   Removes whitespace characters (such as spaces, tabs, and line breaks)
   in addition to the characters specified in *Characters*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/trim_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Trim String Node > Limit
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Trim String Node Limit
text:
Start
   Enables trimming from the beginning of the string.

End
   Enables trimming from the end of the string.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/trim_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Value to String Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Value to String Node Inputs
text:
Value
   Floating-point value to be converted.

Decimals Float Data Type
   Integer value used to determine the precision of the output value.

Base Integer Data Type
   Numeric base used to represent integer values.

   For example, use 2 for binary, 8 for octal, 10 for decimal,
   or 16 for hexadecimal.

Padding Integer Data Type
   Minimum width of the output string.

   If the converted value contains fewer characters than the specified
   width, leading zeros are added until the minimum width is reached.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/value_to_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Value to String Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Text Value to String Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of numerical value to convert to a string.

   :Float: Convert a floating-point value to a string.
   :Integer: Convert a 32-bit integer to a string.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/text/value_to_string.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: 3D to Screen Space Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector 3D to Screen Space Node 3D to Screen Space Node
text:
The *3D to Screen Space* node transforms 3D positions into normalized screen
coordinates relative to a camera.

The output coordinates are normalized such that (0, 0) corresponds to the
bottom-left corner of the camera view and (1, 1) corresponds to the
top-right corner. Values outside this range represent positions outside the
camera frame.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/3d_to_screen_space.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: 3D to Screen Space Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector 3D to Screen Space Node Inputs
text:
Vector
   Position to transform into screen space.

Camera
   Camera used for the transformation.

Clamp Depth
   Clamp the output depth to the camera's clipping range.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/3d_to_screen_space.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: 3D to Screen Space Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector 3D to Screen Space Node Outputs
text:
Normalized
   Normalized screen-space coordinates.

Depth
   Distance of the input position from the camera.

   Values outside the camera's clipping range are only returned when
   *Clamp Depth* is disabled.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/3d_to_screen_space.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Cylindrical Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Combine Cylindrical Node Combine Cylindrical Node
text:
The *Combine Cylindrical* node converts cylindrical coordinates (R, Φ, Z)
into a Cartesian vector (X, Y, Z). It is the inverse of the
Separate Cylindrical node.

This node is useful for constructing positions or directions based on radial distance,
rotation angle, and height, such as creating spiral shapes or cylindrical displacements.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/combine_cylindrical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Cylindrical Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Combine Cylindrical Node Inputs
text:
R
   The radial distance from the origin in the X-Y plane.

Phi
   The angle around the Z axis.

Z
   The vertical position or height component.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/combine_cylindrical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Cylindrical Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Combine Cylindrical Node Outputs
text:
Vector
   The resulting Cartesian vector corresponding to the input cylindrical coordinates.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/combine_cylindrical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Spherical Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Combine Spherical Node Combine Spherical Node
text:
The *Combine Spherical* node converts spherical coordinates (R, Φ, Θ)
into a Cartesian vector (X, Y, Z). It is the inverse of the
Separate Spherical node.

Spherical coordinates represent a point in 3D space by its distance from the origin,
horizontal rotation, and vertical inclination, which can be useful for constructing
radial or rotational patterns and generating coordinates on a sphere.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/combine_spherical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Spherical Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Combine Spherical Node Inputs
text:
R
   The radial distance from the origin.

Phi
   The azimuthal angle (horizontal rotation) around the Z axis.

Theta
   The polar angle (vertical inclination) from the ground plane.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/combine_spherical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Combine Spherical Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Combine Spherical Node Outputs
text:
Vector
   The resulting Cartesian vector corresponding to the input spherical coordinates.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/combine_spherical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Vector Component Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Get Vector Component Node Get Vector Component Node
text: The *Get Vector Component* node retrieves an individual component of a vector using its index.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/get_vector_component.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Get Vector Component Node Inputs
text:
Vector
   The vector from which to retrieve a component.

Index
   Index of the component to retrieve:

   - **0:** X component.
   - **1:** Y component.
   - **2:** Z component.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/get_vector_component.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Project with Depth Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Project with Depth Node Project with Depth Node
text:
The *Project with Depth* node reconstructs a 3D position from normalized
screen coordinates and a depth value using the given transform and projection
matrices.

This is a lower-level version of the Screen Space to 3D
node that operates directly on projection data instead of a camera object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/project_with_depth.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Project with Depth Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Project with Depth Node Inputs
text:
Normalized
   Normalized screen-space coordinates.

   A value of (0, 0) corresponds to the bottom-left corner of the
   projected view and (1, 1) corresponds to the top-right corner.

Depth
   Depth of the point relative to the projection.

Projection
   Projection matrix used to reconstruct the position.

Transform
   Transformation matrix applied after reconstructing the position.

Clip Start
   Near clipping distance used by the projection.

Clip End
   Far clipping distance used by the projection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/project_with_depth.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Screen to 3D Space Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Screen to 3D Space Node Screen to 3D Space Node
text:
The *Screen to 3D Space* node reconstructs a 3D position from normalized
screen coordinates and a depth value relative to a camera.

This is the inverse operation of the 3D to Screen Space node.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/screen_space_to_3d.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Screen to 3D Space Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Screen to 3D Space Node Inputs
text:
Normalized
   Normalized screen-space coordinates.

   A value of (0, 0) corresponds to the bottom-left corner of the camera
   view and (1, 1) corresponds to the top-right corner.

Depth
   Depth of the point relative to the camera.

Camera
   Camera used to reconstruct the 3D position.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/screen_space_to_3d.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Cylindrical Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate Cylindrical Node Separate Cylindrical Node
text:
The *Separate Cylindrical* node converts a vector from Cartesian coordinates (X, Y, Z)
into cylindrical coordinates (R, Φ, Z) and outputs each component separately. It is the inverse of the
Combine Cylindrical node.

This node is useful for analyzing geometry or generating procedural effects that depend on
radial distance, angular position, or height -- for example, creating spiral deformations,
cylindrical gradients, or radial masks.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_cylindrical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Cylindrical Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate Cylindrical Node Inputs
text:
Vector
   The input vector to be converted from Cartesian to cylindrical coordinates.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_cylindrical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Cylindrical Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate Cylindrical Node Outputs
text:
R
   The radial distance from the origin in the X-Y plane.

Phi
   The angular position around the Z axis.

Z
   The vertical component of the input vector, corresponding directly to its Z coordinate.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_cylindrical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Spherical Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate Spherical Node Separate Spherical Node
text:
The *Separate Spherical* node converts a vector from Cartesian coordinates (X, Y, Z)
into spherical coordinates (R, Φ, Θ) and outputs each component separately.
It is the inverse of the Combine Spherical node.

Spherical coordinates describe a position in 3D space using radius, azimuth (horizontal angle),
and polar (vertical) angle. This representation is useful for procedural effects involving
rotational symmetry, spherical gradients, or direction-based transformations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_spherical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Spherical Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate Spherical Node Inputs
text:
Vector
   The input Cartesian vector to be converted into spherical coordinates.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_spherical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate Spherical Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate Spherical Node Outputs
text:
R
   The radial distance from the origin.

Phi
   The azimuthal angle (horizontal rotation) around the Z axis, measured in radians.

Theta
   The polar angle (vertical inclination) from the Z axis, measured in radians.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_spherical.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate XYZ Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Separate XYZ Node Separate XYZ Node
text:
The *Separate XYZ Node* splits a vector into its individual components.

Tip:

   To retrieve a vector component dynamically using an index,
   use the Get Vector Component node
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/separate_xyz.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform and Project Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Transform and Project Node Transform and Project Node
text:
The *Transform and Project* node transforms a 3D position and projects it
into normalized screen coordinates using the given transform and projection
matrices.

This is a lower-level version of the 3D to Screen Space
node that operates directly on projection data instead of a camera object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/transform_and_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform and Project Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Transform and Project Node Inputs
text:
Vector
   Position to project.

Transform
   Transformation matrix applied before projection.

Projection
   Projection matrix used to project the transformed position.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/transform_and_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Transform and Project Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Utilities > Vector Transform and Project Node Outputs
text:
Normalized
   Normalized screen-space coordinates.

   A value of (0, 0) corresponds to the bottom-left corner of the
   projected view and (1, 1) corresponds to the top-right corner.

Depth
   Depth of the transformed position relative to the projection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/vector/transform_and_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clip Grid Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Clip Grid Node Clip Grid Node
text:
The *Clip Grid* node restricts a voxel grid to a bounding box defined in
index space.

Voxels outside the specified minimum and maximum indices are deactivated
and their values are set to the grid's background value.

If a tile is partially inside the clipping bounds, it is fully voxelized
so that individual voxels can be clipped correctly.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/clip_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clip Grid Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Clip Grid Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input voxel grid to clip.

Min X
   Minimum X index of the clipping bounding box.

Min Y
   Minimum Y index of the clipping bounding box.

Min Z
   Minimum Z index of the clipping bounding box.

Max X
   Maximum X index of the clipping bounding box.

Max Y
   Maximum Y index of the clipping bounding box.

Max Z
   Maximum Z index of the clipping bounding box.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/clip_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clip Grid Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Clip Grid Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the grid (for example *Float*, *Integer*,
   *Boolean*, or *Vector*).
   Must match the data type of the input grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/clip_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clip Grid Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Clip Grid Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The clipped voxel grid with voxels outside the specified bounds
   deactivated and reset to the background value.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/clip_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deactivate Voxels Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Deactivate Voxels Node Deactivate Voxels Node
text:
The *Deactivate Voxels* node deactivates any active voxels or tiles of a grid where the *Selection*
field is *true*. The *Selection* field is evaluated at every voxel and tile position of the input
grid.

If *Set Background Value* is enabled the value of deactivated voxels is reset to the grid background
value. Otherwise the values of the output grid are unchanged, only the active state is changed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/deactivate_voxels.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deactivate Voxels Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Deactivate Voxels Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   A grid whose voxels will be deactivated based on the *Selection* field.

Selection
   Boolean field defining which voxels to deactivate.

Set Background Value
   If enabled all deactivated voxels will be set to the background value of the grid.

Note:

      Inactive voxels are usually invisible but still have values assigned, which can be accessed
      by sampling from the grid. To avoid unexpected behavior the value of deactivated voxels is
      reset to the background value by default.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/deactivate_voxels.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to Grid Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Field to Grid Node Field to Grid Node
text:
The *Field to Grid* node creates one or more new voxel grids by evaluating
geometry fields on the topology of an existing grid.
This allows generating new volumetric data (such as density, temperature,
velocity, or distance fields) directly from field inputs defined in the node
tree.

Each input field is sampled at the voxel positions of the provided topology
grid, producing a corresponding output grid that matches the same resolution,
transform, and domain.
This enables consistent evaluation of multiple attributes or procedural
quantities across the same volume structure.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/field_to_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to Grid Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Field to Grid Node Inputs
text:
Topology
   The reference grid whose voxel layout, resolution, and transform define
   where the input fields will be evaluated.

Additional input sockets can be added for each field to be evaluated.
Each field defines a scalar or vector value to sample on the topology grid.

Fields can be added by dragging them into the blank socket area.

Note:

   When a color field is connected, it will be evaluated as a *Vector* data
   type, since color grids are not currently supported.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/field_to_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to Grid Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Field to Grid Node Properties
text:
In the properties panel, each field input can be configured individually.
This includes setting its **data type** (such as *Float*, *Vector*, or *Boolean*)
and managing the order of evaluation.
Each field input produces a corresponding output grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/field_to_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Field to Grid Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Field to Grid Node Outputs
text:
For each field input, a separate grid output is created that contains the
evaluated voxel data.
All output grids share the same topology as the input grid, ensuring that
they are aligned and compatible for further processing or combination.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/field_to_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Dilate & Erode Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Dilate & Erode Node Grid Dilate & Erode Node
text:
The *Grid Dilate & Erode* node expands or contracts the active regions of a volume grid.
It modifies which voxels are considered active, without changing the stored voxel values.

This operation is commonly used to grow or shrink volume regions, fill small gaps,
remove noise, or adjust boundaries in volumetric data.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_dilate_erode.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Dilate & Erode Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Dilate & Erode Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the grid (e.g. *Float*, *Integer*, *Boolean*,
   *Vector*).
   Must match the type of the input grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_dilate_erode.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Dilate & Erode Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Dilate & Erode Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input volume grid whose active voxels are modified.

Connectivity
   Defines which neighboring voxels are considered connected during the operation.

   :Face:
      Use 6-connectivity, affecting only voxels connected by faces.
   :Edge:
      Use 18-connectivity, affecting voxels connected by faces or edges.
   :Vertex:
      Use 26-connectivity, affecting voxels connected by faces, edges, or vertices.

Tiles
   Controls how active tiles are handled during dilation or erosion.

   :Ignore:
      Ignore active tiles entirely.
      Tiles are neither modified nor contribute to the operation.
   :Expand:
      Convert active tiles to individual voxels, apply the operation,
      and leave the result fully voxelized.
   :Preserve:
      Keep tiles unchanged when possible, only performing voxelization when necessary.
      This option is more memory efficient.

Steps
   Number of times to apply the dilation or erosion operation.
   Higher values increase the distance the active region is expanded or contracted.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_dilate_erode.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Mean Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Mean Node Grid Mean Node
text:
The *Grid Mean* node applies a mean (box) filter to a volume grid.
For each active voxel, the value is replaced with the average of neighboring
voxels within a box-shaped region defined by the filter width.

This operation smooths voxel data and reduces high-frequency variations.
It is commonly used to soften density fields, smooth noise,
or prepare volume data for further processing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_mean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Mean Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Mean Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the grid (for example *Float*, *Integer*,
   or *Vector*). Must match the data type of the input grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_mean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Mean Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Mean Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input volume grid to smooth.

Width
   The filter kernel radius in voxels.
   Larger values increase the size of the neighborhood used for averaging,
   resulting in stronger smoothing.

Iterations
   Number of times the mean filter is applied.
   Higher values produce progressively smoother results.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_mean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Median Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Median Node Grid Median Node
text:
The *Grid Median* node applies a median (box) filter to a volume grid.
For each active voxel, the value is replaced with the median value of
neighboring voxels within a box-shaped region defined by the filter width.

Unlike the mean filter,
the median filter is more effective at preserving
sharp features and removing isolated noise or outliers.
It is commonly used to clean up sparse artifacts while maintaining edges
in density or level set volumes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_median.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Median Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Median Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the grid (for example *Float*, *Integer*,
   or *Vector*). Must match the data type of the input grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_median.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Median Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Median Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input volume grid to smooth.

Width
   The filter kernel radius in voxels.
   Larger values increase the size of the neighborhood considered,
   resulting in stronger smoothing.

Iterations
   Number of times the median filter is applied.
   Repeated iterations progressively increase the smoothing effect.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_median.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Solve Poisson Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Solve Poisson Node Grid Solve Poisson Node
text:
The *Grid Solve Poisson* node is an advanced math node for solving a wide range of problems in
geometry and physics simulation using 3D grids.

It solves `Poisson's equation <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson%27s_equation>`__, which relates
the value of each grid voxel to its neighbors using the
`Laplace operator <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace_operator>`__.

The Laplace operator computes the difference between a voxel and the average of its neighbors.
The node solves the *inverse* problem, reconstructing the original potential where applying the
Laplace operator produces the input grid again.

The solution to the Poisson equation is not unique, for example adding a constant to every voxel
results in the same difference from the neighborhood average (one *degree-of-freedom*). The solution
has as many degrees-of-freedom as there are boundary voxels. To fully define the solution the
*boundary conditions* at the edge of the solution space must also be specified.

The default boundary condition enforces a solution value of *zero* at the
boundary everywhere. Other modes allow enforcing custom fixed values
(`Dirichlet condition <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet_boundary_condition>`__),
or custom gradient values of the resulting function
(`Neumann condition <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neumann_boundary_condition>`__),
or a combination of both ("Mixed" boundary condition).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_solve_poisson.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Solve Poisson Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Solve Poisson Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   "Source" values on the right-hand side of the Poisson equation. The active voxels of the grid
   define the solution space.

Warning:

      The input grid must have a uniform voxel size (all components are the same).

Max Iterations
   Maximum number of iterations the solver will use.

Error Threshold
   Threshold below which the solution is considered valid. After each iteration the solver computes
   the maximum absolute residual error of all voxels and compares it to the threshold value.

Threshold Mode
   Defines how the *Error Threshold* is interpreted:

   :Relative:
      The error threshold is relative to the `maximum norm <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norm_(mathematics)#Maximum_norm_(special_case_of:_infinity_norm,_uniform_norm,_or_supremum_norm)>`__
      of the input grid, including boundary conditions. In the case that the norm is zero the
      relative error is used like an absolute error threshold.
   :Absolute:
      The solution error is compared directly to the error threshold value.

Boundary
   Mode that defines what boundary conditions to use for the solution:

   :Fixed:
      The solution must be equal to the specified *Boundary Value* at the boundary.
      This is equivalent to a Dirichlet boundary condition with a custom value.
   :Gradient:
      The gradient of the solution must be equal to the specified *Boundary Gradient* at the
      boundary. This is equivalent to a Neumann boundary condition with a custom vector value.
   :Mixed:
      Enforce both *Fixed* and *Gradient* conditions, using the *Boundary Factor* to mix between both.
      This can be used to apply different types of boundary conditions in different regions of the
      boundary.

      A typical use case is to distinguish between empty (air) cells and obstacles i
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_solve_poisson.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Solve Poisson Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Solve Poisson Node Outputs
text:
Solution
   The solution of the Poisson equation. The grid has the same topology (active voxels) as the input
   grid.

Success
   Single value indicating whether the solver succeeded or not.

Iterations
   Number of iterations used by the solver.

   If this matches the *Max Iterations* input (and the *Success* output is false) then
   the solver may require more iterations to compute a valid solution.

Absolute Error
   Maximum residual error of any solution voxel.

Relative Error
   Maximum residual error of any solution voxel, relative to the maximum norm of the input grid.

Debug
   Various debug outputs to help investigate potential issues.

   Boundary Value
      Grid values of the evaluated *Boundary Value* input field.
   Boundary Gradient
      Grid values of the evaluated *Boundary Gradient* input field.
   Boundary Factor
      Grid values of the evaluated *Boundary Factor* input field.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_solve_poisson.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Mesh Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Mesh Node Grid to Mesh Node
text:
The *Grid to Mesh* node converts a voxel grid into a polygonal mesh by
extracting an isosurface at a specified threshold value.
This process is similar to the *Marching Cubes* algorithm used in many
volumetric modeling systems.

The resulting mesh represents the boundary where the grid's values cross the
given threshold—typically the surface of a signed distance field (SDF) or density grid.
This makes it possible to convert procedural volumetric data into geometry for
rendering, simulation, or further modeling operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Mesh Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Mesh Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input voxel grid to convert into a mesh.
   The grid must store float values such as those from a signed distance or density field.

Threshold
   The value that defines the surface of the generated mesh.
   Voxels with values larger than this threshold are considered *inside* the
   mesh, while smaller values are considered *outside*.
   For SDF grids, a threshold of 0.0 typically corresponds to the surface.

Adaptivity
   Controls the simplification of the generated mesh based on curvature.
   Higher values reduce polygon count by merging nearly flat areas, while
   smaller values preserve more detail.
   A value of 0.0 disables adaptivity and produces a uniform mesh density.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Mesh Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Mesh Node Outputs
text:
Mesh
   The resulting mesh extracted from the grid's isosurface.
   The mesh follows the region where the grid's scalar values equal the
   specified *Threshold*, and can be used for further geometry processing or rendering.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Points Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Points Node Grid to Points Node
text:
The *Grid to Points* node converts a voxel grid into a point cloud.
Each active voxel or tile in the grid becomes a point.

The voxel value is stored as an anonymous attribute on the generated
points and is available as a field output. Additional information about
the voxel or tile is provided in index space.

This node is useful for creating custom visualizations of volume grids
or for further processing voxel data as points.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Points Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Points Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The data type stored in the grid (e.g. *Float*, *Integer*, *Boolean*, *Vector*).
   This determines the type of the *Value* output.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Points Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Points Node Outputs
text:
Points
   A point cloud containing one point for each active voxel or tile.

Value
   The value stored in the grid at each voxel.
   For tiles, this represents the shared value for all voxels in that tile.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid to Points Node > Voxel Index
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid to Points Node Voxel Index
text:
X
   The X coordinate of the voxel in index space,
   or the minimum X coordinate of a tile.

Y
   The Y coordinate of the voxel in index space,
   or the minimum Y coordinate of a tile.

Z
   The Z coordinate of the voxel in index space,
   or the minimum Z coordinate of a tile.

Is Tile
   True when the point represents a tile (multiple voxels)
   rather than a single voxel.

Extent
   The size of the voxel or tile.
   For individual voxels this is 1.
   For tiles this represents the cubic dimension of the tile in voxels.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_to_points.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Topology Boolean Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Topology Boolean Node Grid Topology Boolean Node
text:
The *Grid Topology Boolean* node combines the topology of active voxels and tiles of two or more
grids. The result is a grid with active voxels where at least one input grid has an active voxel,
depending on the *operation*.

The boolean combination happens in index space. All input grids should have the same grid transform,
otherwise the node will show a warning.

Conceptually this node is similar to the
SDF Grid Boolean node. Unlike
the SDF node it only takes active voxel state into account instead of signed distance values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_topology_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Topology Boolean Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Topology Boolean Node Inputs
text:
Grid 1
   The first input grid for boolean combination.
   The output grid uses voxel values of this grid, or its background value.

Grid 2
   The secondary input grids that are combined with *Grid 1*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_topology_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Topology Boolean Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Topology Boolean Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The data type stored in the grid (e.g. *Float*, *Integer*, *Boolean*, *Vector*).
   This determines the type of the *Grid* output.

Operation
   The boolean operation to perform between the input grids:

   :Intersection:
      Creates active voxels where all input grids have active voxels.
      The voxel value is the value of the first input grid.
   :Union:
      Creates active voxels where any input grid has an active voxel.
      The voxel value is the value of the first input grid, or its background value if the voxel is
      inactive in the first input grid.
   :Difference:
      Creates active voxel where the first input grid is active but none of the secondary input
      grids are active.
      The voxel value is the value of the first input grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_topology_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Grid Topology Boolean Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Grid Topology Boolean Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting grid after the boolean operation is applied.
   The grid values are the same as in the first input grid, using the background value for any
   newly added voxels in *Union* mode.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/grid_topology_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Prune Grid Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Prune Grid Node Prune Grid Node
text:
The *Prune Grid* node optimizes the storage of a voxel grid by collapsing
uniform regions into coarser tiles or inner nodes, reducing memory usage and
improving performance.

This node performs the inverse operation of the
Voxelize Grid node.
While voxelization expands sparse tiles into dense voxels, pruning
detects large uniform areas and replaces them with more compact representations.
This is especially useful after operations that create large
regions of constant values, such as filling, clipping, or thresholding.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/prune_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Prune Grid Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Prune Grid Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input grid to optimize.

Mode
   The pruning method used to simplify the grid structure:

   :Inactive:
      Turns inactive voxels and tiles into inactive background tiles.
      This is the simplest mode and provides basic cleanup for grids with
      empty or unused regions.

   :Threshold:
      Collapses regions where all voxels have approximately the same value and
      active state (within a given tolerance threshold) into background tiles.
      This is useful for fog or scalar grids where smooth variations may leave
      near-uniform areas that can be simplified.

   :SDF:
      Specialized mode for signed distance field (SDF) grids.
      Replaces inactive tiles with inactive nodes, providing faster and more
      targeted pruning without the need for threshold comparison.
      This mode is efficient for narrow-band SDFs that contain large interior
      or exterior regions of constant sign.

Threshold Threshold
   Voxels within a region are considered uniform if the difference between
   their values is less than this amount. Higher thresholds allow more
   aggressive simplification, while smaller values preserve finer details.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/prune_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Prune Grid Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Prune Grid Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the grid (e.g. *Float*, *Integer*, *Boolean*,
   *Vector*).
   Must match the type of the input grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/prune_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Prune Grid Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Prune Grid Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting grid with optimized storage. Uniform regions are collapsed
   into larger tiles or nodes, resulting in a more compact and efficient
   representation.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/prune_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Boolean Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Boolean Node SDF Grid Boolean Node
text:
The *SDF Grid Boolean* node performs boolean operations between two or more
**Signed Distance Field (SDF)** grids.
This allows combining, subtracting, or intersecting volumetric shapes directly
in grid space, similar to mesh boolean operations but with smooth and continuous results.

The node computes the resulting signed distance field by applying mathematical
operations to the input grids, preserving the SDF property where each voxel
stores the shortest distance to the nearest surface.
This makes it useful for blending or sculpting complex volumes procedurally.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Boolean Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Boolean Node Inputs
text:
Grid Intersect
   The input grids used for intersection operations.
   Only the regions common to all intersecting grids will remain active.

Grid Union
   The input grids used for union operations.
   All grid interior regions are added.

Grid 1 Difference
   The first input grid for boolean combination.
   Acts as the base grid from which the secondary grids are subtracted.

Grid 2 Difference
   The secondary input grids subtracted from *Grid 1*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Boolean Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Boolean Node Properties
text:
Operation
   The boolean operation to perform between the input SDF grids:

   :Intersect:
      Keeps only the overlapping region of the two grids where both contain
      interior (negative) values.
   :Union:
      Combines both grids by taking the minimum distance at each voxel.
      The resulting grid contains the merged shape of both inputs.
   :Difference:
      Subtracts the second grid from the first by inverting its sign and then
      taking the maximum distance.
      Useful for cutting holes or carving one SDF out of another.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Boolean Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Boolean Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid after the boolean operation is applied.
   The output maintains valid signed distance values and can be converted
   to a mesh using the Grid to Mesh
   node or used in further volumetric operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_boolean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Fillet Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Fillet Node SDF Fillet Node
text:
The *SDF Fillet* node smooths or rounds off concave internal corners in a Signed Distance Field (SDF) grid.
It modifies the field to produce softer transitions between surfaces that meet
at sharp inward angles, similar to adding a *fillet* or *bevel* in mesh modeling.

This operation only affects regions with **negative principal curvature**
(concave corners) and preserves overall volume. The result is a more organic
and continuous surface, useful for soft blending of intersecting shapes or
removing hard transitions after boolean operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_fillet.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Fillet Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Fillet Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input SDF grid to be smoothed.
   Typically generated from another SDF operation such as a boolean or mesh conversion.

Iterations
   The number of smoothing iterations to apply.
   Higher values produce a larger, smoother fillet radius but also increase computation time.
   A single iteration results in a subtle rounding, while multiple iterations
   create progressively softer surfaces.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_fillet.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Fillet Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Fillet Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid with concave corners rounded off.
   The output can be visualized by converting it to a mesh with
   Grid to Mesh or
   used in further volumetric operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_fillet.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Laplacian Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Laplacian Node SDF Grid Laplacian Node
text:
The *SDF Grid Laplacian* node applies Laplacian flow smoothing to a Signed Distance Field (SDF) grid.
This process gradually smooths the surface of the SDF by diffusing fine
details and noise across neighboring voxels, resulting in a cleaner, more uniform field.

Laplacian flow is a computationally efficient alternative to
mean curvature flow
smoothing. It is particularly useful for refining SDFs generated from
meshes or boolean operations, where sharp transitions or voxel artifacts may occur.
The operation helps improve the quality of surfaces before converting the SDF back into a mesh.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_laplacian.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Laplacian Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Laplacian Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input signed distance field to be smoothed.

Iterations
   The number of Laplacian smoothing iterations to apply.
   Each iteration progressively diffuses high-frequency surface variations,
   reducing surface noise.
   Higher values increase smoothness but may cause slight surface shrinkage.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_laplacian.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Laplacian Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Laplacian Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid after Laplacian flow smoothing.
   The output surface is smoother and more continuous, while preserving
   the main shape features of the original field.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_laplacian.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Mean Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Mean Node SDF Grid Mean Node
text:
The *SDF Grid Mean* node applies mean (box) filter smoothing to a Signed Distance Field (SDF) grid.
This operation averages voxel values within a local neighborhood to smooth
out small variations and noise while preserving the overall shape of the field.

The filter works as a fast, separable averaging operation—sometimes called a
*box filter*—and is well suited for general-purpose smoothing or softening of
SDF data after boolean, voxelization, or other volumetric operations.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_mean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Mean Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Mean Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input signed distance field to be smoothed.

Width
   The radius of the smoothing kernel in voxels.
   Larger values result in a broader smoothing effect, producing softer,
   less detailed surfaces. Smaller values restrict smoothing to immediate
   neighbors, retaining more fine detail.

Iterations
   The number of times the mean filter is applied.
   Each iteration increases the smoothness of the surface.
   Multiple passes can approximate a Gaussian-like blur effect.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_mean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Mean Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Mean Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid after mean filtering.
   The surface becomes smoother and more uniform, making it useful for
   refining noisy or rough SDFs before further operations such as
   Grid to Mesh.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_mean.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node
text:
The *SDF Grid Mean Curvature* node applies mean curvature flow smoothing to a Signed Distance Field (SDF) grid.
This operation evolves the surface of the field over time based on its mean curvature,
causing high-curvature (sharp or noisy) regions to smooth out more rapidly than flatter areas.

Unlike simple averaging or Laplacian smoothing, mean curvature flow adapts to
the geometric features of the surface, providing a more natural, shape-preserving
smoothing process. It can be used to refine complex SDF surfaces, remove small
artifacts, and create organically blended transitions between features.

This node is particularly effective after boolean operations or mesh-to-SDF
conversion, where the resulting fields may contain high-frequency noise.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_mean_curvature.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input signed distance field to smooth.
   Typically, the grid represents a surface or volume generated from a mesh or procedural operation.

Iterations
   The number of mean curvature flow iterations to apply.
   Each iteration progressively smooths the surface, with higher values
   resulting in a more pronounced smoothing effect.
   A small number of iterations will gently polish the surface, while
   larger values can significantly alter its shape.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_mean_curvature.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Mean Curvature Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid after mean curvature flow smoothing.
   The output surface has reduced high-curvature noise and smoother transitions,
   while retaining major structural features of the original shape.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_mean_curvature.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Median Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Median Node SDF Grid Median Node
text:
The *SDF Grid Median* node applies a median filter to a Signed Distance Field (SDF) grid.
This operation smooths the field by replacing each voxel value with the
median of its neighboring values, effectively removing noise and small
artifacts while preserving sharp features and edges.

Unlike mean
or Laplacian
smoothing, the median filter is non-linear and
better suited for cleaning up impulsive noise (isolated spikes or dips) in
the grid. It maintains the overall structure and boundaries of the surface,
making it useful for refining SDFs generated from noisy or voxelized meshes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_median.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Median Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Median Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input signed distance field to be filtered.

Width
   The radius of the median filter kernel, measured in voxels.
   Larger widths produce stronger smoothing by considering a wider
   neighborhood around each voxel.

Iterations
   The number of times the median filter is applied.
   Multiple iterations increase smoothing and noise reduction while
   maintaining edge sharpness.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_median.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Median Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Median Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid after median filtering.
   The output has reduced high-frequency noise and artifacts while
   retaining sharp edges and important structural details of the surface.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_median.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Offset Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Offset Node SDF Grid Offset Node
text:
The *SDF Grid Offset* node offsets the surface of a Signed Distance Field (SDF)
by a specified world-space distance.
This operation effectively dilates (expands) or erodes (contracts) the
surface while maintaining the correct signed distance values across the field.

A positive offset increases the surface thickness by pushing it outward,
while a negative offset shrinks it inward. This is a fundamental operation in
volumetric modeling, useful for adjusting wall thickness, creating shells,
expanding collision volumes, or controlling blend margins between shapes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_offset.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Offset Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Offset Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input signed distance field to offset.

Distance
   The offset distance applied to the surface, in world units.
   Positive values expand the surface (dilation), and negative values contract it (erosion).
   The offset is applied uniformly in all directions, preserving smoothness and the signed distance property.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_offset.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: SDF Grid Offset Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations SDF Grid Offset Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting SDF grid with the surface offset by the specified distance.
   The output preserves the SDF property, ensuring that distances remain
   accurate for subsequent operations such as booleans or conversion to a mesh.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/sdf_grid_offset.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Volume to Mesh Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Volume to Mesh Node Volume to Mesh Node
text:
The *Volume to Mesh* node generates a mesh on the "surface" of a volume.
The surface is defined by a threshold value.
All voxels with a larger value than the threshold are considered to be inside.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/volume_to_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Volume to Mesh Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Volume to Mesh Node Inputs
text:
Volume
   The volume geometry to convert.

Resolution Mode
   Mode for how the resolution of the final mesh is controlled.

   :Grid:
      This makes the resolution dependent on the resolution of the grid that is converted.
      Higher resolution grids result in a higher resolution mesh.
      In many cases, that is the most efficient mode.
   :Voxel Amount:
      Specifies the approximate resolution of the final mesh.
      The voxel size is adapted to the size of the entire volume.
   :Voxel Size:
      Use a fixed resolution that does not change when the volume changes.

Note:

      This option applies individually for every grid in the input geometry.

Voxel Amount
   Specifies the approximate resolution of the final mesh.
   The voxel size is adapted to the size of the entire volume.

Voxel Size
   Use a fixed resolution that does not change when the volume changes.

Threshold
   Voxels with a larger value are considered to be inside the mesh.
   The mesh will be generated on the boundary of inside and outside voxels.
   This is also called "iso value".

Adaptivity
   Reduces the final face count by simplifying geometry where detail is not needed.
   This is similar to decimating the final to reduce resolution where it is not needed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/volume_to_mesh.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Voxelize Grid Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Voxelize Grid Node Voxelize Grid Node
text:
The *Voxelize Grid* node converts all active tiles in a sparse voxel grid
into fully populated voxel regions, removing sparseness.

In voxel-based grids such as signed distance fields (SDF) or fog volumes,
inactive areas are often stored as *tiles*—compact representations that save
memory by not allocating individual voxel values. This node expands those tiles
into explicit voxels, making every voxel within an active tile directly
accessible and editable.

This can be useful before performing operations that require dense voxel data,
such as sampling, filtering, or arithmetic operations that depend on
neighboring voxel values.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/voxelize_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Voxelize Grid Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Voxelize Grid Node Inputs
text:
Grid
   The input grid to voxelize.
   Typically a sparse SDF or fog volume grid whose active tiles should be
   expanded into dense voxels.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/voxelize_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Voxelize Grid Node > Properties
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Voxelize Grid Node Properties
text:
Data Type
   The type of data stored in the grid (e.g. *Float*, *Integer*, *Boolean*, *Vector*).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/voxelize_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Voxelize Grid Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Operations Voxelize Grid Node Outputs
text:
Grid
   The resulting grid with all active tiles converted into individual voxels.

   For fog volumes, this means that interior sparse tiles are expanded into
   voxels with individually adjustable values. For SDF grids, this produces a
   fully dense voxel representation suitable for precise sampling and editing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/operations/voxelize_grid.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cube Grid Topology Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Primitives Cube Grid Topology Node Cube Grid Topology Node
text:
The *Cube Grid Topology* node generates a boolean grid topology
with the specified bounds and resolution.
This topology defines the voxel layout and active region and can be used with nodes such as
field to grid to construct volume grids.

The output topology contains active voxels within a regular, axis-aligned cube region.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/primitives/cube_grid_topology.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cube Grid Topology Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Primitives Cube Grid Topology Node Inputs
text:
Bounds Min
   The minimum world-space boundary of the grid.
   Defines the lower corner of the cube.

Bounds Max
   The maximum world-space boundary of the grid.
   Defines the upper corner of the cube.

Resolution X / Y / Z
   Number of voxels along the X, Y, and Z axes.
   Higher values increase detail and memory usage.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/primitives/cube_grid_topology.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cube Grid Topology Node > Min
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Primitives Cube Grid Topology Node Min
text:
X, Y, Z
   Minimum coordinate in grid index space.
   This defines the starting voxel index for each axis.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/primitives/cube_grid_topology.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Cube Grid Topology Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Primitives Cube Grid Topology Node Outputs
text:
Topology
   A boolean grid defining the grid topology and active region.
   Active voxels correspond to the cube defined by the bounds
   and resolution inputs.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/primitives/cube_grid_topology.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Volume Cube Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Primitives Volume Cube Node Volume Cube Node
text:
The *Volume Cube* generates a volume by evaluating a density field on a 3D grid.
The *Density* field can only depend on the position.
The grid points are equally spaced between the *Min* and *Max* bounds of the grid.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/primitives/volume_cube.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Volume Cube Node > Inputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Primitives Volume Cube Node Inputs
text:
Density
   The value for the new grid at each voxel.

Background
   The value of the grid outside the *Min*..*Max* grid bounds.
   Voxels with a density equal to the background are pruned, which can lead to more memory-efficient volumes.

Min
   Location of the left-most grid point and lower bound of the voxel volume.

Max
   Location of the right-most grid point and upper bound of the voxel volume.

Resolution X,Y,Z
   The number of grid points on each axis.
   The grid contains one less full voxel on each axis than there are grid points.
   For example a *Volume Cube* with resolution 10 has 9 voxels between the left and right grid points.

Note:

      Changing these values can have a significant impact on performance. For example, the default values
      of 32 mean the input field will be evaluated about 33 thousand times. Increasing the values to 100
      will give 1 million evaluations, and 1000 would give 1 billion.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/primitives/volume_cube.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Grid Names Node
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Read Get Grid Names Node Get Grid Names Node
text:
The *Get Grid Names* node retrieves the names of all grids stored in a volume
and outputs them as a list of strings.

A volume can contain multiple grids, each storing different types of volumetric data,
such as density, temperature, or velocity. This node can be used to inspect the
available grids or dynamically access them by name.

The grid names are returned in alphabetical order, matching the order used by OpenVDB
when loading VDB files.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/volume/read/get_grid_names.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Get Grid Names Node > Outputs
keywords: Modeling > Geometry Nodes > Volume > Read Get Grid Names Node Outputs
text:
Names
