   Positive values move inward relative to the face normals.
   Negative values move outward.

Seealso:

   The solidify does this non-destructively
   and has many more options.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/face/solidify_faces.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Triangles to Quads
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Face Triangles to Quads Triangles to Quads
text:
Shortcut:  Alt-J

Merges adjacent triangles in the selection into quads. This is essentially the opposite of
triangulate faces and can be run on a complete mesh in one go.

The operator uses angle thresholds to prevent creating malformed quads,
meaning that some triangles may remain.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/face/triangles_quads.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Triangles to Quads > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Face Triangles to Quads Options
text:
Max Face Angle
   The maximum allowed angle between triangle normals (that is, coplanar triangles are considered to have an
   angle of 0°, not 180°). Triangle pairs that exceed this limit will not be merged.
Max Shape Angle
   The maximum tolerance for non-rectangular quads. If this is set to 0°, only triangles that form a quad
   with perfect 90° corners will be merged. If set to 40°, corners between 50° and 130° are allowed, and so on.
Topology Influence
   How much to prefer creating new quads that match the topology of existing quads.

Tip:

      For best results, set Topology Influence between 100-130% and Max Angle to 180°.
      Lower values may leave behind parallelograms and triangles, while higher values may cause errors.
Compare UVs
   Don't merge triangles that are disjoint in any UV map.
Compare Color Attributes
   Don't merge triangles that, for any :ref:`Color Attribute
   <modeling-meshes-properties-object_data-color-attributes>`, have different colors at their shared edge.
Compare Seam
   Don't dissolve edges that are marked as UV Seams.
Compare Sharp
   Don't dissolve edges that are marked as Sharp.
Compare Materials
   Don't merge triangles that have different materials.
Deselect Joined
   Deselect the triangles that were successfully merged into quads.
   Useful for identifying the remaining triangles that still need to be converted.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/face/triangles_quads.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Triangulate Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Face Triangulate Faces Triangulate Faces
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-T

Converts each selected face (whether it's a quad or an n-gon) to triangular faces.
See the triangulate.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/face/triangulate_faces.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Weld Edges into Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Face Weld Edges into Faces Weld Edges into Faces
text:
Splits the selected faces along any selected wire edges (edges not part of any faces)
that share their vertices. The wire edges become part of the new faces.

Seealso:

   Instead of creating edges and then running this operator, it may be easier to use
   connect vertex path or the
   knife topology tool to split the faces directly.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/face/weld_edges_faces.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Wireframe
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Face Wireframe Wireframe
text:
Turns the selected faces into a wireframe by replacing their edges with tubes,
similar to the wireframe.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/face/wireframe.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bisect
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Bisect Bisect
text: The Bisect tool cuts the selected geometry in two using an infinitely large plane.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/bisect.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bisect > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Bisect Usage
text:
Orient the view so that the cutting plane will appear as a line (for example, the Top view
when cutting the mesh into left and right halves). Then activate the tool and drag the cutting
line using LMB. While dragging, the following shortcuts are available (also shown in
the status bar):

Move Spacebar
   Changes the location of the line.
Snap Ctrl
   Constrains the rotation of the line to 15 degree intervals.
Flip F
   Changes which side of the plane is seen as the "outer" side. This is later used with the
   *Fill* and *Clear Inner/Outer* options.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/bisect.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bisect > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Bisect Options
text:
After dragging the line, a yellow arrow shows the direction towards the "outer" side,
and the following options are available in the bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel:

Plane Point, Plane Normal
   The plane can be numerically adjusted for precise values.
Fill
   Create new faces along the cutting plane to cover up any holes left by *Clear Inner/Outer*.
   Materials, UV coordinates, and Color Attributes are assigned based on the surrounding geometry.
Clear Inner/Outer
   Delete any geometry on the "inner"/"outer" side of the cutting plane. Note that this also
   affects geometry that was not originally selected.
Axis Threshold
   Any vertices closer to the cutting plane than this threshold will be reused.
   For the rest of the mesh, new vertices and edges are created.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/bisect.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Delete Loose
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Delete Loose
text:
Deletes the selected vertices, edges, and optionally faces that aren't connected
to anything.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Decimate Geometry
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Decimate Geometry
text:
Reduces the face count of the selected geometry while minimizing shape changes.

Ratio
   The target triangle count ratio. For example, enter 0.4 to keep collapsing edges
   until the triangle count is 40% of the original.
Vertex Group
   Use the active vertex group when choosing which edges to collapse.
   The higher the vertex weights for an edge, the more likely it is to be chosen,
   even taking priority over "better" (shorter) candidates.

   Weight
      Factor by which to multiply the vertex weights.
   Invert
      Inverts the vertex weights, making edges with *lower* weights get collapsed first.
Symmetry
   Maintain symmetry on either the *X*, *Y*, or *Z* axis.

Seealso:

   The decimate in *Collapse* mode
   performs the same operation non-destructively.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Degenerate Dissolve
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Degenerate Dissolve
text:
Collapses any selected edges that are shorter than a certain length.
This also results in the removal of small faces.

If two vertices are near to each other but are not connected by an edge,
they will not be merged; see Merge By Distance
for an alternative.

Merge Distance
   Edges shorter than this length will be collapsed.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Make Planar Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Make Planar Faces
text:
Flattens the selected faces.

Factor
   The flattening strength for each iteration. Note that even a value of 1 may not be enough to
   get faces perfectly flat -- increase the *Iterations* in that case.
Iterations
   Number of times to repeat the operation.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Split Non-Planar Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Split Non-Planar Faces
text:
Splits any selected faces that are bent beyond a given limit.

Max Angle
   Faces that are bent by more than this angle will be split.

Hint:

   You can use bpy.ops.mesh.edge_rotate if you'd rather have certain
   newly created edges point in a different direction.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Merge by Distance
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Merge by Distance
text:
Merges the selected vertices that are closer to each other than a certain distance.

Merge Distance
   Vertices closer than this distance will be merged.
Unselected
   Allow merging selected vertices with unselected ones.
Sharp Edges
   If the mesh uses smooth shading and has
   custom split normals, this option will add
   edge marks where needed so that sharp edges will
   remain sharp after merging.

Seealso:

   The bpy.types.WeldModifier performs this operation non-destructively.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Clean Up > Fill Holes
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Clean Up Fill Holes
text:
Fills each hole in the selected geometry with a face.

Sides
   The maximum number of sides: if a hole has more edges than this number,
   it will not be filled. Set to 0 to fill all holes.

Seealso:

   For filling a large hole that has many edges,
   Face Fill or
   grid fill may be a better option.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/cleanup.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Convex Hull
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Convex Hull Convex Hull
text:
Creates a convex hull surrounding the selected vertices.
Original edges and faces that lie on this hull may be reused.

This operator can also serve as an alternative for
bridge edge loops.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/convex_hull.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Convex Hull > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Convex Hull Options
text:
Delete Unused
   Removes vertices, edges, and faces that were selected, but not used as part of the hull.
   Note that vertices and edges that are used
   by other edges and faces not part of the selection will not be deleted.

Use Existing Faces
   Where possible, use existing faces that lie on the hull.
   This allows the hull to contain n-gons rather than just triangles and quads.

Make Holes
   Delete edges and faces that were reused.
   Useful in cases like bridging to delete faces between the existing mesh and the convex hull.

Join Triangles
   The hull is initially generated using only triangles; this option tries to join them into quads.
   Has all the same properties as the bpy.ops.mesh.tris_convert_to_quads
   operator (angle limit, compare UVs, etc.).

Max Face Angle, Max Shape Angle, Compare
   See bpy.ops.mesh.tris_convert_to_quads.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/convex_hull.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Delete
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Delete
text:
Shortcut:  X or Delete

Deletes the selected mesh elements. The following menu items are available:

Vertices
   Deletes the selected vertices, as well as any edges and faces they are part of.
Edges
   Deletes the selected edges, as well as any faces they are part of.
   Orphaned vertices are deleted too.
Faces
   Deletes the selected faces. Orphaned vertices and edges are deleted too.
Only Edges & Faces
   Deletes the selected edges and faces, as well as any unselected faces that
   contain a selected edge. Orphaned vertices are left behind.
Only Faces
   Deletes the selected faces. Orphaned vertices and edges are left behind.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Dissolve
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Dissolve
text:
*Dissolving* is different from deleting in that it keeps the surface closed
rather than leaving a hole.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Dissolve Vertices
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Dissolve Vertices
text:
Shortcut:  X, Delete, or Ctrl-X

Deletes each selected vertex and joins its surrounding faces into one. (This often results in
n-gons.)

If a vertex is part of a wire -- that is, a chain of edges that are not part of any face --
its surrounding edges are merged instead.

The bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel offers the following options:

Face Split
   Split surrounding faces where possible so that only a triangle in their corner is merged instead of
   the whole face. This reduces the size of the final "hole-filling" faces and can make them less uneven.
Tear Boundaries
   Delete faces at the mesh boundary instead of merging them. These faces are always split,
   even if *Face Split* is disabled.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Dissolve Edges
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Dissolve Edges
text:
Shortcut:  X, Delete, or Ctrl-X

Deletes each selected edge and joins its surrounding faces into one. This is only done for edges that
have exactly two neighboring faces.

The Adjust Last Operation panel offers the following options:

Dissolve Vertices
   Also dissolve the vertices of the selected edges, not just the edges themselves.
Angle Threshold
   If *Dissolve Vertices* is enabled, this option allows preserving vertices at corners,
   only dissolving the ones in flattish areas. Faces are considered to form a corner if
   the angle between their *normals* exceeds the Angle Threshold -- that is, coplanar faces
   are considered to have an angle of 0°, not 180°.
Face Split
   Split surrounding faces where possible so that only a triangle in their corner is merged instead of
   the whole face. This reduces the size of the final "hole-filling" faces and can make them less uneven.
Preserve Quads
   Prevents vertices from being removed if doing so would break the quad structure
   when dissolving the edge between two triangles.

   Even if *Dissolve Vertices* is enabled, vertices shared by the two triangles
   are kept so the resulting geometry remains a quad rather than collapsing
   into a triangle or n-gon.

   This option helps maintain clean quad topology when simplifying meshes or
   removing unnecessary edges.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Dissolve Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Dissolve Faces
text:
Shortcut:  X, Delete, Ctrl-X, or F

Merges each patch of connected faces into a single face.

Note:

   The F shortcut is normally used for creating faces, but when run on a selection of existing faces,
   it dissolves them instead. See modeling-mesh-make-face-edge-dissolve.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Limited Dissolve
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Limited Dissolve
text:
Shortcut:  X or Delete

Simplifies the selected geometry by dissolving vertices and edges in flattish areas.

Max Angle
   The maximum allowed angle between faces for the surface to be considered flat (and thus eligible
   for dissolving). Specifically, the angle is measured between face normals, meaning that coplanar
   faces are considered to have an angle of 0°, not 180°.
All Boundaries
   After dissolving the edges using *Max Angle*, dissolve all vertices at boundary corners --
   specifically, vertices that only have two neighboring edges.
Delimit
   Prevent merging faces that are discontinuous in some way. It's possible to activate multiple of
   these options by clicking them with Shift-LMB.

   :Normal: Don't merge faces that have opposite
            orientations.
   :Material: Don't merge faces that have different materials.
   :Seam: Don't dissolve edges that are marked as UV Seams.
   :Sharp: Don't dissolve edges that are marked as Sharp.
   :UVs: Don't merge faces that are disconnected in any UV map.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Collapse Edges & Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Collapse Edges & Faces
text:
Shortcut:  X or Delete

Collapses each patch of connected edges and faces into a single vertex.
This is useful for collapsing edge rings, for example.

Unlike the *Dissolve* operators, this operator doesn't create n-gons
and can add new vertices instead of only removing existing ones. In addition,
the new vertices automatically receive interpolated UV coordinates, color attributes, etc.
This makes it particularly useful for manually removing detail.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Deleting & Dissolving > Edge Loops
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Deleting & Dissolving Edge Loops
text:
Shortcut:  X or Delete

Dissolves the selected edge loops. This is essentially the same as
bpy.ops.mesh.dissolve_edges, except that it selects the surrounding faces afterwards.

Note:

   In Blender terminology, an *edge loop* is any chain of connected edges --
   it doesn't have to be a closed loop. See bpy.ops.mesh.loop_select.

Seealso:

   - Vertex merging
   - triangles quads
   - unsubdivide
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/delete.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Duplicate
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Duplicate Duplicate
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-D

Creates a copy of the selection. After clicking the menu item or pressing the keyboard
shortcut, move the mouse to move the copy to the desired location and press LMB or Return
to confirm. Alternatively, press RMB or Esc to leave the copy at the same
location as the original. (The copy will still be selected, so it can still be easily moved out
of the way afterwards.)
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/duplicate.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Extrude Extrude
text:
Shortcut:  Alt-E

The available operators in this menu depend on the current selection.
Many of them are also available in the Vertex,
Edge, and Face menus.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/extrude.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Extrude > Extrude Repeat
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Extrude Extrude Repeat
text:
Repeatedly extrudes the selection along the current viewing direction, away from the
current viewpoint. Works best when using a top or side view
or a custom viewing direction with orthographic projection.

Steps
   Number of extrusions.
Offset X, Y, Z
   Distance between each extrusion.
Scale Offset
   Multiplication factor for the *Offset*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/extrude.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Project
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Project Knife Project
text:
Projects the outline of one or more "cookie cutter" objects onto the edited object and creates
new edges there.

The cutter objects must be Curves or non-manifold
meshes (e.g. flat shapes, loose edges).

Tip:
   Select Non-Manifold will highlight the cutting edges
   of mesh objects.

Projection is done along the viewing direction.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Project > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Project Usage
text:
#. Select the object(s) that should receive the cut and switch to *Edit Mode*.
#. Select the object(s) that should perform the cut by clicking them with Ctrl-LMB in the
   3D Viewport or the Outliner.
#. Click Mesh > Knife Project in the menu.

If Blender switches back to *Object Mode* when selecting the cutting objects,
make sure that Edit > Lock Object Modes is checked in the topbar.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Project > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Project Options
text:
Cut Through
   Projects the cut through the entire mesh, including back faces not currently visible.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Project > Known Limitations
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Project Known Limitations
text:
When cutting multiple meshes in Edit Mode at once,
geometry from these meshes does not occlude separate mesh objects behind them.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_project.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Topology Tool
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Topology Tool Knife Topology Tool
text:
Shortcut:  K

The Knife tool allows to interactively "cut through" faces,
subdividing them and creating a chain of new edges along the way.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_topology_tool.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Topology Tool > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Topology Tool Usage
text:
First, select the tool in the Toolbar or press K. The cursor
will change into a scalpel to indicate it's active.

Click LMB at the place where you want to start cutting.
This can be anywhere: on an existing vertex, edge, or face,
or even outside of the mesh.

Move your mouse to the next location. You'll see a yellow line indicating
the new edges that will be created, and aqua dots indicating the new
vertices. Click LMB to confirm and start on the next cutting segment.

Once you're done, press Spacebar or Return to apply the cuts.
Alternatively, press Esc to cancel.

Hint:

   By using 3dview-multi-object-mode, you can cut multiple objects
   at the same time.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_topology_tool.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Topology Tool > Tool Settings
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Topology Tool Tool Settings
text:
These settings are only available when using the tool from the Toolbar
(not when pressing K). They can be found in the *Tool* tab of the
properties editor editor and of the Sidebar.

Occlude Geometry
   Only cut geometry visible on screen. By disabling this, you can cut all the way
   through the mesh, including faces that are on the backside or behind others.

Only Selected
   Only cut through selected geometry. You can press Shift-K instead of
   K to start cutting with this option enabled.

X-Ray
   Show the cutting path even if it's occluded by geometry.

Measurements
   The measurements to show along the cutting path: distances, angles, or both.

Angle Snapping
   Whether to constrain the cutting lines to multiples of the *Snap Increment* angle.

   :None: No snapping.
   :Screen: Snap in screen space (the viewing plane).
   :Relative: Snap in a plane on the geometry, relative to an adjacent edge or cutting line.

Snap Increment
   The angle to use for *Angle Snapping*.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_topology_tool.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Topology Tool > Controls
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Topology Tool Controls
text:
These keyboard shortcuts are shown in the
status bar while cutting.
They're available both when using the tool from the Toolbar and when pressing K.

Cut LMB
   You can either click to add a new cutting line, or drag to create cutting lines
   as you move the mouse over edges.

Close Loop - Double-click LMB
   Adds a cutting point at the cursor (just like when single-clicking) and then connects
   it to the first point in the current path, closing the loop.

Stop RMB
   Completes the current cutting path and begins a new one. The cursor will snap to previously
   defined cuts.

Confirm Spacebar or Return
   Confirms the cut, turning the cutting paths into edges.

Cancel Esc
   Cancels the cut.

Undo Ctrl-Z
   Undoes the previous cutting line (or, if you dragged the mouse before, all the cutting
   lines created during that drag).

Midpoint Snap Shift
   Hold to snap the cursor to the center of edges.

Ignore Snap Ctrl
   Hold to temporarily stop the cursor from snapping to existing vertices, edges,
   and cutting lines.

Cut Through C
   Also cut through occluded faces, instead of only the visible ones.
   This is linked to (and the opposite of) the *Occlude Geometry* setting above.

Axis X, Y, or Z
   Constrains the current cutting line to a global axis. Press a second time to use the
   object's local axis, and a third time to disable the constraint again.

Measure S
   Cycles between measurements to show: distances, angles, or both.

X-Ray V
   Toggles whether to display cuts occluded by geometry.

Angle Constraint A
   Constrains cutting lines to multiples of the *Snap Increment* angle. This angle
   can be specified in the Tool Settings before cutting (see above) or typed
   while cutting with *Angle Constraint* active.

   By default, the snapping is done in the *
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_topology_tool.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Knife Topology Tool > Duplicate Vertices
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Knife Topology Tool Duplicate Vertices
text:
If a cut creates duplicate vertices, this is often caused by the clipping range
being too large. Try increasing the Clip Start
to avoid this problem.
Also see Depth Troubleshooting for details.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/knife_topology_tool.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Merge Merge
text:
Context Menu > Merge
   Shortcut:  M

Merges the selected vertices together. The menu has the following options:

At Center
   Merge all selected vertices into one vertex placed at their geometric center
   (i.e. the average of their positions, not their bounding box center).
At Cursor
   Merge all selected vertices into one vertex placed at the 3d cursor.
Collapse
   Merge each island of connected vertices into one vertex placed at the average position.
At First
   Merge all selected vertices into the one that was selected first.
   Only available in the *Vertex* selection mode.
At Last
   Merge all selected vertices into the one that was selected last.
   Only available in the *Vertex* selection mode.
By Distance
   Merge each cluster of vertices that are closer to each other than a certain distance.

Note:

   *At First* and *At Last* depend on the selection order which is easily lost (e.g. by
   changing the selection mode). They should typically be run right after making the selection.

Seealso:

   The weld merges vertices by distance non-destructively.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/merge.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Merge > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Merge Options
text:
After merging, the following options are available in the bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel:

Type
   The type of merge to perform.
UVs
   Corrects the UV coordinates to avoid texture distortion.

*Merge By Distance* instead has the following options:

Merge Distance
   Vertices closer than this distance will be merged.
Centroid Merge
   Place each new vertex at the average position of the vertices that were merged together.
   When disabled, the position of the original vertex closest to this average is used.
Unselected
   Allow merging selected vertices with unselected ones.
Sharp Edges
   If the mesh uses smooth shading and has
   custom split normals, this option will add
   edge marks where needed so that sharp edges will
   remain sharp after merging.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/merge.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mirror > Interactive Mirror
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Mirror Interactive Mirror
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-M

The *Mirror* operator flips the selected elements around the
Pivot Point along an axis of the
Transformation Orientation.
Mirroring is equivalent to scaling the selection by -1 along the selected axis,
but it offers a faster and more direct workflow.

Hint:

   After mirroring a mesh, the face normals tend to get flipped inside out
   (see the bpy.types.View3DOverlay.show_face_orientation overlay).
   The Flip Normals operator can fix this.

Seealso:

   - The symmetrize operator creates a mirrored
     copy of the mesh.
   - The mirror creates a mirrored copy that's
     automatically kept up to date.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/mirror.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mirror > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Mirror Usage
text:
#. Place the pivot point at the desired mirror location.
#. When not mirroring along a global axis, ensure the transform orientation has an axis
   pointing along the desired mirror direction (perpendicular to the mirror plane).
#. Press Ctrl-M to activate the *Mirror* operator.
#. Choose an axis by dragging with MMB or by pressing X, Y, or Z.
   (The chosen axis is shown at the top of the 3D Viewport.) Press an axis key a second
   time to toggle between the transform orientation axis and the global axis.
#. Press LMB or Return to confirm, or RMB or Esc to cancel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/mirror.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mirror > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Mirror Options
text:
Orientation
   The transform orientation to take the *Constraint Axis* from.

Constraint Axis
   The axis (or axes) to mirror across.
   For example, mirroring across the X axis flips the selection horizontally.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/mirror.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mirror > X/Y/Z Global
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Mirror X/Y/Z Global
text: These operations perform a non-interactive mirror along the global X, Y, or Z axis.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/mirror.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mirror > X/Y/Z Local
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Mirror X/Y/Z Local
text: These operations perform a non-interactive mirror along the object's local X, Y, or Z axis.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/mirror.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mirror > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Mirror Examples
text:
Mirroring along the global X axis around the object origin:

Mirroring around the 3d cursor:
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/mirror.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Editing Normals
text:
The *Normals* menu can be accessed as a popover by pressing Alt-N.

Most of the operators in this menu work with custom split normals,
which are normal vectors that belong to face corners (not vertices). Selecting these corners can be done in
multiple ways:

- If the selection mode is set to *Vertex* or *Edge*, selecting a
  vertex or edge also selects the nearest corners of the faces it's part of.
- If the selection mode is *Face*, selecting a face also selects its corners.
- If both the *Vertex* and *Face* modes are enabled, selecting a vertex and then adding a face
  will select just the matching face corner.
- Similar to the above, if both the *Edge* and *Face* modes are enabled, selecting an edge and
  then adding a face will select just the two matching face corners.

Seealso:

   - The 3D Viewport overlay for visualizing normals.
   - The custom data panel of the mesh properties for
     clearing custom normals.
   - Mesh Data Transfer (operator
     or modifier) for copying normals from
     another mesh.
   - The normal edit and the
     weighted normal for calculating or changing normals
     based on certain criteria.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Flip
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Flip
text:
Changes the orientation of the selected faces, turning their "front side" into their
"back side" and vice versa. This does not affect custom split normals.

The 3D Viewport's bpy.types.View3DOverlay.show_face_orientation overlay is useful for quickly
spotting faces that are oriented the wrong way.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Recalculate
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Recalculate
text:
Mesh > Normals > Recalculate Inside
   Shortcut:  Shift-N and Shift-Ctrl-N

Flips the orientation of the selected faces where necessary, making them all point outward (or inward).
The mesh does not need to be a closed volume for this.

As with `Flip`_, this operation does not affect custom split normals.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Set from Faces
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Set from Faces
text:
Sets the custom split normals of each selected vertex to the average normal of its surrounding
selected faces.

Keep Sharp Edges
   When checked, face corners that are part of a Sharp edge will
   keep their original custom normal.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Rotate
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Rotate
text:
Shortcut:  R followed by N

Tool for rotating the custom split normals of the selected face corners by moving the mouse.
Click LMB to confirm or RMB to cancel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Point to Target
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Point to Target
text:
Shortcut:  Alt-L

Makes the custom split normals of the selected face corners point at a certain target.
After clicking the menu item or pressing the keyboard shortcut, choose the target by
pressing one of the following keys (also shown in the status bar):

- M for the mouse cursor.
- L for the Pivot Point.
- O for the object origin.
- Ctrl-LMB for the 3d cursor. This also changes the location of the Cursor.
- Ctrl-RMB for a certain vertex, edge, or face. Make sure not to click a space where there's no geometry,
  as doing so will extrude the selection instead.

In addition, the following options are available:

Invert I
   Make the normals point away from the target instead.
Align A
   All normals will point in the same direction: from the average position of the selected vertices
   to the target.
Spherize S
   Interpolate between each normal's original and new orientation. The interpolation value can be set
   in the bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel after confirming the operator.
Reset R
   Reset the custom normals to what they were when the operation started.

After configuring the normals, press LMB or Return to confirm. The above options can
then still be changed in the Adjust Last Operation panel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Merge
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Merge
text:
Applies smooth shading to the selected faces and clears the
Sharp mark for the selected edges. Then, at each selected vertex,
sets the custom normals that are part of a smooth-shaded face to their average orientation.
(Custom normals that are part of a flat-shaded face are left unchanged.)

To average the custom normals regardless of face selection, use the bpy.ops.mesh.average_normals
operator.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Split
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Split
text:
Applies flat shading to the selected faces and marks the selected
edges as Sharp. Then, at each selected vertex, sets each custom normal
that's part of a flat-shaded face to the normal of that face. (Custom normals that are part of a
smooth-shaded face are set to the average of the normals of those faces.)
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Average
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Average
text:
For each selected vertex, divides the connected face corners into groups based on :ref:`Sharp
<bpy.ops.mesh.mark_sharp>` edges, then sets the custom normals of the face corners in each group to a certain average.
The bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel has the following options:

Type
   :Custom Normal: Set the custom normals of the face corners in each group to their average.
   :Face Area: Set the custom normals of the face corners in each group to a weighted average of their
       face normals. The weights are determined by face area: larger faces have more influence on the final normal.
   :Corner Angle: Like *Face Area*, except the weights are determined by the face corner angles.
Weight
   If the *Type* is set to *Face Area* or *Corner Angle*, the *Weight* influences which face normals the
   averaged normal leans towards. If it's 50, a simple weighted average is used. If it's 100, the averaged normal
   is based solely on the faces with the largest area (or corners with the largest angle).
   If it's 1, the normal is based solely on the faces with the smallest area (or corners with the smallest angle).
Threshold
   Tolerance value for treating face areas (or corner angles) as equal.

Seealso:

   The weighted normal does this non-destructively.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Copy Vector
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Copy Vector
text:
Copies a single normal vector to an internal clipboard:

- If a face is selected, its normal is copied.
- If a vertex is selected, its normal is copied, but only if all its custom split normals are the same.
- If a face corner is selected, its custom split normal is copied.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Paste Vector
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Paste Vector
text:
Pastes the previously copied normal vector onto the selected face corners.
The bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel has the following option:

Absolute Coordinates
   When enabled, sets the custom split normals of the selected face corners to the
   pasted normal. When disabled, adds the pasted normal as an offset.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Smooth Vectors
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Smooth Vectors
text:
Smooths out the custom normals of each selected vertex by averaging with
the normals at neighboring vertices. The bpy.ops.screen.redo_last
panel has the following option:

Factor
   Smoothing strength. Specifically, this is the interpolation value between
   the original normals and the averaged ones.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Select by Face Strength
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Select by Face Strength
text:
Selects the faces that have a specific *Strength* (Weak, Medium, or Strong)
and deselects the others.

This property is used by the weighted normal
if its *Face Influence* setting is enabled.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Editing Normals > Set Face Strength
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Editing Normals Set Face Strength
text:
Sets the *Strength* of the selected faces to Weak, Medium, or Strong.
By default, all faces have a strength of Medium.

This property is used by the weighted normal
if its *Face Influence* setting is enabled.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/normals.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Separate > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Separate Options
text:
Selection
   Disconnects the selected geometry from its surroundings and moves it into a new object.
By Material
   Splits the mesh into an object per material slot,
   each containing the faces using that material slot. This is done for the whole mesh regardless
   of the selection.
By Loose Parts
   Creates an object for every independent (disconnected) piece of the original mesh.
   This is done for the whole mesh regardless of the selection.

Seealso:

   - bpy.ops.mesh.split for disconnecting geometry without moving it into a new object.
   - join for merging multiple objects into one.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/separate.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Set Attribute
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Set Attribute Set Attribute
text:
Opens a pop-up window showing the name of the active attribute
as well as the value of that attribute for the active element (vertex/edge/face).
From there, you can change the value to apply it to all selected elements.

The "active" attribute is the one last selected in the
Data tab of the properties editor editor.
It could be a UV Map,
a Color Attribute,
or a generic Attribute.

Seealso:

   Attribute values can be viewed in the spreadsheet editor.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/set_attribute.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shading > Smooth/Sharp Vertices
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Shading Smooth/Sharp Vertices
text:
Clears or applies the Sharp mark for
all edges that have at least one selected vertex.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/shading.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Snap to Symmetry
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Snap to Symmetry Snap to Symmetry
text:
The *Snap to Symmetry* operator gives perfect symmetry to a mesh that was only approximately
symmetrical before. Unlike symmetrize, which deletes
one half of the mesh and mirrors the other, *Snap to Symmetry* matches up pairs of vertices
based on their position, then repositions them.

This is useful after, for example, moving a few vertices while accidentally having
Mesh Symmetry disabled.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/snap_symmetry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Snap to Symmetry > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Snap to Symmetry Options
text:
Direction
   The axis and direction of the effect, in the object's local space.
   For example, *-X to +X* goes over vertices to the left of the
   object origin (negative X coordinate)
   and matches them up with vertices on the right (positive X coordinate).
Threshold
   The search radius for finding matching vertices.
Factor
   When set to 1, both vertices in each matching pair receive the position of the vertex on the "from"
   side of the *Direction*. When set to 0, both receive the position of the vertex on the "to" side.
   Other values result in interpolation: with a value of 0.5, for example, both vertices are
   moved to their averaged position.
Center
   Move vertices that are near the symmetry plane so they're exactly on that plane (by setting their
   coordinate for the *Direction* axis to zero).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/snap_symmetry.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sort Elements
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Sort Elements Sort Elements
text:
Changes the internal storage order of the selected mesh elements.

Hint:

   To see the storage indices of the selected elements, first ensure the
   bpy.types.PreferencesView.show_developer_ui option is enabled in the Preferences,
   then enable the bpy.types.View3DOverlay.show_extra_indices overlay in the 3D Viewport.

View Z Axis
   Sort along the active view's Z axis, from farthest to nearest.
View X Axis
   Sort along the active view's X axis, from left to right.
Cursor Distance
   Sort by distance from the 3d cursor, from nearest to farthest.
Material
   Sort faces by their material slot index, from lowest
   to highest. The order of faces within each "material group" remains unchanged.
Selected
   Move all selected elements to the beginning (without affecting their relative order).
   Warning: This will also affect the indices of **unselected** elements!
Randomize
   Randomize the order of the selected elements.
Reverse
   Reverse the order of the selected elements.

The bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel has the following options:

Type
   The sort order as described above.
Elements
   Whether to sort vertices, edges, or faces. This is initially determined by the
   current selection mode.
Reverse
   Sort in the opposite order than the default one.
Seed
   When using *Randomize*, changing the seed will result in a different order.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/sort_elements.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Split Split
text:
The *Split* menu can be accessed as a popover by pressing Alt-M.

These operators are about splitting meshes by disconnecting faces from each other.
For splitting faces into smaller ones, see the knife topology tool
or the connect vertex path operator.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/split.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split > Split Selection
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Split Split Selection
text:
Shortcut:  Y

Cuts the mesh along the border of the selected faces. The faces can then be moved elsewhere.

This operator can also disconnect "wires" (edges that are not part of a face) from
their surroundings. However, using it on edges that *are* part of a face will simply duplicate them.

Seealso:

   The separate operator disconnects the selection
   and moves it into a new mesh object.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/split.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split > Split Faces by Edges
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Split Split Faces by Edges
text:
Cuts the mesh along the selected edges. The vertices can then be pulled apart to create a hole.

Seealso:

   rip vertices also cuts neighboring unselected edges.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/split.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Split > Split Faces & Edges by Vertices
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Split Split Faces & Edges by Vertices
text:
Cuts the mesh along *all* neighboring edges of each selected vertex. (This is different from
*Rip Vertices* which only cuts two edges per vertex.)

The vertices can then be pulled apart to create a hole.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/split.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Symmetrize
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Symmetrize Symmetrize
text:
The *Symmetrize* operator is a quick way to make a mesh symmetrical.
It does the following:

#. Cuts the selected geometry at the origin
   of the object using an infinite plane, much like
   bisect.
#. Deletes the geometry on one side of the plane.
#. Copies the geometry on the other side of the plane and mirrors it.
#. Merges the vertices that lie on the plane.

Seealso:

   - Mesh Symmetry continuously
     maintains symmetry while editing the mesh.
   - The mirror symmetrizes the mesh
     non-destructively.
   - The mirror operator simply flips the
     mesh without cutting or copying.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/symmetrize.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Symmetrize > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh Symmetrize Options
text:
Direction
   The axis and direction of the effect, in the object's local space.
   For example, *-X to +X* deletes the geometry that's to the right of the
   object origin (positive X coordinate) and replaces it by a mirrored copy
   of the geometry on the left (negative X coordinate).
Threshold
   The vertices in this range will be snapped to the plane of symmetry.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/symmetrize.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Move, Rotate, Scale
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Move, Rotate, Scale Move, Rotate, Scale
text:
Shortcut:  G, R, S

Move G, rotate R, or scale S the selected vertices, edges, or faces.
This can also be done using the transform gizmos.

Seealso:

   - Manipulation in 3D Space
   - orientation
   - index

These transformations are affected by proportional editing.

Pressing G twice will instead activate
Vertex Slide
or Edge Slide depending on the selection.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/basic.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Move, Rotate, Scale > Transform Panel
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Move, Rotate, Scale Transform Panel
text:
This panel shows the properties of the selected vertex or edge.
If more than one item is selected, it shows the average of their properties instead.

X/Y/Z
   The coordinates of the selected vertex. (When multiple vertices are selected, the label
   says "Median," even though technically speaking the panel does *not* show the
   `geometric median <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometric_median>`__
   but the `geometric center <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centroid>`__.)
Space
   Whether to show the coordinates in Local Space or Global Space.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/basic.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Move, Rotate, Scale > Vertex Data
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Move, Rotate, Scale Vertex Data
text:
Bevel Weight
   Typically used with the bevel (with *Affect* set to
   *Vertices*). By default, this modifier applies the same bevel amount to all vertices,
   but if its *Limit Method* is set to *Weight*, the Bevel Weight of each vertex serves as
   a multiplier. This makes it possible to apply a smaller bevel, or no bevel at all,
   to specific vertices.

   Internally, the Bevel Weight is stored as an
   attribute
   called bevel_weight_vert. This means it can also be read by the
   named attribute in
   geometry nodes.

Crease
   A higher Crease value makes the corner at the vertex appear sharper when using the
   subdivision surface.

   Internally, the Crease value is stored as an attribute called crease_vert.

Radius X/Y
   The radii for the skin.
   Only shown if the mesh has this modifier.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/basic.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Move, Rotate, Scale > Edge Data
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Move, Rotate, Scale Edge Data
text:
When an edge is selected, the following options are available:

Bevel Weight
   Typically used with the bevel (with *Affect* set to
   *Edges*). See the vertex *Bevel Weight* above.

   Internally, this property is stored as an attribute called bevel_weight_edge.
   It can also be set using the bpy.ops.transform.edge_bevelweight operator.

.. todo move to attribute page

Crease
   A higher Crease value makes the corner at the edge appear sharper when using the
   subdivision surface.

   Internally, this property is stored as an attribute called crease_edge.
   It can also be set using the bpy.ops.transform.edge_crease operator.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/basic.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bend
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Bend Bend
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-W

This transformation bends part of the selection into a circle segment. It's similar to
warp, except that here, the 3D Cursor
is on the circle instead of at the center.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/bend.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bend > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Bend Usage
text:
#. Align the 3D Viewport's viewpoint to the plane
   in which the bend should happen.
#. Place the 3d cursor at the base of the bend. The geometry around
   this point will stay in place.
#. Place the mouse cursor so that the line between it and the 3D Cursor lies along the
   geometry to bend.
#. Press Shift-W to activate the tool and move the mouse to bend the geometry.

   - The distance between the mouse cursor and the 3D Cursor determines the bend radius
     and how much of the selected geometry is bent (instead of just rotated).
     Hold Alt to disable clamping and bend all selected geometry instead.
   - The angle between the original line and the new line determines the bend angle.

#. Press LMB or Return to confirm, or RMB or Esc to cancel.

Note:

   Unlike most other transform tools, *Bend* does not take into account the
   transform orientation or the
   pivot point, instead always
   using the view plane and the 3D Cursor.

Hint:

   Moving the mouse cursor around the 3D Cursor multiple times will correspondingly
   bend the geometry over multiple circle revolutions.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/bend.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Bend > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Bend Options
text:
Unlike other operators, the Bend operator doesn't support the
bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/bend.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Curve Edge Loops Between Selected
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Curve Edge Loops Between Selected Curve Edge Loops Between Selected
text:
The *Curve Edge Loops Between Selected* operator reshapes unselected vertices along edge loops
to follow a curve defined by selected vertices. The selected vertices remain fixed as control points.
The operator moves existing vertices without adding or removing geometry.

Control vertices can be selected at intervals along an edge loop or wire chain.
Selecting entire edge loops uses those vertices as control points for the loops running across them.
This allows the shape between selected loops to be adjusted while keeping the selected loops unchanged.

With *Extend Loop* disabled, only vertices between the outermost selected control vertices are affected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/curve_edge_loops_between_selected.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Curve Edge Loops Between Selected > Operator Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Curve Edge Loops Between Selected Operator Options
text:
Factor
   Strength of the adjustment. A value of zero leaves the mesh unchanged;
   a value of one moves affected vertices fully to the calculated curve.

Clamp Elevation
   Restricts movement relative to each vertex's normal.
   This restriction does not apply to wire vertices, which have no face normal.

   :None: Allows movement in either direction.
   :Only Raise:
      Prevents adjustments that move a vertex against its normal, allowing outward adjustments.
   :Only Lower:
      Prevents adjustments that move a vertex along its normal, allowing inward adjustments.

Extend Loop
   Includes vertices beyond the outermost selected control vertices.
   For open chains, the chain endpoints are also kept fixed and used as control points.
   For closed loops with a large unselected gap, the affected region is limited around the selection
   to prevent the loop from collapsing.

Space Evenly
   Calculates the curve using evenly spaced vertex parameters rather than the existing distances along the loop.
   Selected control vertices remain fixed.

Lock
   Prevents changes along the enabled X, Y, or Z axes in the object's local space.

Interpolation
   Determines the shape of the curve between control vertices.

   :Cubic: Uses a cubic spline to create a smooth curve through the control vertices.
   :Linear: Uses straight segments between control vertices.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/curve_edge_loops_between_selected.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Fit Edge Loops To Annotation
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Fit Edge Loops To Annotation Fit Edge Loops To Annotation
text:
The *Fit Edge Loops To Annotation* operator reshapes selected edge loops to follow
annotation strokes.
It moves existing vertices without adding or removing geometry.

Guide strokes can be drawn in the 3D Viewport using the *Annotate* tool with *Placement*
set to *3D Cursor* or *Surface*. The operator then fits the edges selected in Edit Mode to these strokes.
Only 3D strokes with at least two points from the active annotation layer's active frame are used.
Strokes drawn with *View* placement are ignored.

When several edge loops and strokes are present, strokes that have not yet been assigned
to a loop are preferred. Among equally used strokes, the stroke whose center is closest
to the loop's center is chosen. A stroke can be reused when there are more loops than strokes.

If no usable annotation strokes are available, a straight line between the first and last
vertices of each edge chain is used instead.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/fit_edge_loops_to_annotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Fit Edge Loops To Annotation > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Fit Edge Loops To Annotation Options
text:
Factor
   Controls how far the vertices move toward their target positions.
   A value of zero leaves the vertices unchanged; a value of one applies the full adjustment.

Method
   Determines how vertices are fitted to the stroke.

   :Spread:
      Distributes vertices along the entire stroke while preserving their relative spacing along the edge loop.
   :Spread Evenly:
      Distributes vertices at equal distances along the entire stroke.
   :Project:
      Projects vertices onto the stroke along connected unselected edges that share faces with the selected edges.
      If no suitable projection is found, the vertex normal is used instead.
      The stroke must lie close to these projection lines; vertices without a suitable projection remain unchanged.

Delete Strokes
   Removes the usable 3D annotation strokes from the active layer's active frame after applying the operator.

Lock
   Prevents changes to vertex coordinates along the enabled X, Y, or Z axes in the object's local space.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/fit_edge_loops_to_annotation.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Flatten
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Flatten Flatten
text:
Flatten selected vertices onto a plane.

The operator calculates a target plane and moves vertices toward it while
preserving their relative positions along the unlocked axes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/flatten.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Flatten > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Flatten Options
text:
Factor
   Strength of the flatten operation.

   A value of 1 fully flattens the selection onto the target plane,
   while lower values partially move vertices toward the plane.

Method
   Method used to determine the flattening plane.

   :Best Fit: Calculates a plane that best fits the selected vertices.
   :Normal: Derives the plane from the averaged normals of the selected faces.
   :View: Uses a plane perpendicular to the current view direction.

Lock
   Prevents movement along selected axes while flattening.

   This can be used to constrain the flatten operation to specific directions.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/flatten.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Push/Pull
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Push/Pull Push/Pull
text:
Moves the selected elements further away from or closer to the
Pivot Point,
all by the same distance.

When using the tool, simply drag the yellow pin.

When using the menu item, move the mouse down to Push or up to Pull
(Alternatively, type a number for the *Distance* option.)
Then press LMB or Return to confirm,
or RMB or Esc to cancel.

After confirming, the distance can still be changed in the
bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/push_pull.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Push/Pull > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Push/Pull Options
text:
Distance
   How far to push (negative) or pull (positive) the selected items.
Mirror Editing
   Whether to also affect matching geometry on the other side of the mesh.
   Mesh Symmetry
   needs to be enabled for this to work.
Proportional Editing
   See Proportional Editing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/push_pull.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Randomize > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Randomize Options
text:
Amount
   Maximum displacement distance for each vertex.
Uniform
   How uniform the displacement distance should be. When 0, each vertex moves by a
   random distance between 0 and *Amount*. When 1, all vertices move by a distance
   of exactly *Amount*. The displacement direction stays random, however.
Normal
   How close the displacement direction should be to each vertex normal.
   When 0, the direction is completely random. When 1, the direction is always
   equal to the normal or its opposite.
Random Seed
   Different seeds will produce different random displacements.

Seealso:

   randomize in Object Mode
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/randomize.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Relax Edge Loops
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Relax Edge Loops Relax Edge Loops
text:
The *Relax Edge Loops* operator smooths selected edge loops by adjusting the positions
of their vertices while preserving the overall shape of the mesh.

Only separate edge loops containing two or more edges can be relaxed.
Faces must not be selected.

Note:

   The operator requires at least one separate edge loop containing two or more selected edges.
   It cannot be used when faces are selected.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/relax_edge_loops.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Relax Edge Loops > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Relax Edge Loops Options
text:
Iterations
   Number of times the relaxation is applied.
   Higher values produce a smoother distribution of vertices.

Space Evenly
   Distribute vertices at constant distances along the loop.

Interpolation
   Algorithm used to compute the new vertex positions.

   :Cubic:
      Uses a natural cubic spline to produce a smooth distribution that better
      preserves the curvature of the loop.
   :Linear:
      Interpolates directly along the existing edges.
      This is faster and preserves straight edge segments.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/relax_edge_loops.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shear
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Shear Shear
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-Ctrl-Alt-S

Shearing deforms the selected geometry by moving the vertices above the
Pivot Point to the left and the vertices below
that point to the right (or vice versa). The higher or lower a vertex is compared to the pivot point,
the further it will be moved. The result is that vertical edges become diagonal while horizontal edges
stay the same.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/shear.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shear > Tool
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Shear Tool
text:
Set up a pivot point and optionally a transform orientation.
Pick an axis on the gizmo that matches the desired "above"/"below" direction (which determines
how much each vertex should be sheared). Finally, drag the handle that matches the desired
"horizontal" direction (in which the vertices should be moved).
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/shear.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shear > Operator
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Shear Operator
text:
Set up a pivot point, then either click the menu item or press the keyboard shortcut.
Move the mouse left or right to shear, then click LMB to confirm.

By default, the meanings of "above," "below," and "horizontal" are all in the current
viewing plane in the 3D Viewport, but this can be changed in the options.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/shear.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shear > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Shear Options
text:
Angle
   How much to "rotate" the vertical edges.
Axis
   The axis that's perpendicular to the shearing plane. For example, if the vertices
   should move along the X axis and their distance from the pivot point should be
   measured along the Y axis, the *Axis* should be set to Z.
Axis Ortho
   The axis along which the vertices should move. This must be different from *Axis*.
Orientation
   The Transform Orientation from which
   to pick the *Axis* and *Axis Ortho*.
Mirror Editing
   Whether to also affect matching geometry on the other side of the mesh.
   Mesh Symmetry
   needs to be enabled for this to work.
Proportional Editing
   See Proportional Editing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/shear.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shrink/Fatten
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Shrink/Fatten Shrink/Fatten
text:
Shortcut:  Alt-S

Moves the selected vertices "inwards" or "outwards" along their normal,
all by the same distance.

After clicking the menu item or pressing the keyboard shortcut, move the mouse down to
shrink or up to fatten. (Alternatively, type a distance on the keyboard.) Then
press LMB or Return to confirm or RMB or Esc to cancel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/shrink-fatten.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Shrink/Fatten > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Shrink/Fatten Options
text:
These settings can be changed in the bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel.

Offset
   How far to move each vertex.

Offset Even
   When disabled, each vertex is offset by the same distance.
   When enabled, each *edge* is offset by the same distance.

   This option can also be toggled before confirming by pressing S or holding Alt.
   (These shortcuts are shown in the status bar.)

Mirror Editing
   Whether to also affect matching geometry on the other side of the mesh.
   Mesh Symmetry
   needs to be enabled for this to work.

Proportional Editing
   See Proportional Editing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/shrink-fatten.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Skin Resize
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Skin Resize Skin Resize
text:
Shortcut:  Ctrl-A

Changes the X and Y skinning radii of the selected vertices for use with the
skin. (For meshes that don't have this modifier,
activating this operator does nothing.)

To change only one of the radii, press X or Y while the operator is active,
or change a *Scale X/Y* property in the bpy.ops.screen.redo_last panel.

The radii can also be adjusted in the modeling-mesh-transform-panel in the Sidebar.

Note:

   If the modifier is deleted, the skinning radii will be lost.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/skin_resize.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Space Edge Loops Evenly
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Space Edge Loops Evenly Space Edge Loops Evenly
text:
Redistribute the vertices of the selected edge loops so they are spaced more
evenly along the loop while preserving its overall shape.

This is useful for improving the distribution of vertices after modeling
operations such as extrusion, subdivision, or manual editing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/space_edge_loops_evenly.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Space Edge Loops Evenly > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Space Edge Loops Evenly Options
text:
Factor
   Strength of the operation.

   A value of 0 leaves the mesh unchanged, while 1 fully redistributes the vertices.

Interpolation
   Algorithm used to compute the new vertex positions.

   :Cubic:
      Uses a natural cubic spline to produce a smooth distribution that better
      preserves the curvature of the loop.
   :Linear:
      Interpolates directly along the existing edges.
      This is faster and preserves straight edge segments.

Lock
   Restrict movement to the selected axes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/space_edge_loops_evenly.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: To Circle
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform To Circle To Circle
text:
Transforms selected vertices into a circular shape.

The operator works best on edge loops but can also be used on arbitrary vertex selections,
including open loops or multiple disconnected selections.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/to_circle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: To Circle > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform To Circle Options
text:
Factor
   Controls the strength of the transformation.

   A value of 0 leaves the geometry unchanged,
   while 1 fully transforms the selection into a circle.

Method
   Determines how the circle is calculated.

   :Best Fit:
      Computes a circle that best fits the selected vertices using a least-squares method.

      This preserves the overall shape of the selection while making it circular.
   :Interior Fit:
      Computes a circle that fits inside the existing selection.

      Vertices are not moved farther away from the center,
      which helps preserve surrounding topology.

Rotation
   Rotates (twists) the resulting circle around its center.

Radius
   Overrides the automatically calculated radius.

   Useful for creating circles of consistent size or for precise control.

Space Evenly
   Distributes vertices evenly along the circle.

   When disabled, vertex spacing follows the original distribution.

Flatten
   Controls how much the selection is flattened to a best-fit plane before circularizing.

   A value of 0 keeps the original shape,
   while a value of 1 fully flattens the selection.

   Intermediate values blend between the original shape and the flattened result.

Lock
   Restricts transformations along selected axes.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/to_circle.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: To Sphere
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform To Sphere To Sphere
text:
Shortcut:  Shift-Alt-S

The *To Sphere* transformation deforms the selected geometry to look more like a sphere.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/to_sphere.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: To Sphere > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform To Sphere Usage
text:
Click the menu item or press the keyboard shortcut, then move the mouse right or left
(or type a number between 0 and 1) to make the selection more or less spherical.
Finally, press LMB or Return to confirm, or RMB or Esc to cancel.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/to_sphere.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: To Sphere > Options
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform To Sphere Options
text:
Factor
   A value between 0 and 1 indicating how strongly the selection is spherized.

Mirror Editing
   Whether to also affect matching geometry on the other side of the mesh.
   Mesh Symmetry
   needs to be enabled for this to work.

Proportional Editing
   See proportional editing.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/to_sphere.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: To Sphere > Examples
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform To Sphere Examples
text:
Meshes with higher density will give better results:

The results are also different depending on the number and arrangement of the selected elements:
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/to_sphere.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Warp
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Warp Warp
text:
This transformation bends part of the selection into a circle segment.
It's similar to bend,
except that here, the 3D Cursor is at the center instead of on the circle.
source: Blender Manual, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/meshes/editing/mesh/transform/warp.html, by the Blender Documentation Team, CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Warp > Usage
keywords: Modeling > Meshes > Editing > Mesh > Transform Warp Usage
text:
#. Align the 3D Viewport's viewpoint to the plane
   in which the warp should happen.
